"""
schema_evolution.py - Managing Message Schema Changes Over Time
"""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Type, Union
from enum import Enum
import json
import hashlib


# =============================================================================
# Schema Evolution Strategies
# =============================================================================

"""
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     SCHEMA EVOLUTION STRATEGIES                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│  1. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE (New reader, old data)                              │
│     ┌──────────────┐    reads    ┌──────────────┐                           │
│     │ Consumer v2  │ ◀────────── │  Message v1  │                           │
│     └──────────────┘             └──────────────┘                           │
│     • Add optional fields with defaults                                     │
│     • Safe: old messages still work                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  2. FORWARD COMPATIBLE (Old reader, new data)                               │
│     ┌──────────────┐    reads    ┌──────────────┐                           │
│     │ Consumer v1  │ ◀────────── │  Message v2  │                           │
│     └──────────────┘             └──────────────┘                           │
│     • Remove optional fields                                                │
│     • Old consumers ignore unknown fields                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  3. FULL COMPATIBLE (Both directions)                                       │
│     Most restrictive but safest for rolling deployments                     │
│                                                                              │
│  4. BREAKING CHANGE (New topic required)                                    │
│     • Rename fields                                                         │
│     • Change field types                                                    │
│     • Remove required fields                                                │
│     → Requires migration strategy                                           │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
"""


class Compatibility(Enum):
    BACKWARD = "backward"      # New code reads old data
    FORWARD = "forward"        # Old code reads new data
    FULL = "full"              # Both directions
    NONE = "none"              # Breaking change


# =============================================================================
# Schema Definition
# =============================================================================

@dataclass
class FieldSchema:
    """Definition of a single field"""
    name: str
    field_type: str  # string, int, float, bool, object, array
    required: bool = True
    default: Any = None
    description: str = ""
    nested_schema: Optional["MessageSchema"] = None  # For object types
    deprecated: bool = False
    added_in_version: int = 1
    removed_in_version: Optional[int] = None
    
    def is_active(self, version: int) -> bool:
        """Check if field exists in given schema version"""
        if self.added_in_version > version:
            return False
        if self.removed_in_version and self.removed_in_version <= version:
            return False
        return True


@dataclass  
class MessageSchema:
    """Schema definition for a message type"""
    name: str
    version: int
    fields: List[FieldSchema]
    description: str = ""
    
    def get_field(self, name: str) -> Optional[FieldSchema]:
        return next((f for f in self.fields if f.name == name), None)
    
    def get_active_fields(self, version: Optional[int] = None) -> List[FieldSchema]:
        """Get fields active in given version"""
        v = version or self.version
        return [f for f in self.fields if f.is_active(v)]
    
    def get_required_fields(self, version: Optional[int] = None) -> List[FieldSchema]:
        """Get required fields active in given version"""
        return [f for f in self.get_active_fields(version) if f.required]
    
    def fingerprint(self) -> str:
        """Generate schema fingerprint for caching"""
        content = json.dumps({
            "name": self.name,
            "version": self.version,
            "fields": [(f.name, f.field_type, f.required) for f in self.fields]
        }, sort_keys=True)
        return hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


# =============================================================================
# Schema Registry
# =============================================================================

class SchemaRegistry:
    """
    Central registry for message schemas
    Similar to Confluent Schema Registry for Avro
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self._schemas: Dict[str, Dict[int, MessageSchema]] = {}
        self._compatibility: Dict[str, Compatibility] = {}
        
    def register(
        self, 
        schema: MessageSchema,
        compatibility: Compatibility = Compatibility.BACKWARD
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Register a new schema version
        Validates compatibility with previous version
        """
        if schema.name not in self._schemas:
            self._schemas[schema.name] = {}
            self._compatibility[schema.name] = compatibility
        
        # Check compatibility if not first version
        existing = self._schemas[schema.name]
        if existing:
            latest_version = max(existing.keys())
            latest_schema = existing[latest_version]
            
            if not self._check_compatibility(
                latest_schema, 
                schema, 
                self._compatibility[schema.name]
            ):
                raise IncompatibleSchemaError(
                    f"Schema {schema.name} v{schema.version} is not "
                    f"{self._compatibility[schema.name].value} compatible"
                )
        
        self._schemas[schema.name][schema.version] = schema
        return True
    
    def get(self, name: str, version: Optional[int] = None) -> Optional[MessageSchema]:
        """Get schema by name and optional version"""
        if name not in self._schemas:
            return None
        
        versions = self._schemas[name]
        if version:
            return versions.get(version)
        
        # Return latest version
        return versions[max(versions.keys())]
    
    def get_all_versions(self, name: str) -> List[int]:
        """Get all registered versions for a schema"""
        if name not in self._schemas:
            return []
        return sorted(self._schemas[name].keys())
    
    def _check_compatibility(
        self,
        old: MessageSchema,
        new: MessageSchema,
        mode: Compatibility
    ) -> bool:
        """Check if new schema is compatible with old"""
        
        if mode == Compatibility.NONE:
            return True
        
        if mode in (Compatibility.BACKWARD, Compatibility.FULL):
            # New reader must understand old data
            # Cannot add new required fields (old data won't have them)
            for field in new.get_active_fields():
                old_field = old.get_field(field.name)
                if field.required and not old_field:
                    # New required field - not backward compatible
                    return False
        
        if mode in (Compatibility.FORWARD, Compatibility.FULL):
            # Old reader must understand new data
            # Cannot remove required fields (old reader expects them)
            for field in old.get_active_fields():
                new_field = new.get_field(field.name)
                if field.required and not new_field:
                    # Removed required field - not forward compatible
                    return False
                if new_field and field.field_type != new_field.field_type:
                    # Type change - not compatible
                    return False
        
        return True


class IncompatibleSchemaError(Exception):
    """Raised when schema change breaks compatibility"""
    pass


# =============================================================================
# Schema-Aware Serialization
# =============================================================================

class SchemaAwareSerializer:
    """
    Serializer that embeds schema information in messages
    """
    
    def __init__(self, registry: SchemaRegistry):
        self.registry = registry
        
    def serialize(
        self, 
        data: Dict[str, Any], 
        schema_name: str,
        schema_version: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> bytes:
        """
        Serialize data with schema metadata
        """
        schema = self.registry.get(schema_name, schema_version)
        if not schema:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown schema: {schema_name}")
        
        # Validate data against schema
        self._validate(data, schema)
        
        # Create envelope with schema info
        envelope = {
            "_schema": {
                "name": schema_name,
                "version": schema.version,
                "fingerprint": schema.fingerprint()
            },
            "_data": data
        }
        
        return json.dumps(envelope).encode()
    
    def deserialize(
        self, 
        data: bytes,
        target_version: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], MessageSchema]:
        """
        Deserialize data and optionally transform to target version
        """
        envelope = json.loads(data.decode())
        
        schema_info = envelope["_schema"]
        schema_name = schema_info["name"]
        data_version = schema_info["version"]
        
        # Get schema for data version
        schema = self.registry.get(schema_name, data_version)
        payload = envelope["_data"]
        
        # Transform to target version if needed
        if target_version and target_version != data_version:
            target_schema = self.registry.get(schema_name, target_version)
            payload = self._transform(payload, schema, target_schema)
            schema = target_schema
        
        return payload, schema
    
    def _validate(self, data: Dict[str, Any], schema: MessageSchema):
        """Validate data against schema"""
        for field in schema.get_required_fields():
            if field.name not in data:
                raise ValueError(f"Missing required field: {field.name}")
        
        for key, value in data.items():
            field = schema.get_field(key)
            if field and not self._check_type(value, field.field_type):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid type for {key}: expected {field.field_type}")
    
    def _check_type(self, value: Any, expected_type: str) -> bool:
        """Check if value matches expected type"""
        type_map = {
            "string": str,
            "int": int,
            "float": (int, float),
            "bool": bool,
            "object": dict,
            "array": list,
        }
        expected = type_map.get(expected_type)
        if expected:
            return isinstance(value, expected)
        return True  # Unknown types pass
    
    def _transform(
        self,
        data: Dict[str, Any],
        from_schema: MessageSchema,
        to_schema: MessageSchema
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Transform data from one schema version to another"""
        result = {}
        
        for field in to_schema.get_active_fields():
            if field.name in data:
                result[field.name] = data[field.name]
            elif field.default is not None:
                result[field.name] = field.default
            elif not field.required:
                continue
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Cannot transform: missing required field {field.name}")
        
        return result


# =============================================================================
# Message Versioning Patterns
# =============================================================================

class MessageVersioningPattern:
    """
    Common patterns for handling message versions
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def envelope_pattern(payload: Dict, schema_name: str, version: int) -> Dict:
        """
        Wrap payload in versioned envelope
        """
        return {
            "schema": schema_name,
            "version": version,
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "data": payload
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def header_pattern(payload: Dict, version: int) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict]:
        """
        Add version to message headers (Kafka-style)
        """
        headers = {
            "content-type": "application/json",
            "schema-version": str(version)
        }
        return payload, headers
    
    @staticmethod
    def duck_typing_pattern(payload: Dict) -> int:
        """
        Infer version from payload structure
        """
        # Example: v2 added 'email' field
        if "email" in payload:
            return 2
        return 1

# Multi-Version Consumer

class MultiVersionConsumer:
    """
    Consumer that handles multiple schema versions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, registry: SchemaRegistry):
        self.registry = registry
        self.serializer = SchemaAwareSerializer(registry)
        self._handlers: Dict[Tuple[str, int], Callable] = {}
        self._transformers: Dict[Tuple[str, int, int], Callable] = {}
        
    def register_handler(
        self,
        schema_name: str,
        version: int,
        handler: Callable[[Dict], Any]
    ):
        """Register handler for specific schema version"""
        self._handlers[(schema_name, version)] = handler
    
    def register_transformer(
        self,
        schema_name: str,
        from_version: int,
        to_version: int,
        transformer: Callable[[Dict], Dict]
    ):
        """Register custom transformer between versions"""
        self._transformers[(schema_name, from_version, to_version)] = transformer
    
    async def process(self, raw_message: bytes) -> Any:
        """Process message, handling any schema version"""
        
        data, schema = self.serializer.deserialize(raw_message)
        
        # Try to find handler for this version
        handler_key = (schema.name, schema.version)
        if handler_key in self._handlers:
            return await self._handlers[handler_key](data)
        
        # Try to transform to a version we can handle
        for (name, version), handler in self._handlers.items():
            if name != schema.name:
                continue
            
            # Try to transform
            transform_key = (schema.name, schema.version, version)
            if transform_key in self._transformers:
                transformed = self._transformers[transform_key](data)
                return await handler(transformed)
        
        raise ValueError(f"No handler for {schema.name} v{schema.version}")

"""

"""

│                                                                              │

│  │  retry_count_total            Number of retry attempts              │    │
│  │  dlq_messages_total           Messages sent to DLQ                  │    │
│  │  error_rate                   Failures / total processed            │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
"""


class MetricType(Enum):
    COUNTER = "counter"        # Monotonically increasing
    GAUGE = "gauge"            # Current value
    HISTOGRAM = "histogram"    # Distribution
    SUMMARY = "summary"        # Percentiles


@dataclass
class Metric:
    """Single metric data point"""
    name: str
    value: float
    metric_type: MetricType
    labels: Dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    timestamp: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)


class MetricsCollector:
    """
    Collects and aggregates metrics
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self._counters: Dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
        self._gauges: Dict[str, float] = {}
        self._histograms: Dict[str, List[float]] = defaultdict(list)
        self._labels: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]] = {}
        
    def _make_key(self, name: str, labels: Dict[str, str] = None) -> str:
        """Create key from name and labels"""
        if not labels:
            return name
        label_str = ",".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(labels.items()))
        return f"{name}{{{label_str}}}"
    
    def inc_counter(self, name: str, value: float = 1, labels: Dict[str, str] = None):
        """Increment a counter"""
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        self._counters[key] += value
        self._labels[key] = labels or {}
    
    def set_gauge(self, name: str, value: float, labels: Dict[str, str] = None):
        """Set a gauge value"""
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        self._gauges[key] = value
        self._labels[key] = labels or {}
    
    def observe_histogram(self, name: str, value: float, labels: Dict[str, str] = None):
        """Add observation to histogram"""
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        self._histograms[key].append(value)
        self._labels[key] = labels or {}
        
        # Keep only recent observations (sliding window)
        max_observations = 10000
        if len(self._histograms[key]) > max_observations:
            self._histograms[key] = self._histograms[key][-max_observations:]
    
    def get_counter(self, name: str, labels: Dict[str, str] = None) -> float:
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        return self._counters.get(key, 0)
    
    def get_gauge(self, name: str, labels: Dict[str, str] = None) -> float:
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        return self._gauges.get(key, 0)
    
    def get_histogram_stats(self, name: str, labels: Dict[str, str] = None) -> Dict[str, float]:
        key = self._make_key(name, labels)
        values = self._histograms.get(key, [])
        
        if not values:
            return {"count": 0}
        
        sorted_values = sorted(values)
        return {
            "count": len(values),
            "min": min(values),
            "max": max(values),
            "mean": statistics.mean(values),
            "median": statistics.median(values),
            "p95": sorted_values[int(len(sorted_values) * 0.95)] if len(sorted_values) >= 20 else max(values),
            "p99": sorted_values[int(len(sorted_values) * 0.99)] if len(sorted_values) >= 100 else max(values),
        }
    
    def get_all_metrics(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:

class InstrumentedProcessor:
    """
    Message processor with built-in metrics collection
    """
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, metrics: MetricsCollector):
        self.name = name
        self.metrics = metrics
        
    async def process(
        self,
        message: Dict[str, Any],
        handler: Callable
    ) -> Tuple[bool, float]:
        """
        Process message and record metrics
        Returns: (success, processing_time_ms)
        """
        labels = {"processor": self.name}
        
        # Record message received
        self.metrics.inc_counter("messages_received_total", labels=labels)
        
        # Calculate queue wait time (if timestamp in message)
        if "timestamp" in message:
            msg_time = datetime.fromisoformat(message["timestamp"])
            wait_time_ms = (datetime.utcnow() - msg_time).total_seconds() * 1000
            self.metrics.observe_histogram("queue_wait_time_ms", wait_time_ms, labels=labels)
        
        # Process and measure
        start_time = time.perf_counter()
        
        try:
            if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(handler):
                await handler(message)
            else:
                handler(message)
            
            processing_time_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000
            
            # Record success
            self.metrics.inc_counter("messages_processed_total", labels=labels)
            self.metrics.observe_histogram("processing_time_ms", processing_time_ms, labels=labels)
            
            return True, processing_time_ms
            
        except Exception as e:
            processing_time_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_time) * 1000
            
            # Record failure
            error_labels = {**labels, "error_type": type(e).__name__}
            self.metrics.inc_counter("messages_failed_total", labels=error_labels)
            self.metrics.observe_histogram("failed_processing_time_ms", processing_time_ms, labels=labels)
            
            raise

@dataclass
class PartitionOffset:
    """Tracks offset for a topic partition"""
    topic: str
    partition: int
    latest_offset: int
    committed_offset: int
    
    @property
    def lag(self) -> int:
        return self.latest_offset - self.committed_offset


class ConsumerLagMonitor:
    """
    Monitors consumer lag across topics and partitions
    """
    
    def __init__(self, metrics: MetricsCollector):
        self.metrics = metrics
        self._offsets: Dict[Tuple[str, str, int], PartitionOffset] = {}
        
    def update_offset(
        self,
        consumer_group: str,
        topic: str,
        partition: int,
        latest_offset: int,
        committed_offset: int
    ):
        """Update offset information"""
        key = (consumer_group, topic, partition)
        
        self._offsets[key] = PartitionOffset(
            topic=topic,
            partition=partition,
            latest_offset=latest_offset,
            committed_offset=committed_offset
        )
        
        # Update metrics
        labels = {
            "consumer_group": consumer_group,
            "topic": topic,
            "partition": str(partition)
        }
        
        self.metrics.set_gauge("consumer_lag", latest_offset - committed_offset, labels)
        self.metrics.set_gauge("latest_offset", latest_offset, labels)
        self.metrics.set_gauge("committed_offset", committed_offset, labels)
    
    def get_total_lag(self, consumer_group: str) -> int:
        """Get total lag across all partitions for consumer group"""
        return sum(
            offset.lag
            for (group, _, _), offset in self._offsets.items()
            if group == consumer_group
        )
    
    def get_lag_by_topic(self, consumer_group: str) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Get lag per topic for consumer group"""
        lag_by_topic = defaultdict(int)
        for (group, topic, _), offset in self._offsets.items():
            if group == consumer_group:
                lag_by_topic[topic] += offset.lag
        return dict(lag_by_topic)

class HealthStatus(Enum):
    HEALTHY = "healthy"
    DEGRADED = "degraded"
    UNHEALTHY = "unhealthy"


@dataclass
class HealthCheckResult:
    """Result of a health check"""
    name: str
    status: HealthStatus
    message: str = ""
    details: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


class HealthChecker:
    """
    Health checks for message queue system
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        metrics: MetricsCollector,
        lag_monitor: ConsumerLagMonitor
    ):
        self.metrics = metrics
        self.lag_monitor = lag_monitor
        self._checks: List[Callable[[], HealthCheckResult]] = []
        
        # Register default checks
        self._register_default_checks()
    
    def _register_default_checks(self):
        """Register standard health checks"""
        self._checks.extend([
            self._check_processing_rate,
            self._check_error_rate,
            self._check_consumer_lag,
            self._check_dlq_size,
        ])
    
    def _check_processing_rate(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        """Check if messages are being processed"""
        processed = self.metrics.get_counter("messages_processed_total")
        received = self.metrics.get_counter("messages_received_total")
        
        if received == 0:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                name="processing_rate",
                status=HealthStatus.HEALTHY,
                message="No messages received yet"
            )
        
        rate = processed / received if received > 0 else 0
        
        if rate >= 0.95:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                name="processing_rate",
                status=HealthStatus.HEALTHY,
                message=f"Processing rate: {rate:.2%}",
                details={"rate": rate, "processed": processed, "received": received}
            )
        elif rate >= 0.8:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                name="processing_rate",
                status=HealthStatus.DEGRADED,
                message=f"Processing rate degraded: {rate:.2%}",
                details={"rate": rate}
            )
        else:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                name="processing_rate",
                status=HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY,
                message=f"Processing rate critical: {rate:.2%}",
                details={"rate": rate}
            )
    
    def _check_error_rate(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        """Check error rate"""
        failed = self.metrics.get_counter("messages_failed_total")
        processed = self.metrics.get_counter("messages_processed_total")
        total = failed + processed
        
        if total == 0:
            return HealthCheckResult(
                name="error_rate",
                status=HealthStatus.HEALTHY,
                message="No messages processed yet"
            )
        
        error_rate = failed / total
        
        if error_rate <= 0.01:
            status = HealthStatus.HEALTHY
            message = f"Error rate normal: {error_rate:.2%}"
        elif error_rate <= 0.05:
            status = HealthStatus.DEGRADED
            message = f"Error rate elevated: {error_rate:.2%}"
        else:
            status = HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY
            message = f"Error rate critical: {error_rate:.2%}"
        
        return HealthCheckResult(
            name="error_rate",
            status=status,
            message=message,
            details={"error_rate": error_rate, "failed": failed, "processed": processed}
        )
    
    def _check_consumer_lag(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        """Check consumer lag"""
        # This is a simplified check - in practice, check all consumer groups
        total_lag = sum(
            offset.lag for offset in self.lag_monitor._offsets.values()
        )
        
        if total_lag <= 100:
            status = HealthStatus.HEALTHY
            message = f"Consumer lag normal: {total_lag}"
        elif total_lag <= 1000:
            status = HealthStatus.DEGRADED
            message = f"Consumer lag elevated: {total_lag}"
        else:
            status = HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY
            message = f"Consumer lag critical: {total_lag}"
        
        return HealthCheckResult(
            name="consumer_lag",
            status=status,
            message=message,
            details={"total_lag": total_lag}
        )
    
    def _check_dlq_size(self) -> HealthCheckResult:
        """Check DLQ size"""
        dlq_size = self.metrics.get_gauge("dlq_size")
        
        if dlq_size <= 10:
            status = HealthStatus.HEALTHY
            message = f"DLQ size normal: {int(dlq_size)}"
        elif dlq_size <= 100:
            status = HealthStatus.DEGRADED
            message = f"DLQ size elevated: {int(dlq_size)}"
        else:
            status = HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY
            message = f"DLQ size critical: {int(dlq_size)}"
        
        return HealthCheckResult(
            name="dlq_size",
            status=status,
            message=message,
            details={"dlq_size": dlq_size}
        )
    
    def run_all_checks(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Run all health checks"""
        results = [check() for check in self._checks]
        
        overall_status = HealthStatus.HEALTHY
        for result in results:
            if result.status == HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY:
                overall_status = HealthStatus.UNHEALTHY
                break
            elif result.status == HealthStatus.DEGRADED:
                overall_status = HealthStatus.DEGRADED
        
        return {
            "status": overall_status.value,
            "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "checks": [
                {
                    "name": r.name,
                    "status": r.status.value,
                    "message": r.message,
                    "details": r.details
                }
                for r in results
            ]
        }

        self._alert_handlers: List[Callable[[str, str, str], None]] = []

        """Check all alert conditions"""
        now = datetime.utcnow()
        
        for alert in self._alerts:
            # Check cooldown

                self._last_fired[alert.name] = now
                
                # Fire alert to all handlers

## 5. Inhaler Technique

### Metered-Dose Inhaler (MDI)

```
WITHOUT SPACER:
1. Remove cap, shake well (5 seconds)
2. Exhale fully away from inhaler
3. Head slightly tilted back
4. Seal lips around mouthpiece
5. Start SLOW inhalation
6. Press canister ONCE at start of breath
7. Continue slow, deep breath (3-5 seconds)
8. Hold breath 10 seconds (or as long as comfortable)
9. Wait 30-60 seconds before second puff
10. Rinse mouth after ICS
```

### MDI with Spacer (Preferred)

```
1. Assemble spacer, remove MDI cap
2. Shake MDI vigorously
3. Insert MDI into spacer
4. Exhale fully
5. Seal lips around spacer mouthpiece
6. Press canister ONCE
7. Breathe in slowly and deeply OR 4-6 tidal breaths
8. Hold breath 10 seconds
9. One puff at a time (shake between puffs)
10. Rinse mouth after ICS
```

### Dry Powder Inhaler (DPI)

```
CRITICAL: DO NOT exhale into device!

1. Load dose per device instructions
2. Exhale fully AWAY from device
3. Seal lips tightly around mouthpiece
4. Inhale FAST and DEEP (like sipping hot soup)
5. Hold breath 10 seconds
6. Rinse mouth after ICS

Note: Requires adequate inspiratory flow (~30-60 L/min)
```

### Device-Specific Loading

| Device | Loading Method |
|--------|---------------|
| **Turbuhaler** | Twist base back and forth (click) |
| **Diskus** | Slide lever until click |
| **Ellipta** | Open cover fully until click |
| **HandiHaler** | Pierce capsule, press buttons |
| **Breezhaler** | Pierce capsule, hear rattle |

### Soft Mist Inhaler (Respimat)

```
1. Hold upright, turn clear base until click
2. Open cap
3. Exhale fully away from device
4. Seal lips around mouthpiece
5. Press dose-release button while inhaling SLOWLY
6. Hold breath 10 seconds
7. Close cap
```

### Common Technique Errors

| Error | Impact | Correction |
|-------|--------|------------|
| Not shaking MDI | Inconsistent dose delivery | Shake 5+ seconds before each use |
| Poor coordination | Minimal lung deposition | Use spacer |
| Fast inhalation (MDI) | Oropharyngeal deposition | Slow 3-5 second inhalation |
| Slow inhalation (DPI) | Poor powder dispersion | Fast, forceful inhalation |
| Exhaling into DPI | Moisture damages powder | Always exhale away from device |
| No breath hold | Reduced deposition | Hold 5-10 seconds |
| Not rinsing after ICS | Oral candidiasis, dysphonia | Rinse and spit after each use |

## 7. Exacerbation Management

### Severity Assessment

| Parameter | Mild-Moderate | Severe | Life-Threatening |
|-----------|--------------|--------|------------------|
| **Talks in** | Sentences | Words/phrases | Unable |
| **Position** | Can lie down | Sits hunched | Drowsy, confused |
| **Alertness** | May be agitated | Agitated | Drowsy, confused |
| **Resp rate** | Increased | >30/min | May be decreased |
| **Accessory muscles** | None | Yes | Paradoxical |
| **Wheeze** | Moderate | Loud | Silent chest |
| **Heart rate** | <100 | 100-120 | >120 or bradycardia |
| **SpO₂ (room air)** | 90-95% | <90% | <90% |
| **PEF** | >50% predicted | ≤50% | <25% or unable |

### Emergency Department Management

```
INITIAL ASSESSMENT (0-30 minutes)
├─ ABC assessment, vital signs, SpO₂
├─ Brief history (severity, triggers, prior ICU, current meds)
├─ PEF or FEV₁ if possible
└─ CXR if suspect complication (pneumothorax, infection)

IMMEDIATE TREATMENT
├─ Oxygen: target SpO₂ 93-95% (adults), 94-98% (children)
├─ SABA: Salbutamol 4-10 puffs via MDI+spacer every 20 min × 1 hr
│         OR 2.5-5 mg nebulized every 20 min × 1 hr
├─ Ipratropium: Add if severe (500 mcg nebulized × 3 doses)
└─ Corticosteroids: Prednisolone 40-50 mg PO (or IV equivalent)
                     Within first hour!
```

### Additional Treatments for Severe/Life-Threatening

| Treatment | Dose | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| **IV Magnesium sulfate** | 2g over 20 min (adults) | Single dose; reduces admissions |
| **Continuous nebulized SABA** | 10-15 mg/hr salbutamol | For severe exacerbations |
| **IV aminophylline** | Load 5mg/kg then 0.5mg/kg/hr | Rarely used; monitor levels |
| **IV salbutamol** | 250 mcg bolus, then 5-20 mcg/min | ICU setting |
| **Epinephrine** | 0.3-0.5 mg IM | Anaphylaxis or angioedema |
| **NIV/intubation** | As indicated | ICU; ketamine preferred for sedation |

### Discharge Criteria

```
✓ Symptoms resolved or significantly improved
✓ PEF >60-70% predicted or personal best
✓ SpO₂ >94% on room air
✓ Can use inhaler correctly (demonstrated)
✓ Has adequate medication supply
✓ Has written action plan
✓ Follow-up arranged within 2-7 days
✓ Understands when to seek emergency care
```

### Discharge Medications

| Medication | Regimen |
|------------|---------|
| **Oral corticosteroids** | Prednisolone 40-50 mg daily × 5-7 days (no taper needed) |
| **Controller step-up** | Ensure ICS-containing controller; often step up for 2-4 weeks |
| **Reliever** | As needed; should need less frequently as improving |

## 8. Follow-Up Care

### Assessment Framework at Each Visit

```
SYMPTOM CONTROL (past 4 weeks):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Daytime symptoms >2×/week?              □ Yes □ No │
│ 2. Any night waking due to asthma?         □ Yes □ No │
│ 3. Reliever needed >2×/week?               □ Yes □ No │
│ 4. Any activity limitation due to asthma?  □ Yes □ No │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

CONTROL LEVEL:
• Well-controlled = 0 "Yes"
• Partly controlled = 1-2 "Yes"
• Uncontrolled = 3-4 "Yes"
```

### Risk Factor Assessment

| Risk Factor | Implications |
|-------------|--------------|
| **≥1 severe exacerbation in past year** | High risk for future exacerbations |
| **ICU admission/intubation ever** | High risk |
| **Low FEV₁** (especially <60% predicted) | Increased exacerbation risk |
| **High SABA use** (>1 canister/month) | Increased mortality risk |
| **Poor adherence** | Address barriers |
| **Incorrect inhaler technique** | Re-educate |
| **No ICS prescription** | Prescribe controller |
| **Smoking** | Counsel cessation |
| **Comorbidities** | Rhinosinusitis, GERD, obesity, anxiety/depression |
| **Major psychological problems** | May need additional support |
| **Food allergy in patient with asthma** | Increased anaphylaxis/asthma death risk |

### Stepping Down

```
CONSIDER STEP-DOWN WHEN:
• Symptoms well-controlled for ≥3 months
• Low risk of exacerbations
• No current respiratory infection
• No upcoming high-risk period (exams, travel)

APPROACH:
• Reduce ICS dose by 25-50% every 3 months
• Never completely stop ICS in adults diagnosed with asthma
• Maintain as-needed ICS-formoterol even when stepping down maintenance
• Monitor closely; step back up if control deteriorates
```

### Follow-Up Schedule

| Situation | Timing |
|-----------|--------|
| After starting treatment | 1-3 months |
| After exacerbation/ED visit | 2-7 days, then 1-3 months |
| Stable, well-controlled | Every 3-12 months |
| Step-down attempt | 3 months |
| Pregnancy | Every 4-6 weeks |

### Monitoring Tests

| Test | Frequency |
|------|-----------|
| **Spirometry** | At diagnosis; 3-6 months after starting controller; annually when stable |
| **PEF diary** | If variable symptoms, poor perception, severe asthma |
| **FeNO** | Guide ICS dosing; monitor adherence; assess eosinophilic inflammation |
| **ACT/ACQ** | At each visit (validated questionnaires) |

## 9. Pediatric Considerations

### Age-Based Diagnostic Approach

#### Children <5 Years

```
DIAGNOSIS IS CHALLENGING:
• Cannot perform spirometry reliably
• Wheeze common with viral infections
• Many will "outgrow" wheezing

SUGGESTIVE FEATURES:
• Wheeze or cough with exercise, laughing, crying
• History of other allergies or atopy
• Family history of asthma/atopy
• Clinical improvement with bronchodilator/ICS trial
• Symptoms persist beyond age 3
```

#### Wheezing Phenotypes in Preschoolers

| Phenotype | Features | Prognosis |
|-----------|----------|-----------|
| **Episodic viral wheeze** | Only with colds; well between episodes | Usually resolves by school age |
| **Multiple-trigger wheeze** | Various triggers including exercise, allergens | More likely to persist; treat as asthma |

#### Children 6-11 Years
- Can perform spirometry
- Diagnosis similar to adults
- Use child-specific predicted values

### Pediatric Treatment (GINA 2023)

#### Children 0-5 Years

| Step | Preferred Controller | Alternative |
|------|---------------------|-------------|
| 1 | As-needed SABA | — |
| 2 | Daily low-dose ICS | Intermittent ICS or daily LTRA |
| 3 | Double low-dose ICS | Low-dose ICS + LTRA |
| 4 | Continue treatment and REFER | — |

#### Children 6-11 Years

| Step | Preferred Controller | Alternative |
|------|---------------------|-------------|
| 1 | As-needed ICS-formoterol OR ICS whenever SABA used | — |
| 2 | Daily low-dose ICS | Daily LTRA |
| 3 | Low-dose ICS-formoterol MART | Med-dose ICS or low ICS-LABA |
| 4 | Medium-dose ICS-formoterol MART | Med-dose ICS-LABA ± LTRA or tiotropium |
| 5 | Refer; consider biologics | — |

### Pediatric ICS Doses (mcg/day)

| Drug | Low (6-11 yrs) | Low (<5 yrs) |
|------|----------------|--------------|
| Beclomethasone HFA | 50-100 | 100 |
| Budesonide DPI | 100-200 | — |
| Budesonide nebulized | — | 250-500 |
| Fluticasone propionate | 50-100 | 50 |
| Fluticasone furoate | 50 | — |

### Device Selection by Age

| Age | Preferred Device |
|-----|-----------------|
| 0-3 years | MDI + spacer with face mask |
| 4-5 years | MDI + spacer with mouthpiece |
| ≥6 years | MDI + spacer OR DPI (if adequate inspiratory flow) |
| Any age (acute) | MDI + spacer OR nebulizer |

### Growth and ICS

```
EVIDENCE:
• ICS may reduce growth velocity by ~0.5 cm in first 1-2 years
• Effect generally not cumulative
• Final adult height reduced by ~1 cm on average
• Uncontrolled asthma also impairs growth

RECOMMENDATION:
• Use lowest effective ICS dose
• Monitor height annually
• Benefits of asthma control outweigh risks
• Do not withhold ICS due to growth concerns
```

|------------|------|
| **Salbutamol** | 2-6 puffs (100mcg/puff) via spacer, every 20 min × 3 |
| **Prednisolone** | 1-2 mg/kg/day (max 40 mg) × 3-5 days |
| **IV Magnesium** | 25-50 mg/kg (max 2g) over 20 min |

## 10. Occupational Asthma

### Classification

| Type | Mechanism | Latency | Examples |
|------|-----------|---------|----------|
| **Sensitizer-induced** | Immunologic (IgE or non-IgE) | Weeks to years | Isocyanates, flour, latex |
| **Irritant-induced (RADS)** | Non-immunologic, single high exposure | None | Chlorine gas, ammonia |
| **Work-exacerbated asthma** | Pre-existing asthma worsened by work | N/A | Various irritants |

### Common Occupational Sensitizers

| Agent | Occupations |
|-------|-------------|
| **Isocyanates** | Spray painters, foam production, adhesives |
| **Flour/grain dust** | Bakers, millers, farmers |
| **Wood dust** | Carpenters, sawmill workers |
| **Laboratory animals** | Researchers, animal handlers |
| **Latex** | Healthcare workers |
| **Enzymes** | Detergent industry, baking |
| **Metals (platinum, chromium)** | Welders, metalworkers, electroplating |
| **Cleaning agents** | Healthcare workers, cleaners |
| **Persulfates** | Hairdressers |

### Diagnostic Approach

```
CLINICAL SUSPICION:
• Adult-onset asthma
• Symptoms improve on weekends/vacations
• Symptoms worsen after returning to work
• Multiple co-workers affected (if outbreak)

DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP:
1. Detailed occupational history
   └─ Timeline, exposures, ventilation, PPE use
2. Serial PEF monitoring
   └─ ≥4× daily for ≥2 weeks at work and 2 weeks away
   └─ >20% variation suggests occupational component
3. Immunological testing
   └─ Skin prick tests or specific IgE (if available)
4. Specific inhalation challenge
   └─ Gold standard; specialized centers only
```

### Serial PEF Interpretation

```
SUGGESTIVE PATTERN:
• Lower PEF values on work days
• Higher PEF on rest days
• Progressive decline during work week
• Improvement during vacation/sick leave

ANALYSIS:
• Plot data graphically
• Calculate work vs. non-work means
• Use validated scoring systems (e.g., Oasys-2)
```

### Management

| Strategy | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Complete removal from exposure** | Best outcome; ideally within 12 months of diagnosis |
| **Reduce exposure** | May be insufficient; symptoms may persist |
| **PPE (respirators)** | Temporary measure; not long-term solution |
| **Standard asthma treatment** | ICS, bronchodilators as per guidelines |
| **Workplace modifications** | Improved ventilation, substitution of agents |
| **Medical surveillance** | Periodic spirometry for exposed workers |
| **Legal/compensation** | Document diagnosis; support workers' compensation claims |

### Prognosis

```
FAVORABLE FACTORS:
• Early diagnosis (<1 year of symptoms)
• Complete removal from exposure
• Normal lung function at diagnosis
• Younger age

POOR PROGNOSIS:
• Prolonged exposure after symptom onset
• Severe airflow limitation at diagnosis
• High-molecular-weight sensitizers
• Continued exposure (even at reduced levels)

NOTE: ~70% have persistent symptoms even after removal from exposure
```

### Prevention

| Level | Intervention |
|-------|--------------|
| **Primary** | Eliminate/substitute hazardous agents; engineering controls |
| **Secondary** | Medical surveillance; pre-placement spirometry; early detection |
| **Tertiary** | Early removal from exposure; optimal treatment |

## 1. Fundamentals & Stationarity {#1-fundamentals}

```python
"""
TIME SERIES FUNDAMENTALS AND STATIONARITY
==========================================
Understanding the building blocks of time series analysis.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller, kpss, acf, pacf
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf, plot_pacf
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose, STL
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# Set plotting style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')


class TimeSeriesFundamentals:
    """
    Core concepts and tools for time series analysis.
    
    A time series has four main components:
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Y(t) = Trend + Seasonality + Cyclical + Irregular     │
    │                                                         │
    │  • Trend: Long-term increase/decrease                  │
    │  • Seasonality: Regular patterns at fixed intervals    │
    │  • Cyclical: Patterns without fixed period             │
    │  • Irregular: Random noise/residuals                   │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    """
    
    def __init__(self, random_state: int = 42):
        np.random.seed(random_state)
    
    def generate_synthetic_series(
        self,
        n_points: int = 365 * 3,
        include_trend: bool = True,
        include_seasonality: bool = True,
        include_noise: bool = True,
        trend_slope: float = 0.05,
        seasonal_period: int = 365,
        seasonal_amplitude: float = 10,
        noise_std: float = 2
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Generate synthetic time series with controllable components.
        
        This helps understand how each component contributes to the series.
        """
        dates = pd.date_range(start='2020-01-01', periods=n_points, freq='D')
        t = np.arange(n_points)
        
        # Initialize components
        trend = np.zeros(n_points)
        seasonality = np.zeros(n_points)
        noise = np.zeros(n_points)
        
        if include_trend:
            # Linear trend with slight curvature
            trend = trend_slope * t + 0.0001 * t**1.2
        
        if include_seasonality:
            # Annual seasonality (sinusoidal)
            seasonality = seasonal_amplitude * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / seasonal_period)
            # Add weekly pattern
            seasonality += 3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t / 7)
        
        if include_noise:
            noise = np.random.normal(0, noise_std, n_points)
        
        # Combine components
        values = 100 + trend + seasonality + noise  # Base level of 100
        
        df = pd.DataFrame({
            'date': dates,
            'value': values,
            'trend': 100 + trend,
            'seasonality': seasonality,
            'noise': noise
        })
        df.set_index('date', inplace=True)
        
        return df
    
    def plot_decomposition(self, series: pd.Series, period: int = None):
        """
        Decompose and visualize time series components.
        
        Two decomposition types:
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ ADDITIVE:       Y(t) = T(t) + S(t) + R(t)         │
        │ MULTIPLICATIVE: Y(t) = T(t) × S(t) × R(t)         │
        │                                                    │
        │ Use additive when seasonal variations are constant │
        │ Use multiplicative when they scale with the level  │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        """
        if period is None:
            period = min(len(series) // 2 - 1, 365)
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(5, 1, figsize=(14, 12))
        
        # Original series
        axes[0].plot(series.index, series.values, 'b-', linewidth=0.8)
        axes[0].set_title('Original Time Series', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        axes[0].set_ylabel('Value')
        
        # Classical decomposition
        decomposition = seasonal_decompose(series, model='additive', period=period)
        
        axes[1].plot(series.index, decomposition.trend, 'g-', linewidth=1.5)
        axes[1].set_title('Trend Component', fontsize=12)
        axes[1].set_ylabel('Trend')
        
        axes[2].plot(series.index, decomposition.seasonal, 'orange', linewidth=0.8)
        axes[2].set_title('Seasonal Component', fontsize=12)
        axes[2].set_ylabel('Seasonal')
        
        axes[3].plot(series.index, decomposition.resid, 'r-', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.7)
        axes[3].set_title('Residual Component', fontsize=12)
        axes[3].set_ylabel('Residual')
        
        # STL Decomposition (more robust)
        stl = STL(series, period=period, robust=True).fit()
        axes[4].plot(series.index, stl.resid, 'purple', linewidth=0.5, alpha=0.7)
        axes[4].set_title('STL Residual (Robust Decomposition)', fontsize=12)
        axes[4].set_ylabel('Residual')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        return fig, decomposition


class StationarityAnalysis:
    """
    Stationarity testing and transformation tools.
    
    WHAT IS STATIONARITY?
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ A stationary series has:                                   │
    │                                                             │
    │ 1. CONSTANT MEAN: E[Y(t)] = μ for all t                    │
    │ 2. CONSTANT VARIANCE: Var[Y(t)] = σ² for all t             │
    │ 3. AUTOCOVARIANCE depends only on lag, not time:           │
    │    Cov[Y(t), Y(t+k)] = γ(k) for all t                      │
    │                                                             │
    │ WHY IT MATTERS:                                             │
    │ • Most forecasting models assume stationarity               │
    │ • Non-stationary series have unpredictable long-term       │
    │   behavior and can produce spurious correlations           │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.test_results = {}
    
    def adf_test(
        self,
        series: pd.Series,
        significance_level: float = 0.05,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test for stationarity.
        
        HYPOTHESIS:
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ H₀: Series has a unit root (non-stat) │
        │ H₁: Series is stationary              │
        │                                        │
        │ Reject H₀ if p-value < α              │
        │ → Evidence for stationarity           │
        └────────────────────────────────────────┘
        
        The test checks if ρ = 1 in: Y(t) = ρ·Y(t-1) + ε(t)
        Transformed to: ΔY(t) = (ρ-1)·Y(t-1) + ε(t) = δ·Y(t-1) + ε(t)
        Tests if δ = 0 (unit root) vs δ < 0 (stationary)
        """
        # Remove NaN values
        clean_series = series.dropna()
        
        result = adfuller(clean_series, autolag='AIC')
        
        output = {
            'test_statistic': result[0],
            'p_value': result[1],
            'lags_used': result[2],
            'n_observations': result[3],
            'critical_values': result[4],
            'is_stationary': result[1] < significance_level,
            'significance_level': significance_level
        }
        
        if verbose:
            print("=" * 60)
            print("AUGMENTED DICKEY-FULLER TEST")
            print("=" * 60)
            print(f"Test Statistic:    {output['test_statistic']:.6f}")
            print(f"P-Value:           {output['p_value']:.6f}")
            print(f"Lags Used:         {output['lags_used']}")
            print(f"Observations:      {output['n_observations']}")
            print("-" * 60)
            print("Critical Values:")
            for key, value in output['critical_values'].items():
                marker = "←" if output['test_statistic'] < value else ""
                print(f"  {key}: {value:.4f} {marker}")
            print("-" * 60)
            
            if output['is_stationary']:
                print(f"✓ STATIONARY at {significance_level:.0%} significance level")
                print("  (Reject null hypothesis of unit root)")
            else:
                print(f"✗ NON-STATIONARY at {significance_level:.0%} significance level")
                print("  (Cannot reject null hypothesis of unit root)")
            print("=" * 60)
        
        self.test_results['adf'] = output
        return output
    
    def kpss_test(
        self,
        series: pd.Series,
        regression: str = 'c',
        significance_level: float = 0.05,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> dict:
        """
        KPSS Test for stationarity.
        
        HYPOTHESIS (opposite of ADF!):
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ H₀: Series is stationary              │
        │ H₁: Series has a unit root (non-stat) │
        │                                        │
        │ Reject H₀ if p-value < α              │
        │ → Evidence AGAINST stationarity       │
        └────────────────────────────────────────┘
        
        Parameters:
        - regression='c': Test stationarity around constant mean
        - regression='ct': Test trend stationarity
        """
        clean_series = series.dropna()
        
        result = kpss(clean_series, regression=regression, nlags='auto')
        
        output = {
            'test_statistic': result[0],
            'p_value': result[1],
            'lags_used': result[2],
            'critical_values': result[3],
            'is_stationary': result[1] >= significance_level,
            'significance_level': significance_level,
            'regression_type': regression
        }
        
        if verbose:
            print("=" * 60)
            print(f"KPSS TEST (regression='{regression}')")
            print("=" * 60)
            print(f"Test Statistic:    {output['test_statistic']:.6f}")
            print(f"P-Value:           {output['p_value']:.6f}")
            print(f"Lags Used:         {output['lags_used']}")
            print("-" * 60)
            print("Critical Values:")
            for key, value in output['critical_values'].items():
                marker = "←" if output['test_statistic'] > value else ""
                print(f"  {key}: {value:.4f} {marker}")
            print("-" * 60)
            
            if output['is_stationary']:
                print(f"✓ STATIONARY at {significance_level:.0%} significance level")
                print("  (Cannot reject null hypothesis of stationarity)")
            else:
                print(f"✗ NON-STATIONARY at {significance_level:.0%} significance level")
                print("  (Reject null hypothesis of stationarity)")
            print("=" * 60)
        
        self.test_results['kpss'] = output
        return output
    
    def combined_stationarity_test(
        self,
        series: pd.Series,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Run both ADF and KPSS tests for comprehensive analysis.
        
        INTERPRETATION MATRIX:
        ┌─────────────┬─────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ ADF Result  │ KPSS Result │ Conclusion                         │
        ├─────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
        │ Stationary  │ Stationary  │ ✓ Series is stationary             │
        │ Stationary  │ Non-stat    │ ⚠ Trend stationary (difference)   │
        │ Non-stat    │ Stationary  │ ⚠ Difference stationary (careful) │
        │ Non-stat    │ Non-stat    │ ✗ Non-stationary (transform)       │
        └─────────────┴─────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
        """
        adf_result = self.adf_test(series, verbose=False)
        kpss_result = self.kpss_test(series, verbose=False)
        
        adf_stationary = adf_result['is_stationary']
        kpss_stationary = kpss_result['is_stationary']
        
        # Determine conclusion
        if adf_stationary and kpss_stationary:
            conclusion = "STATIONARY"
            recommendation = "Series can be modeled directly"
            confidence = "High"
        elif adf_stationary and not kpss_stationary:
            conclusion = "TREND-STATIONARY"
            recommendation = "Consider differencing or detrending"
            confidence = "Medium"
        elif not adf_stationary and kpss_stationary:
            conclusion = "DIFFERENCE-STATIONARY"
            recommendation = "Apply differencing transformation"
            confidence = "Medium"
        else:
            conclusion = "NON-STATIONARY"
            recommendation = "Apply transformations (diff, log, or both)"
            confidence = "High"
        
        output = {
            'adf_stationary': adf_stationary,
            'kpss_stationary': kpss_stationary,
            'conclusion': conclusion,
            'recommendation': recommendation,
            'confidence': confidence
        }
        
        if verbose:
            print("\n" + "=" * 60)
            print("COMBINED STATIONARITY ANALYSIS")
            print("=" * 60)
            print(f"ADF Test:  {'Stationary' if adf_stationary else 'Non-stationary'}")
            print(f"KPSS Test: {'Stationary' if kpss_stationary else 'Non-stationary'}")
            print("-" * 60)
            print(f"CONCLUSION: {conclusion}")
            print(f"Confidence: {confidence}")
            print(f"Recommendation: {recommendation}")
            print("=" * 60)
        
        return output
    
    def make_stationary(
        self,
        series: pd.Series,
        method: str = 'auto',
        max_diff: int = 2,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> tuple:
        """
        Transform series to achieve stationarity.
        
        TRANSFORMATION METHODS:
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ 1. DIFFERENCING: Y'(t) = Y(t) - Y(t-1)                     │
        │    → Removes trend, applies d times for integration order  │
        │                                                             │
        │ 2. LOG TRANSFORM: Y'(t) = log(Y(t))                        │
        │    → Stabilizes variance when it grows with level          │
        │                                                             │
        │ 3. BOX-COX: Y'(t) = (Y(t)^λ - 1) / λ                       │
        │    → General power transformation, finds optimal λ         │
        │                                                             │
        │ 4. SEASONAL DIFFERENCING: Y'(t) = Y(t) - Y(t-m)            │
        │    → Removes seasonal pattern of period m                  │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        
        Returns:
            (transformed_series, transformations_applied)
        """
        transformations = []
        transformed = series.copy()
        
        if method == 'auto':
            # Check if log transform might help (for positive series with growing variance)
            if (series > 0).all():
                # Rolling std to check if variance increases with level
                rolling_std = series.rolling(window=min(30, len(series)//10)).std()
                rolling_mean = series.rolling(window=min(30, len(series)//10)).mean()
                correlation = np.corrcoef(
                    rolling_mean.dropna(),
                    rolling_std.dropna()
                )[0, 1]
                
                if correlation > 0.5:  # Variance increases with level
                    transformed = np.log(transformed)
                    transformations.append('log')
                    if verbose:
                        print(f"Applied log transform (variance-mean correlation: {correlation:.2f})")
            
            # Apply differencing until stationary
            for d in range(1, max_diff + 1):
                adf_result = self.adf_test(transformed.dropna(), verbose=False)
                
                if adf_result['is_stationary']:
                    break
                
                transformed = transformed.diff()
                transformations.append(f'diff_order_{d}')
                if verbose:
                    print(f"Applied differencing (order {d})")
        
        elif method == 'difference':
            transformed = transformed.diff()
            transformations.append('diff_order_1')
        
        elif method == 'log':
            if (series > 0).all():
                transformed = np.log(transformed)
                transformations.append('log')
            else:
                raise ValueError("Log transform requires all positive values")
        
        elif method == 'log_diff':
            if (series > 0).all():
                transformed = np.log(transformed).diff()
                transformations.append('log')
                transformations.append('diff_order_1')
            else:
                raise ValueError("Log transform requires all positive values")
        
        # Final stationarity check
        if verbose:
            print("\nFinal stationarity check:")
            self.combined_stationarity_test(transformed.dropna())
        
        return transformed.dropna(), transformations
    
    def plot_acf_pacf(
        self,
        series: pd.Series,
        lags: int = 40,
        title: str = "ACF and PACF Analysis"
    ):
        """
        Plot ACF and PACF for model identification.
        
        INTERPRETATION GUIDE:
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ ACF (AutoCorrelation Function):                            │
        │   • Shows correlation between Y(t) and Y(t-k)              │
        │   • Includes indirect correlations through intermediate    │
        │     lags                                                   │
        │                                                             │
        │ PACF (Partial AutoCorrelation Function):                   │
        │   • Shows DIRECT correlation between Y(t) and Y(t-k)       │
        │   • Removes effect of intermediate lags                    │
        │                                                             │
        │ MODEL IDENTIFICATION:                                       │
        │ ┌──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────────┐ │
        │ │ ACF Pattern  │ PACF Pattern │ Suggested Model          │ │
        │ ├──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────────────┤ │
        │ │ Decays       │ Cuts off p   │ AR(p)                    │ │
        │ │ Cuts off q   │ Decays       │ MA(q)                    │ │
        │ │ Decays       │ Decays       │ ARMA(p,q)                │ │
        │ │ Slow decay   │ ~1 at lag 1  │ Need differencing        │ │
        │ └──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────────┘ │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        """
        clean_series = series.dropna()
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 10))
        
        # Time series plot
        axes[0, 0].plot(clean_series.index, clean_series.values, 'b-', linewidth=0.8)
        axes[0, 0].set_title('Time Series', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Time')
        axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Value')
        
        # Distribution
        axes[0, 1].hist(clean_series.values, bins=50, edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
        axes[0, 1].axvline(clean_series.mean(), color='r', linestyle='--', label=f'Mean: {clean_series.mean():.2f}')
        axes[0, 1].set_title('Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        axes[0, 1].legend()
        
        # ACF
        plot_acf(clean_series, lags=lags, ax=axes[1, 0], alpha=0.05)
        axes[1, 0].set_title('Autocorrelation Function (ACF)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        
        # PACF
        plot_pacf(clean_series, lags=lags, ax=axes[1, 1], alpha=0.05, method='ywm')
        axes[1, 1].set_title('Partial Autocorrelation Function (PACF)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
        
        fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        return fig


# Demonstration
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=" * 70)
    print("TIME SERIES FUNDAMENTALS DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Generate synthetic data
