## 3. Centering and Standardization

### Step 1: Centering (Always Required)

Subtract the mean of each variable:

```
x_centered = x - x̄

Example:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Original X         Means          Centered X_c
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│ 1   2 │                        │ -2   -1 │
│ 2   1 │        x̄₁ = 3          │ -1   -2 │
│ 4   5 │        x̄₂ = 3          │  1    2 │
│ 5   4 │                        │  2    1 │
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

**Why center?** PCA finds directions of maximum variance *from the origin*. Without centering, PC1 would point toward the data cloud's center, not along its spread.

### Step 2: Standardization (Often Required)

Divide by standard deviation to create **z-scores**:

```
z = (x - x̄) / s

When to standardize:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STANDARDIZE (use correlation)     DON'T STANDARDIZE (use covariance)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Variables on different scales   • Variables on same scale
  (meters vs. kilograms)           (all in centimeters)
  
• Variables with very different   • Variance differences are
  variances                         meaningful
  
• When you want equal             • When some variables should
  contribution from all vars        contribute more
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

### Numeric Example: Why Standardization Matters

```
Original data (Height in cm, Weight in kg):
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Person    Height(cm)    Weight(kg)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1         160            60
  2         170            65
  3         180            70
  4         190            75
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Variances:
  Var(Height) = 166.67    (large because of units)
  Var(Weight) = 41.67     (smaller number scale)
  
Without standardization:
  PC1 ≈ [0.97, 0.24]  ← Dominated by Height!
  
With standardization:
  PC1 ≈ [0.71, 0.71]  ← Equal contribution
```

## 4. Covariance vs. Correlation Matrix

Both matrices can drive PCA:

### Covariance Matrix (on centered data)

```
         1
Σ = ───────── X_c^T X_c

Structure:
        ┌─────────────────────────────┐
        │  Var(X₁)    Cov(X₁,X₂)  ... │
Σ =     │  Cov(X₂,X₁) Var(X₂)     ... │
        │  ...        ...         ... │
        └─────────────────────────────┘
```

### Correlation Matrix (on standardized data)

```
        ┌─────────────────────────────┐
        │    1       r(X₁,X₂)    ...  │
R =     │ r(X₂,X₁)     1         ...  │

```

Using our centered data:

```
X_c =   │ -1   -2 │

        │  2    1 │

Var(X₂) = [(-1)² + (-2)² + 2² + 1²] / 3 = 10/3
Cov(X₁,X₂) = [(-2)(-1) + (-1)(-2) + (1)(2) + (2)(1)] / 3 = 8/3
```

## 5. Eigen-Decomposition Method

Find eigenvalues (λ) and eigenvectors (v) of the covariance/correlation matrix.

### The Math

```
Σv = λv

Where:
• λ = eigenvalue (variance captured by that component)
• v = eigenvector (direction of that component, the "loadings")
```

### Numeric Example

```
Find eigenvalues of Σ = ┌ 10/3   8/3 ┐
                        └  8/3  10/3 ┘

Characteristic equation: det(Σ - λI) = 0

│ 10/3 - λ     8/3    │
│                     │ = 0
│   8/3     10/3 - λ  │

(10/3 - λ)² - (8/3)² = 0
(10/3 - λ)² = 64/9
10/3 - λ = ± 8/3

λ₁ = 10/3 + 8/3 = 18/3 = 6
λ₂ = 10/3 - 8/3 = 2/3

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Finding Eigenvectors:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

For λ₁ = 6:
(Σ - 6I)v = 0

┌ 10/3-6    8/3   ┐ ┌ v₁ ┐   ┌ 0 ┐
│                 │ │    │ = │   │
└  8/3    10/3-6  ┘ └ v₂ ┘   └ 0 ┘

┌ -8/3   8/3 ┐ ┌ v₁ ┐   ┌ 0 ┐
│            │ │    │ = │   │
└  8/3  -8/3 ┘ └ v₂ ┘   └ 0 ┘

-8/3 v₁ + 8/3 v₂ = 0  →  v₁ = v₂

Normalized eigenvector: v₁ = [1/√2, 1/√2] = [0.707, 0.707]

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
For λ₂ = 2/3:

┌ 8/3   8/3 ┐ ┌ v₁ ┐   ┌ 0 ┐
│           │ │    │ = │   │
└ 8/3   8/3 ┘ └ v₂ ┘   └ 0 ┘

v₁ + v₂ = 0  →  v₁ = -v₂

Normalized eigenvector: v₂ = [1/√2, -1/√2] = [0.707, -0.707]
```

### Summary of Eigen-Decomposition

```
Principal Component Loadings (V):
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
              PC1      PC2
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Variable 1   0.707    0.707
Variable 2   0.707   -0.707
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Eigenvalues:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PC1: λ₁ = 6      (larger variance)
PC2: λ₂ = 0.667  (smaller variance)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Geometric Interpretation:
                    X₂
                    ↑      
                    │   ╱ PC1 (v₁)
                    │  ╱  direction [0.71, 0.71]
                    │ ╱   max variance
            ────────┼╱────────→ X₁
                   ╱│
                  ╱ │
           PC2   ╱  │
      [0.71,-0.71]  │
      min variance  │
```

## 6. SVD Method (Alternative to Eigen-Decomposition)

SVD decomposes the centered data matrix directly:

```
X_c = U S V^T

Where:
• U (n × n): Left singular vectors (observation scores, normalized)
• S (n × p): Diagonal matrix of singular values
• V^T (p × p): Right singular vectors (loadings) ← Same as eigenvectors of Σ!
```

### Connection Between SVD and Eigen-Decomposition

```
Covariance matrix:  Σ = X_c^T X_c / (n-1)

Using SVD:
X_c^T X_c = (USV^T)^T (USV^T)
          = VS^T U^T U S V^T
          = V S² V^T              (since U^T U = I)

Therefore:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Eigenvalues of Σ:  λᵢ = sᵢ² / (n-1)
• Eigenvectors of Σ: columns of V
• PC scores:         X_c × V = US
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

### Why Use SVD?

```
┌─────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Eigen-decomposition │           SVD                       │
├─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Computes Σ first    │ Works directly on X_c               │
│ (p × p matrix)      │ (n × p matrix)                      │
├─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Problem with        │ Numerically stable                  │
│ near-singular Σ     │                                     │
├─────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Fast when n >> p    │ Fast when p >> n                    │
│                     │ (doesn't form p×p matrix)           │
└─────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Transform original data to PC space:

```
Scores = X_centered × V

Using our example:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
        │ -2   -1 │         │ 0.707   0.707 │
X_c =   │ -1   -2 │    V =  │               │
        │  1    2 │         │ 0.707  -0.707 │
        │  2    1 │

Scores = X_c × V

        │ -2(0.707) + (-1)(0.707)    -2(0.707) + (-1)(-0.707) │
      = │ -1(0.707) + (-2)(0.707)    -1(0.707) + (-2)(-0.707) │
        │  1(0.707) +   2(0.707)      1(0.707) +   2(-0.707)  │
        │  2(0.707) +   1(0.707)      2(0.707) +   1(-0.707)  │

        │ -2.12   -0.71 │
      ≈ │ -2.12    0.71 │     ← PC scores for each observation
        │  2.12   -0.71 │
        │  2.12    0.71 │
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

```python
print("\nCovariance Matrix:")
print(cov_matrix)

# Step 3: Eigen-decomposition
eigenvalues, eigenvectors = np.linalg.eig(cov_matrix)

# Sort by eigenvalue (descending)
idx = eigenvalues.argsort()[::-1]
eigenvalues = eigenvalues[idx]
eigenvectors = eigenvectors[:, idx]

print("\nEigenvalues:", eigenvalues)
print("Eigenvectors (columns):")
print(eigenvectors)

# Step 4: Compute scores
scores = X_centered @ eigenvectors
print("\nPC Scores:")
print(scores)

# Step 5: Variance explained
var_explained = eigenvalues / eigenvalues.sum()
print("\nVariance Explained:", var_explained)
print("Cumulative:", np.cumsum(var_explained))
```

## 11. Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: Forgetting to Center

```
✗ WRONG: PCA on raw data
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Data cloud at [100, 100]:
Without centering, PC1 points TOWARD the cloud center
instead of ALONG the direction of maximum spread.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

✓ CORRECT: Always center (subtract mean)
```

### Pitfall 2: Ignoring Scale Differences

```
✗ WRONG: Using covariance when scales differ
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Income ($): 30,000 - 100,000    Var ≈ 10⁹
Age (yrs):  20 - 80             Var ≈ 10²

PC1 will be ~100% income, ignoring age entirely!
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

✓ CORRECT: Standardize (use correlation matrix)
```

### Pitfall 3: Applying PCA to Non-Linear Relationships

```
            ●●●●●●
           ●      ●
          ●        ●        PCA finds linear directions!
         ●          ●       
        ●            ●      For circular/curved data:
         ●          ●       → Use Kernel PCA
          ●        ●        → Use UMAP/t-SNE
           ●      ●
            ●●●●●●
```

### Pitfall 4: Over-interpreting Components

```
✗ WRONG: "PC1 IS the latent factor causing X1 and X2"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PCA is purely mathematical rotation.
It finds correlation, not causation.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

✓ CORRECT: "PC1 captures shared variance in X1, X2"
           Use Factor Analysis if you want latent variables.
```

### Pitfall 5: Using PCA on Categorical Variables

```
✗ WRONG: PCA on [Male=1, Female=2, Other=3]
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PCA assumes continuous, linear relationships.
"2" is not "twice" the gender of "1"!
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

✓ CORRECT: Use Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA)
           or one-hot encode with caution
```

### Pitfall 6: Outlier Sensitivity

```
Regular data:              With outlier:
    ╱                          ●
   ╱  ●●●●                      ╲
  ╱ ●●●●                         ╲
 ╱●●●●                            ╲ PC1 now tilted
  PC1                              ╲ toward outlier!
                                    ●●●●
                                    
Solution: Use robust PCA or remove outliers first
```

### Pitfall 7: Sign Ambiguity of Eigenvectors

```
Both v = [0.71, 0.71] and v = [-0.71, -0.71] are valid!
Eigenvectors are defined up to a sign flip.

✓ Resolution:
  • Be consistent within your analysis
  • Focus on relative relationships, not absolute signs
  • Convention: largest loading positive
```

### Pitfall 8: Too Few Observations

```
Rule of thumb: n ≥ 5p (observations ≥ 5× variables)

With n < p:
• Covariance matrix is singular
• At most n-1 non-zero eigenvalues
• Overfitting risk

Solutions:
• Use regularized PCA
• Use SVD directly
• Collect more data
```

### Pitfall 9: Assuming Independence = Uncorrelatedness

```
PCA creates UNCORRELATED components, not INDEPENDENT.

Uncorrelated: Cov(PC1, PC2) = 0  (linear relationship = 0)
Independent:  All relationships = 0 (including nonlinear)

For independence: Use Independent Component Analysis (ICA)
```

### Trade-off Theory
- Firm trades off benefits of debt (tax shield) against costs (distress)

### Pecking Order Theory
- Firms prefer internal financing
- Then debt
- Then equity (last resort)
- No optimal capital structure; capital structure is cumulative result of past financing decisions

### Signaling Theory


Management uses capital structure choices to communicate internal insights. High debt levels can indicate confidence in future cash flows, while equity issuance might suggest management believes the stock is overvalued. ## WACC Calculation

The weighted average cost of capital represents the blended expense of a company's financing sources. It combines the proportional costs of equity and debt, adjusted for tax benefits. By weighting each capital component, WACC provides a comprehensive measure of a firm's overall cost of financing.

### Levered Beta

Levered beta captures the financial risk introduced by a firm's debt structure. It demonstrates how a company's equity risk changes with financial leverage, reflecting increased volatility as debt levels rise. The formula adjusts the unlevered beta by incorporating the firm's debt-to-equity ratio and tax implications.

## Tax Shield

Tax shields represent a critical value creation mechanism through debt financing. By deducting interest expenses, firms reduce their tax liability. The present value of these tax benefits depends on the debt's characteristics and the firm's risk profile, offering a quantifiable financial advantage.

## Financial Distress

Financial distress involves both tangible and intangible costs. Beyond direct expenses like legal fees, companies face significant indirect challenges such as lost business opportunities and management disruption. The expected distress cost integrates the probability of financial difficulty with potential economic consequences.

## Optimal Leverage

Firms seek an ideal capital structure balancing debt's benefits against potential risks. The optimal point emerges where the marginal advantages of additional debt precisely offset the incremental costs of financial vulnerability.

```
│ Equity Issuance    │ Normal financing choice │ Signal of overvaluation     │
│                    │                         │                             │
│ Financial Slack    │ Less important          │ Very important              │
│                    │                         │                             │
│ Market Timing      │ Not considered          │ Opportunistic financing     │
│                    │                         │                             │
│ Industry Leverage  │ Firms converge to       │ Firm-specific factors       │
│                    │ industry mean           │ dominate                    │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE:
═══════════════════
• Profitable firms have less debt → Supports pecking order
• Firms have target ranges     → Supports trade-off
• Stock prices drop on equity announcements → Supports pecking order
• Firms adjust toward targets slowly → Supports dynamic trade-off
```

## 5. Signaling Theory

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          SIGNALING THEORY                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  CORE CONCEPT: Capital structure choices convey information to markets     │
│                                                                             │
│  ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ │
│  ║                    ROSS MODEL (1977)                                   ║ │
│  ╠═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  Managers know true firm value; outsiders don't                       ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  DEBT AS A SIGNAL:                                                    ║ │
│  ║  • High-quality firms can support more debt                           ║ │
│  ║  • Debt ↑ → Signal of high expected cash flows                       ║ │
│  ║  • Equity issuance may signal overvaluation                          ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  V₀ = V₀* + λ(D - D*)                                                ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  Market infers quality from debt level                                ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ │
│                                                                             │
│  LELAND-PYLE MODEL (1977):                                                  │
│  ─────────────────────────                                                  │
│  • Entrepreneur's retained ownership signals quality                        │
│  • Higher ownership retention → Higher expected value                      │
│  • Equilibrium: Value = f(α), where α = fraction retained                  │
│                                                                             │
│  SIGNALING ACTIONS AND MARKET REACTIONS:                                    │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Action                      │ Typical Market Reaction                │  │
│  ├─────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
│  │ Debt increase              │ Positive (+1% to +3%)                  │  │
│  │ Leverage buyout            │ Strong positive (+15% to +40%)         │  │
│  │ Stock repurchase           │ Positive (+3% to +5%)                  │  │
│  │ Dividend increase          │ Positive (+1% to +2%)                  │  │
│  │ Equity issuance (SEO)      │ Negative (-2% to -3%)                  │  │
│  │ Convertible bond issue     │ Slight negative (-1% to -2%)           │  │
│  │ Debt reduction             │ Mixed (depends on reason)              │  │
│  └─────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                             │
│  CONDITIONS FOR CREDIBLE SIGNAL:                                            │
│  • Cost of false signal must be high                                        │
```

## 6. Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)

### WACC Formula and Components

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    WACC ESTIMATION FRAMEWORK                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║         WACC = (E/V) × rₑ + (D/V) × r_d × (1 - τ_c)                  ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  EXPANDED (with preferred stock):                                     ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  WACC = (E/V)×rₑ + (P/V)×r_p + (D/V)×r_d×(1-τ_c)                    ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ │
│                                                                             │
│  COMPONENT BREAKDOWN:                                                       │
│  ════════════════════                                                       │
│                                                                             │
│  MARKET VALUES:                                                             │
│    E = Share price × Shares outstanding                                     │
│    D = Market value of debt (≈ book value if trading near par)             │
│    V = E + D (or E + P + D)                                                 │
│                                                                             │
│  COST OF EQUITY (rₑ):                                                       │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  CAPM:    rₑ = r_f + βₑ × (r_m - r_f)                              │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Fama-French: rₑ = r_f + β₁(MKT) + β₂(SMB) + β₃(HML)              │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Dividend Growth: rₑ = (D₁/P₀) + g                                 │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Build-up: rₑ = r_f + Equity Premium + Size Premium + Specific Risk│   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  COST OF DEBT (r_d):                                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Yield to Maturity on existing debt                                 │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  OR: r_d = r_f + Default Spread                                    │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Credit Rating   │  Typical Spread                                  │   │
│  │  ────────────────┼──────────────────                                │   │
│  │  AAA             │  0.5% - 0.7%                                     │   │
│  │  AA              │  0.7% - 1.0%                                     │   │
│  │  A               │  1.0% - 1.5%                                     │   │
│  │  BBB             │  1.5% - 2.5%                                     │   │
│  │  BB              │  3.0% - 4.0%                                     │   │
│  │  B               │  4.5% - 6.0%                                     │   │
│  │  CCC             │  8.0% - 12.0%                                    │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Beta Calculations

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         BETA RELATIONSHIPS                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  UNLEVERING BETA (remove capital structure effect):                         │
│  ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════                        │
│                                                                             │
│  HAMADA EQUATION (assuming β_d = 0):                                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │         β_U = β_L / [1 + (1 - τ_c)(D/E)]                           │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │         β_L = β_U × [1 + (1 - τ_c)(D/E)]                           │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  WITH DEBT BETA (more accurate):                                            │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  β_U = (E/(E+D)) × β_L + (D/(E+D)) × β_D                           │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  β_L = β_U + (β_U - β_D) × (D/E)                                   │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  MILES-EZZELL (with tax adjustment for rebalancing):                        │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  β_L = β_U × [1 + D/E × (1 - τ_c × r_d/(1+r_d))]                   │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  PRACTICAL APPLICATION - COMPARABLE COMPANY ANALYSIS:                       │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────                       │
│  Step 1: Obtain βL for each comparable company                              │
│  Step 2: Unlever each: β_U = β_L / [1 + (1-τ)(D/E)]                        │
│  Step 3: Calculate average or median unlevered beta                         │
│  Step 4: Relever to target capital structure: β_L* = β_U × [1 + (1-τ)(D/E)*]│
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Complete WACC Example

```
COMPANY DATA:
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Shares outstanding:     100 million
  Current stock price:    $50
  Equity market value:    $5,000 million
  
  Debt (book/market):     $2,000 million
  Debt yield (YTM):       6%
  Corporate tax rate:     25%
  
  Risk-free rate:         4%
  Market risk premium:    6%
  Equity beta (βL):       1.3

CALCULATIONS:
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 1: Capital Structure Weights
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  V = E + D = $5,000 + $2,000 = $7,000 million
  
  E/V = $5,000 / $7,000 = 71.43%
  D/V = $2,000 / $7,000 = 28.57%

Step 2: Cost of Equity (CAPM)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rₑ = r_f + βL × (r_m - r_f)
  rₑ = 4% + 1.3 × 6%
  rₑ = 4% + 7.8% = 11.8%

Step 3: After-Tax Cost of Debt
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  r_d(1 - τ) = 6% × (1 - 0.25) = 4.5%

Step 4: WACC Calculation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WACC = (E/V) × rₑ + (D/V) × r_d × (1 - τ)
  WACC = (0.7143 × 11.8%) + (0.2857 × 4.5%)
  WACC = 8.43% + 1.29%
  
  ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │  WACC = 9.72%            │
  └──────────────────────────┘

Step 5: Unlevered Cost of Capital (for comparison)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  β_U = β_L / [1 + (1-τ)(D/E)]
  β_U = 1.3 / [1 + (0.75)(2,000/5,000)]
  β_U = 1.3 / 1.30 = 1.0
  
  r_U = 4% + 1.0 × 6% = 10%
  
  (Unlevered cost > WACC due to tax shield benefit of debt)
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

## 7. Optimal Capital Structure

### Determining Optimal Leverage

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    OPTIMAL LEVERAGE DETERMINATION                           │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  OPTIMALITY CONDITION:                                                      │
│  ═════════════════════                                                      │
│                                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  ∂V/∂D = 0                                                         │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  Marginal Tax Shield Benefit = Marginal Distress Cost              │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  │  τ_c = ∂PV(Distress Costs)/∂D                                      │   │
│  │                                                                     │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                             │
│  EQUIVALENT: Find D* that MINIMIZES WACC                                    │
│                                                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  VALUE FUNCTION (with distress):                                            │
│  ──────────────────────────────                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  V(D) = V_U + τ_c × D - p(D) × L × V(D)                                    │
│                                                                             │
│  Where:                                                                     │
│    p(D) = Probability of distress (increasing in D)                        │
│    L = Loss given distress (as % of value)                                 │
│                                                                             │
│  Solving: V(D) = (V_U + τ_c × D) / (1 + p(D) × L)                          │
│                                                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  PRACTICAL APPROACH - WACC MINIMIZATION:                                    │
│  ───────────────────────────────────────                                    │
│                                                                             │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Step 1: Estimate β_U from current capital structure                 │  │
│  │                                                                      │  │
│  │  Step 2: For each debt level D (or D/V ratio):                       │  │
│  │          a) Calculate implied credit rating                          │  │
│  │          b) Determine cost of debt (add spread to r_f)              │  │
│  │          c) Relever beta: β_L = β_U × [1 + (1-τ)(D/E)]             │  │
│  │          d) Calculate cost of equity: rₑ = r_f + β_L × MRP         │  │
│  │          e) Compute WACC                                             │  │
│  │                                                                      │  │
│  │  Step 3: Find D/V that minimizes WACC                                │  │
│  │                                                                      │  │
│  │  Step 4: Verify against industry benchmarks and constraints          │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 9. Adjusted Present Value (APV) Approach

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    ADJUSTED PRESENT VALUE (APV)                             │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                             │
│  APV separates value components:                                            │
│                                                                             │
│  ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ║  APV = V_U + PV(Tax Shield) - PV(Distress) + PV(Other Side Effects)  ║ │
│  ║                                                                       ║ │
│  ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ │
│                                                                             │
│  WHERE:                                                                     │
│  ═══════                                                                    │
│                                                                             │
│  V_U = Unlevered Firm Value (discount FCF at r_U)                          │
│                 T                                                           │
│      V_U = Σ  [FCF_t / (1 + r_U)^t] + TV_U / (1 + r_U)^T                  │
│            t=1                                                              │
│                                                                             │
│  PV(Tax Shield) = Value of interest tax deductibility                      │
│                 T                                                           │
│      PV(TS) = Σ  [τ_c × r_d × D_t / (1 + r_d)^t]                          │
│              t=1                                                            │
│                                                                             │
│  or if permanent debt: PV(TS) = τ_c × D                                    │
│                                                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  APV EXAMPLE:                                                               │
│  ════════════                                                               │
│                                                                             │
│  Given:                                                                     │
│    Expected perpetual FCF = $10 million                                     │
│    Unlevered cost of capital (r_U) = 12%                                   │
│    Debt = $30 million (permanent)                                           │
│    Cost of debt = 6%                                                        │
│    Tax rate = 25%                                                           │
│    Expected distress costs = $2 million                                     │
│    Probability of distress = 5%                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  Calculation:                                                               │
│  ────────────                                                               │
│    V_U = $10M / 0.12 = $83.33 million                                      │
│    PV(Tax Shield) = 0.25 × $30M = $7.5 million                             │
│    PV(Distress) = 0.05 × $2M / 0.12 = $0.83 million                        │
│                                                                             │
│    APV = $83.33 + $7.5 - $0.83 = $90.0 million                             │
│                                                                             │
│    Value of Equity = $90.0 - $30.0 = $60.0 million                         │
│                                                                             │
│                                                                             │
│  APV vs. WACC RECONCILIATION:                                               │
│  ────────────────────────────                                               │
│  If APV = FCF / WACC, then:                                                │
│                                                                             │
│    WACC = FCF / APV = $10M / $90M = 11.11%                                 │
│                                                                             │
│  This is lower than r_U (12%) due to tax shield benefit                    │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

```
║    rₑ = r_f + β × (r_m - r_f)                                              ║
║                                                                             ║
║  LEVERED BETA:                                                              ║
║    β_L = β_U × [1 + (1 - τ)(D/E)]                                          ║
║                                                                             ║
║  UNLEVERED BETA:                                                            ║
║    β_U = β_L / [1 + (1 - τ)(D/E)]                                          ║
║                                                                             ║
║  M&M WITH TAXES:                                                            ║
║    V_L = V_U + τ × D                                                        ║
║                                                                             ║
║  APV:                                                                       ║
║    APV = V_U + PV(Tax Shield) - PV(Distress Costs)                         ║
║                                                                             ║

║    PV(TS) = τ × D                                                           ║
║                                                                             ║
║  UNLEVERED COST OF CAPITAL:                                                 ║
║    r_U = (E/V) × rₑ + (D/V) × r_d        [Pre-tax WACC]                    ║
║                                                                             ║
║  COST OF EQUITY (M&M):                                                      ║
║    rₑ = r_U + (D/E)(1 - τ)(r_U - r_d)                                      ║
║                                                                             ║

║                                                                             ║
```

**2. The Consequences Are Real**
> Teams ship features customers don't use. They miss signals from churning accounts. They can't prove product's impact on revenue. The result? Wasted engineering resources, missed market opportunities, and executives questioning product investments.

**3. There's a Better Way**
> What if you could see all customer signals in one place, automatically prioritized by business impact? What if you could trace every product decision to revenue outcomes? What if product could finally prove its value to the business?

**4. We Make It Possible**
> Acme is the product intelligence platform that connects customer signals to business outcomes. We unify every source of customer feedback, apply AI to surface what matters, and track the revenue impact of every product decision.

**5. The Proof Is Real**
> Companies using Acme see 40% faster time-to-insight, 25% reduction in feature waste, and for the first time can prove product's contribution to revenue growth.

### Risk Response Plans

#### Risk 1: Product Delays

```
TRIGGER:    Product confirms launch feature won't be ready by T-4w
IMPACT:     Launch cannot proceed as planned

RESPONSE OPTIONS:
├── Option A: Delay launch (if <2 weeks)
│   └── Communicate to stakeholders, adjust all dates
├── Option B: Launch with reduced scope  
│   └── Define "minimum viable launch," ship now, add later
└── Option C: Pre-announce with "coming soon"
    └── Build anticipation, launch when ready

DECISION OWNER: VP Product + VP Marketing (joint)
ESCALATION: CMO if >2 week delay or major scope change
```

#### Risk 2: Competitive Pre-empt

```
TRIGGER:    Major competitor announces similar feature within 2 weeks of launch

RESPONSE OPTIONS:
├── Option A: Accelerate launch
│   └── Move to earlier date, compress timeline
├── Option B: Hold and differentiate
│   └── Delay 1-2 weeks, sharpen differentiation
└── Option C: Proceed with enhanced positioning
    └── Maintain date, add "why we're different" content

DECISION OWNER: PMM + VP Marketing
COMMUNICATIONS: Prepare competitive response talking points
```

#### Risk 3: Launch Day Issues

```
TRIGGER:    Critical failure on launch day (website down, major bug, etc.)

DAY-OF WAR ROOM:
├── PMM Lead (command)
├── Engineering (technical)
├── Comms (external messaging)  
├── Sales (customer-facing)
└── Customer Success (existing customers)

RESPONSE PROTOCOL:
1. Assess severity (0-15 min)
2. If critical: pause external communications
3. Communicate status to internal stakeholders
4. Prepare customer-facing messaging if needed
5. Fix forward or rollback decision
6. Resume launch when resolved

ESCALATION: CMO for any public-facing issues
```

## 1. Structure–Property Relationships

### 1.1 Molecular Architecture

The fundamental structure of polymers determines their macroscopic properties through several hierarchical levels:

**Chain Configuration and Conformation**

| Structural Feature | Description | Property Impact |
|-------------------|-------------|-----------------|
| Linear chains | Unbranched backbone | Higher crystallinity, better mechanical strength |
| Branched chains | Side chains off main backbone | Lower density, reduced crystallinity |
| Crosslinked | Covalent bonds between chains | Thermoset behavior, improved solvent resistance |
| Network | 3D interconnected structure | Elastomeric properties, no melting |

**Molecular Weight Relationships**

The molecular weight profoundly influences polymer properties:

$$\bar{M}_n = \frac{\sum N_i M_i}{\sum N_i}$$

$$\bar{M}_w = \frac{\sum N_i M_i^2}{\sum N_i M_i}$$

**Polydispersity Index (PDI or Đ):**
$$Đ = \frac{\bar{M}_w}{\bar{M}_n}$$

| Property | Low MW Effect | High MW Effect |
|----------|--------------|----------------|
| Tensile strength | Low | High (plateau above critical MW) |
| Melt viscosity | Low | High (η ∝ M^3.4 above Me) |
| Tg | Lower | Higher (approaches asymptote) |
| Solubility | Higher | Lower |
| Processability | Easier | More difficult |

### 1.2 Thermal Transitions

**Glass Transition Temperature (Tg)**

The Tg represents the transition from glassy to rubbery behavior:

$$T_g = T_{g,\infty} - \frac{K}{M_n}$$

Factors affecting Tg:
- **Chain stiffness**: Rigid backbones increase Tg
- **Side groups**: Bulky substituents increase Tg
- **Polarity**: Hydrogen bonding increases Tg
- **Plasticizers**: Decrease Tg
- **Crosslinking**: Generally increases Tg

**Fox Equation for Copolymers:**
$$\frac{1}{T_g} = \frac{w_1}{T_{g,1}} + \frac{w_2}{T_{g,2}}$$

### 1.3 Crystallinity

**Degree of Crystallinity:**
$$X_c = \frac{\rho_c(\rho - \rho_a)}{\rho(\rho_c - \rho_a)} \times 100\%$$

Or from DSC:
$$X_c = \frac{\Delta H_m}{\Delta H_m^0} \times 100\%$$

| Property | Amorphous | Semi-crystalline |
|----------|-----------|------------------|
| Optical clarity | Transparent | Often opaque |
| Modulus | Lower | Higher |
| Solvent resistance | Lower | Higher |
| Dimensional stability | Lower | Higher |
| Impact resistance | Often higher | Variable |

### 1.4 Tacticity

```
Isotactic:      R  R  R  R  R
                |  |  |  |  |
            ─C─C─C─C─C─C─C─C─C─C─
                |  |  |  |  |

                |  |  |  |  |

                |  |  |  |  |

```

## 2. Processing Methods

### 2.1 Melt Processing

**Extrusion**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Hopper    Feed Zone    Compression    Metering     │
│    ↓           │            Zone         Zone       │
│   ███         ═══════════════════════════════→ Die  │
│               ↑ Barrel with heaters                 │
│           Rotating screw                            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key Parameters:**
- Barrel temperature profile
- Screw speed (RPM)
- Screw geometry (L/D ratio, compression ratio)
- Die design and temperature
- Residence time

**Injection Molding**

| Stage | Parameters | Considerations |
|-------|------------|----------------|
| Plasticization | Barrel temp, back pressure | Material degradation, homogeneity |
| Injection | Injection speed, pressure | Shear heating, fill pattern |
| Packing | Holding pressure, time | Shrinkage compensation |
| Cooling | Mold temperature, time | Crystallinity, warpage |
| Ejection | Ejection speed, force | Part damage, cycle time |

### 2.2 Other Processing Methods

**Blow Molding (for hollow parts)**
- Extrusion blow molding
- Injection blow molding
- Stretch blow molding

**Thermoforming**
- Vacuum forming
- Pressure forming
- Twin-sheet forming

**Compression Molding**
- Primarily for thermosets
- Lower residual stress
- Suitable for large parts

### 2.3 Solution Processing

**Spin Coating:**
$$h = k\omega^{-1/2}\eta^{1/3}$$

Where:
- h = film thickness
- ω = angular velocity
- η = solution viscosity
- k = constant

**Electrospinning (for nanofibers):**
- Applied voltage: 10-30 kV
- Feed rate: 0.1-5 mL/h
- Tip-to-collector distance: 10-25 cm
- Solution concentration: affects fiber morphology

### 2.4 Additive Manufacturing

| Technology | Mechanism | Polymers Used |
|------------|-----------|---------------|
| FDM/FFF | Melt extrusion | ABS, PLA, PETG, Nylon |
| SLA | Photopolymerization | Acrylates, epoxies |
| SLS | Powder sintering | PA12, TPU, PEEK |
| MJF | Powder + binding agent | PA12, PA11, TPU |

## 3. Characterization Techniques

### 3.1 Molecular Weight Determination

**Gel Permeation Chromatography (GPC/SEC)**

```
Sample → Columns (porous beads) → Detectors → Analysis
              ↓
        Size separation
        (large molecules elute first)
```

*Experimental Considerations:*
- Column selection (pore size distribution)
- Mobile phase compatibility
- Calibration standards (narrow PDI)
- Detector type (RI, UV, light scattering, viscometer)
- Sample concentration (0.1-0.5 wt%)
- Flow rate (typically 1 mL/min)
- Column temperature control

**Intrinsic Viscosity:**
$$[\eta] = \lim_{c \to 0} \frac{\eta_{sp}}{c} = KM_v^a$$

(Mark-Houwink-Sakurada equation)

### 3.2 Thermal Analysis

**Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC)**

Measures heat flow vs. temperature:
- Glass transition (Tg)
- Melting temperature (Tm)
- Crystallization temperature (Tc)
- Heat of fusion (ΔHm)
- Cure behavior

*Experimental Protocol:*
1. Sample mass: 5-15 mg
2. Standard heating rate: 10°C/min
3. First heat: erase thermal history
4. Controlled cooling
5. Second heat: reproducible data

**Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA)**

Measures mass loss vs. temperature:
- Decomposition temperature
- Composition analysis
- Moisture/volatile content
- Filler content

*Key Parameters:*
- Heating rate: 10-20°C/min typical
- Atmosphere: N₂ (pyrolysis) or air (oxidative)
- Sample mass: 5-20 mg

**Dynamic Mechanical Analysis (DMA)**

Measures viscoelastic properties:

$$E^* = E' + iE''$$

$$\tan \delta = \frac{E''}{E'}$$

| Mode | Applications |
|------|-------------|
| Single cantilever | Films, bars |
| Dual cantilever | Rigid samples |
| 3-point bending | Stiff composites |
| Tension | Films, fibers |
| Shear | Soft materials, gels |

### 3.3 Spectroscopic Methods

**FTIR Spectroscopy**

| Wavenumber (cm⁻¹) | Assignment |
|-------------------|------------|
| 3200-3600 | O-H, N-H stretch |
| 2850-3000 | C-H stretch |
| 1650-1750 | C=O stretch |
| 1600-1680 | C=C stretch |
| 1000-1300 | C-O stretch |
| 600-900 | C-H out-of-plane bend |

*Experimental Considerations:*
- ATR correction for penetration depth
- Baseline correction
- Atmospheric compensation (CO₂, H₂O)
- Sample preparation (KBr pellet, film, ATR)

**NMR Spectroscopy**

- ¹H NMR: End-group analysis, tacticity, copolymer composition
- ¹³C NMR: Detailed microstructure, branch points
- 2D NMR: Complex structural assignments

*Sample Preparation:*
- Concentration: 5-20 mg/mL
- Solvent selection: deuterated, good solubility
- Relaxation delay: sufficient for quantitative analysis

### 3.4 Microscopy

**Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM)**

Applications:
- Fracture surface morphology
- Fiber/filler dispersion
- Surface topography
- Phase separation

*Sample Preparation:*
- Conductive coating (Au, Pt, C) for non-conductive samples
- Cryo-fracture for clean cross-sections
- Proper mounting and grounding

**Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM)**

Modes and applications:
- Tapping mode: topography, phase imaging
- Contact mode: friction studies
- Force spectroscopy: mechanical properties

### 3.5 Mechanical Testing

**Tensile Testing (ASTM D638, ISO 527)**

```
Stress-Strain Curve:
       ↑ Stress (σ)
       │         ╭─────────── Yield point
       │        ╱  ╲
       │       ╱    ╲___________
       │      ╱                 ╲ Failure
       │     ╱                    
       │    ╱  Elastic region
       │   ╱   (E = σ/ε)
       └──╱─────────────────────→ Strain (ε)
```

**Key Properties:**
- Young's modulus (E)
- Yield strength (σy)
- Ultimate tensile strength (UTS)
- Elongation at break (εb)
- Toughness (area under curve)

*Testing Considerations:*
- Strain rate effects (polymers are viscoelastic)
- Temperature control
- Sample conditioning (humidity, time)
- Grip design (prevent slippage, stress concentration)

**Impact Testing:**
- Izod (notched/unnotched): ASTM D256
- Charpy: ASTM D6110
- Drop weight impact: ASTM D3763

## 4. Polymer Degradation

### 4.1 Degradation Mechanisms

**Thermal Degradation**

Mechanisms:
1. Random chain scission
2. End-chain scission (depolymerization)
3. Chain stripping (side group elimination)
4. Crosslinking

*Kinetic Analysis:*
$$\frac{d\alpha}{dt} = k(T)f(\alpha)$$

$$k(T) = A\exp\left(-\frac{E_a}{RT}\right)$$

Common methods:
- Kissinger method
- Flynn-Wall-Ozawa method
- Friedman isoconversional method

**Photo-oxidative Degradation**

```
Initiation:   RH + hν → R• + H•

Propagation:  R• + O₂ → ROO•
              ROO• + RH → ROOH + R•

Branching:    ROOH → RO• + •OH

Termination:  R• + R• → R-R
              ROO• + ROO• → products
```

**Hydrolytic Degradation**

Susceptible linkages:
- Esters (PLA, PET, PCL)
- Amides (Nylon)
- Urethanes (PU)
- Anhydrides

*Rate depends on:*
- pH
- Temperature
- Water accessibility
- Crystallinity

### 4.2 Stabilization Strategies

| Stabilizer Type | Mechanism | Examples |
|-----------------|-----------|----------|
| UV absorbers | Absorb UV light | Benzotriazoles, benzophenones |
| HALS | Radical scavengers | Hindered amines |
| Antioxidants (primary) | Radical chain breakers | Hindered phenols |
| Antioxidants (secondary) | Peroxide decomposers | Phosphites, thioesters |
| Thermal stabilizers | Various | Metal stearates (for PVC) |

### 4.3 Accelerated Aging Studies

**Common Test Methods:**

| Test | Conditions | Standards |
|------|------------|-----------|
| Heat aging | Elevated temperature | ASTM D3045 |
| UV weathering | UV-A/UV-B, humidity cycles | ASTM G154 |
| Xenon arc | Full spectrum, water spray | ASTM G155 |
| Hydrolysis | Elevated temp/humidity | ASTM D3137 |
| Ozone exposure | Elevated ozone concentration | ASTM D1149 |

*Correlation Challenges:*
- Activation energy may change
- Multiple degradation pathways
- Synergistic effects
- Dose-rate effects

## 6. Experimental Considerations

### 6.1 Sample Preparation Best Practices

**General Guidelines:**
1. Document material source, lot number, storage conditions
2. Pre-dry hygroscopic materials (verify moisture content)
3. Use consistent thermal history protocols
4. Ensure representative sampling
5. Consider anisotropy from processing

**Pre-Drying Recommendations:**

| Material | Temperature (°C) | Time (h) | Target Moisture |
|----------|------------------|----------|-----------------|
| Nylon 6 | 80-90 | 4-16 | <0.2% |
| PET | 120-150 | 4-6 | <0.02% |
| PC | 120 | 4 | <0.02% |
| PEEK | 150 | 3 | <0.1% |
| PLA | 50-60 | 4-8 | <0.025% |

### 6.2 Statistical Considerations

**Minimum Replicates:**
- Tensile testing: n ≥ 5
- Impact testing: n ≥ 10
- Thermal analysis: n ≥ 3
- GPC: n ≥ 2 with multiple injections

**Data Reporting:**
- Report mean, standard deviation
- Note outliers and basis for exclusion
- Include test conditions
- Reference applicable standards

### 6.3 Common Pitfalls and Solutions

| Issue | Potential Cause | Solution |
|-------|-----------------|----------|
| Variable Tg values | Moisture, thermal history | Pre-dry, use second heat |
| MW inconsistency | Column degradation, calibration | Regular calibration, maintenance |
| Mechanical scatter | Poor sample prep, alignment | Improved specimens, grip check |
| Unexpected degradation | Moisture, contamination | Proper storage, handling |
| Processing defects | Wrong parameters | Process optimization, DOE |

### 6.4 Safety Considerations

**Processing Hazards:**
- Thermal burns
- Mechanical entrapment
- Fumes and volatiles
- High pressure exposure

**Material-Specific:**
- PVC: HCl evolution at high temperatures
- Fluoropolymers: toxic fumes above 400°C
- Acrylic resins: monomer toxicity
- Nanofillers: inhalation hazards

```nginx
# nginx.conf - Optimized for Crawler Performance

    listen 443 ssl http2;
```

### Server Response Time Monitoring

```python
# server_performance_monitor.py
import time
import requests
import statistics
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Dict
from datetime import datetime
import logging
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

@dataclass
class PerformanceMetrics:
    url: str
    ttfb: float  # Time to First Byte
    total_time: float
    status_code: int
    content_size: int
    timestamp: datetime
    
class CrawlPerformanceMonitor:
    """Monitor server performance from crawler's perspective."""
    
    # Simulate different crawler user agents
    CRAWLER_USER_AGENTS = {
        'googlebot': 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)',
        'googlebot_mobile': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 6.0.1; Nexus 5X Build/MMB29P) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/W.X.Y.Z Mobile Safari/537.36 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1; +http://www.google.com/bot.html)',
        'bingbot': 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; bingbot/2.0; +http://www.bing.com/bingbot.htm)',
    }
    
    def __init__(self, domain: str):
        self.domain = domain
        self.metrics_history: List[PerformanceMetrics] = []
        self.logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        
    def measure_url(self, url: str, user_agent: str = 'googlebot') -> PerformanceMetrics:
        """Measure performance metrics for a single URL."""
        headers = {
            'User-Agent': self.CRAWLER_USER_AGENTS.get(user_agent, user_agent),
            'Accept': 'text/html,application/xhtml+xml',
            'Accept-Encoding': 'gzip, deflate, br',
        }
        
        try:
            start_time = time.time()
            response = requests.get(
                url, 
                headers=headers, 
                timeout=30,
                allow_redirects=True
            )
            total_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Calculate TTFB from response elapsed
            ttfb = response.elapsed.total_seconds()
            
            metrics = PerformanceMetrics(
                url=url,
                ttfb=ttfb,
                total_time=total_time,
                status_code=response.status_code,
                content_size=len(response.content),
                timestamp=datetime.now()
            )
            
            self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
            return metrics
            
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            self.logger.error(f"Error measuring {url}: {e}")
            return None
    
    def benchmark_urls(self, urls: List[str], concurrent: int = 5) -> Dict:
        """Benchmark multiple URLs concurrently."""
        results = {
            'successful': [],
            'failed': [],
            'summary': {}
        }
        
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=concurrent) as executor:
            future_to_url = {
                executor.submit(self.measure_url, url): url 
                for url in urls
            }
            
            for future in as_completed(future_to_url):
                url = future_to_url[future]
                try:
                    metrics = future.result()
                    if metrics and metrics.status_code == 200:
                        results['successful'].append(metrics)
                    else:
                        results['failed'].append((url, metrics))
                except Exception as e:
                    results['failed'].append((url, str(e)))
        
        # Calculate summary statistics
        if results['successful']:
            ttfb_values = [m.ttfb for m in results['successful']]
            total_times = [m.total_time for m in results['successful']]
            
            results['summary'] = {
                'total_urls': len(urls),
                'successful': len(results['successful']),
                'failed': len(results['failed']),
                'ttfb': {
                    'mean': statistics.mean(ttfb_values),
                    'median': statistics.median(ttfb_values),
                    'p95': sorted(ttfb_values)[int(len(ttfb_values) * 0.95)] if len(ttfb_values) > 1 else ttfb_values[0],
                    'max': max(ttfb_values)
                },
                'total_time': {
                    'mean': statistics.mean(total_times),
                    'median': statistics.median(total_times),
                    'p95': sorted(total_times)[int(len(total_times) * 0.95)] if len(total_times) > 1 else total_times[0],
                    'max': max(total_times)
                }
            }
        
        return results
    
    def identify_slow_pages(self, threshold_seconds: float = 2.0) -> List[PerformanceMetrics]:
        """Identify pages that are too slow for optimal crawling."""
        return [
            m for m in self.metrics_history 
            if m.ttfb > threshold_seconds
        ]
    
    def generate_performance_report(self) -> str:
        """Generate a comprehensive performance report."""
        if not self.metrics_history:
            return "No metrics collected yet."
        
        report = []
        report.append("=" * 60)
        report.append("CRAWL PERFORMANCE REPORT")
        report.append("=" * 60)
        
        # Overall statistics
        ttfb_values = [m.ttfb for m in self.metrics_history]
        report.append(f"\nTotal URLs analyzed: {len(self.metrics_history)}")
        report.append(f"\nTTFB Statistics:")
        report.append(f"  Mean: {statistics.mean(ttfb_values):.3f}s")
        report.append(f"  Median: {statistics.median(ttfb_values):.3f}s")
        report.append(f"  Max: {max(ttfb_values):.3f}s")
        
        # Performance grades
        fast = sum(1 for t in ttfb_values if t < 0.5)
        acceptable = sum(1 for t in ttfb_values if 0.5 <= t < 1.0)
        slow = sum(1 for t in ttfb_values if 1.0 <= t < 2.0)
        very_slow = sum(1 for t in ttfb_values if t >= 2.0)
        
        report.append(f"\nPerformance Distribution:")
        report.append(f"  Fast (<0.5s): {fast} ({fast/len(ttfb_values)*100:.1f}%)")
        report.append(f"  Acceptable (0.5-1s): {acceptable} ({acceptable/len(ttfb_values)*100:.1f}%)")
        report.append(f"  Slow (1-2s): {slow} ({slow/len(ttfb_values)*100:.1f}%)")
        report.append(f"  Very Slow (>2s): {very_slow} ({very_slow/len(ttfb_values)*100:.1f}%)")
        
        # Recommendations
        report.append(f"\nRecommendations:")
        if very_slow > 0:
            report.append("  ⚠️  Address very slow pages immediately - they waste crawl budget")
        if statistics.mean(ttfb_values) > 1.0:
            report.append("  ⚠️  Average TTFB too high - consider server optimization")
        if max(ttfb_values) > 5.0:
            report.append("  ⚠️  Some pages may be timing out for crawlers")
        
        return "\n".join(report)


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    monitor = CrawlPerformanceMonitor("example.com")
    
    # Sample URLs to test
    test_urls = [
        "https://example.com/",
        "https://example.com/products",
        "https://example.com/category/electronics",
        "https://example.com/product/12345",
    ]
    
    results = monitor.benchmark_urls(test_urls)
    print(monitor.generate_performance_report())
```

```python
# robots_txt_generator.py
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
import re

class CrawlerType(Enum):
    ALL = "*"
    GOOGLEBOT = "Googlebot"
    GOOGLEBOT_IMAGE = "Googlebot-Image"
    GOOGLEBOT_NEWS = "Googlebot-News"
    BINGBOT = "Bingbot"
    YANDEXBOT = "Yandexbot"
    DUCKDUCKBOT = "DuckDuckBot"

@dataclass
class RobotsRule:
    path: str
    allow: bool = False
    comment: Optional[str] = None

@dataclass
class CrawlerDirectives:
    crawler: CrawlerType
    rules: List[RobotsRule] = field(default_factory=list)
    crawl_delay: Optional[float] = None
    
class RobotsTxtGenerator:
    """Generate optimized robots.txt files."""
    
    def __init__(self, domain: str):
        self.domain = domain
        self.directives: Dict[CrawlerType, CrawlerDirectives] = {}
        self.sitemaps: List[str] = []
        
    def add_rule(self, crawler: CrawlerType, path: str, 
                 allow: bool = False, comment: str = None):
        """Add a rule for a specific crawler."""
        if crawler not in self.directives:
            self.directives[crawler] = CrawlerDirectives(crawler=crawler)
        
        self.directives[crawler].rules.append(
            RobotsRule(path=path, allow=allow, comment=comment)
        )
        return self
    
    def set_crawl_delay(self, crawler: CrawlerType, delay: float):
        """Set crawl delay for a specific crawler."""
        if crawler not in self.directives:
            self.directives[crawler] = CrawlerDirectives(crawler=crawler)
        self.directives[crawler].crawl_delay = delay
        return self
    
    def add_sitemap(self, sitemap_url: str):
        """Add a sitemap URL."""
        self.sitemaps.append(sitemap_url)
        return self
    
    def add_common_disallows(self):
        """Add common disallow patterns for crawl budget optimization."""
        common_patterns = [
            # Search and filter parameters
            ("/search", "Block internal search results"),
            ("/*?*sort=", "Block sorting parameters"),
            ("/*?*filter=", "Block filter parameters"),
            ("/*?*page=", "Block pagination parameters (use rel prev/next)"),
            ("/*?*session=", "Block session parameters"),
            ("/*?*tracking=", "Block tracking parameters"),
            ("/*?*ref=", "Block referral parameters"),
            ("/*?*utm_", "Block UTM parameters"),
            
            # Faceted navigation
            ("/*?*color=", "Block color facets"),
            ("/*?*size=", "Block size facets"),
            ("/*?*price=", "Block price facets"),
            ("/*?*brand=", "Block brand facets (combine multiple)"),
            
            # User-specific pages
            ("/cart", "Block cart pages"),
            ("/checkout", "Block checkout pages"),
            ("/account", "Block account pages"),
            ("/wishlist", "Block wishlist pages"),
            ("/compare", "Block product comparison"),
            
            # Admin and system
            ("/admin", "Block admin area"),
            ("/wp-admin", "Block WordPress admin"),
            ("/api/", "Block API endpoints"),
            ("/ajax/", "Block AJAX endpoints"),
            ("/*.json$", "Block JSON files"),
            
            # Thin content
            ("/tag/", "Block tag pages (if thin content)"),
            ("/author/", "Block author archives"),
            ("/print/", "Block print versions"),
            ("/pdf/", "Block PDF generation"),
            
            # Duplicates
            ("/*?*replytocom=", "Block comment reply URLs"),
            ("/*?*preview=", "Block preview URLs"),
        ]
        
        for path, comment in common_patterns:
            self.add_rule(CrawlerType.ALL, path, allow=False, comment=comment)
        
        return self
    
    def add_important_allows(self):
        """Explicitly allow important resources."""
        allow_patterns = [
            ("/*.css", "Allow CSS files"),
            ("/*.js", "Allow JavaScript files"),
            ("/*.jpg", "Allow JPEG images"),
            ("/*.jpeg", "Allow JPEG images"),
            ("/*.png", "Allow PNG images"),
            ("/*.gif", "Allow GIF images"),
            ("/*.webp", "Allow WebP images"),
            ("/*.svg", "Allow SVG images"),
            ("/*.woff", "Allow Web fonts"),
            ("/*.woff2", "Allow Web fonts"),
        ]
        
        for path, comment in allow_patterns:
            self.add_rule(CrawlerType.ALL, path, allow=True, comment=comment)
        
        return self
    
    def generate(self) -> str:
        """Generate the complete robots.txt content."""
        lines = []
        lines.append(f"# Robots.txt for {self.domain}")
        lines.append(f"# Generated by Crawl Budget Optimizer")
        lines.append("")
        
        # Process each crawler's directives
        for crawler, directives in self.directives.items():
            lines.append(f"User-agent: {crawler.value}")
            
            # Sort rules: allows first, then disallows
            sorted_rules = sorted(
                directives.rules, 
                key=lambda r: (not r.allow, r.path)
            )
            
            for rule in sorted_rules:
                prefix = "Allow" if rule.allow else "Disallow"
                if rule.comment:
                    lines.append(f"# {rule.comment}")
                lines.append(f"{prefix}: {rule.path}")
            
            if directives.crawl_delay:
                lines.append(f"Crawl-delay: {directives.crawl_delay}")
            
            lines.append("")
        
        # Add sitemaps
        if self.sitemaps:
            lines.append("# Sitemaps")
            for sitemap in self.sitemaps:
                lines.append(f"Sitemap: {sitemap}")
        
        return "\n".join(lines)
```

```python
# sitemap_generator.py
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from xml.dom import minidom
from typing import List, Optional, Generator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from enum import Enum
import gzip
import os

class ChangeFrequency(Enum):
    ALWAYS = "always"
    HOURLY = "hourly"
    DAILY = "daily"
    WEEKLY = "weekly"
    MONTHLY = "monthly"
    YEARLY = "yearly"
    NEVER = "never"

@dataclass
class SitemapURL:
    loc: str
    lastmod: Optional[datetime] = None
    changefreq: Optional[ChangeFrequency] = None
    priority: Optional[float] = None
    images: Optional[List[dict]] = None
    videos: Optional[List[dict]] = None
    news: Optional[dict] = None

class SitemapGenerator:
    """Generate optimized XML sitemaps with prioritization."""
    
    SITEMAP_NAMESPACE = "http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9"
    IMAGE_NAMESPACE = "http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-image/1.1"
    VIDEO_NAMESPACE = "http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-video/1.1"
    NEWS_NAMESPACE = "http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-news/0.9"
    
    MAX_URLS_PER_SITEMAP = 50000
    MAX_SIZE_BYTES = 50 * 1024 * 1024  # 50MB uncompressed
    
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, output_dir: str = "./sitemaps"):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip('/')
        self.output_dir = output_dir
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        
    def _create_sitemap_element(self) -> ET.Element:
        """Create the root urlset element with namespaces."""
        urlset = ET.Element("urlset")
        urlset.set("xmlns", self.SITEMAP_NAMESPACE)
        urlset.set("xmlns:image", self.IMAGE_NAMESPACE)
        urlset.set("xmlns:video", self.VIDEO_NAMESPACE)
        urlset.set("xmlns:news", self.NEWS_NAMESPACE)
        return urlset
    
    def _add_url_element(self, urlset: ET.Element, url: SitemapURL):
        """Add a URL element to the urlset."""
        url_element = ET.SubElement(urlset, "url")
        
        # Required: loc
        loc = ET.SubElement(url_element, "loc")
        loc.text = url.loc
        
        # Optional: lastmod
        if url.lastmod:
            lastmod = ET.SubElement(url_element, "lastmod")
            lastmod.text = url.lastmod.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00")
        
        # Optional: changefreq
        if url.changefreq:
            changefreq = ET.SubElement(url_element, "changefreq")
            changefreq.text = url.changefreq.value
        
        # Optional: priority
        if url.priority is not None:
            priority = ET.SubElement(url_element, "priority")
            priority.text = f"{url.priority:.1f}"
        
        # Images
        if url.images:
            for img in url.images[:1000]:  # Max 1000 images per page
                image = ET.SubElement(url_element, "image:image")
                img_loc = ET.SubElement(image, "image:loc")
                img_loc.text = img.get('loc', '')
                
                if img.get('title'):
                    img_title = ET.SubElement(image, "image:title")
                    img_title.text = img['title']
                
                if img.get('caption'):
                    img_caption = ET.SubElement(image, "image:caption")
                    img_caption.text = img['caption']
        
        # Videos
        if url.videos:
            for vid in url.videos:
                video = ET.SubElement(url_element, "video:video")
                
                for field in ['thumbnail_loc', 'title', 'description', 
                             'content_loc', 'duration', 'publication_date']:
                    if vid.get(field):
                        elem = ET.SubElement(video, f"video:{field}")
                        elem.text = str(vid[field])
    
    def _prettify(self, elem: ET.Element) -> str:
        """Return a pretty-printed XML string."""
        rough_string = ET.tostring(elem, encoding='unicode')
        reparsed = minidom.parseString(rough_string)
        return reparsed.toprettyxml(indent="  ")
    
    def generate_sitemap(self, urls: List[SitemapURL], filename: str) -> str:
        """Generate a single sitemap file."""
        urlset = self._create_sitemap_element()
        
        for url in urls[:self.MAX_URLS_PER_SITEMAP]:
            self._add_url_element(urlset, url)
        
        xml_content = self._prettify(urlset)
        
        # Save regular XML
        xml_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{filename}.xml")
        with open(xml_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(xml_content)
        
        # Save gzipped version
        gz_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{filename}.xml.gz")
        with gzip.open(gz_path, 'wt', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(xml_content)
        
        return xml_path
    
    def generate_sitemap_index(self, sitemap_files: List[str]) -> str:
        """Generate a sitemap index file."""
        sitemapindex = ET.Element("sitemapindex")
        sitemapindex.set("xmlns", self.SITEMAP_NAMESPACE)
        
        for sitemap_file in sitemap_files:
            sitemap = ET.SubElement(sitemapindex, "sitemap")
            
            loc = ET.SubElement(sitemap, "loc")
            loc.text = f"{self.base_url}/{sitemap_file}"
            
            lastmod = ET.SubElement(sitemap, "lastmod")
            lastmod.text = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00")
        
        xml_content = self._prettify(sitemapindex)
        
        index_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "sitemap-index.xml")
        with open(index_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(xml_content)
        
        return index_path


class PrioritizedSitemapGenerator(SitemapGenerator):
    """Generate sitemaps with intelligent prioritization."""
    
    def __init__(self, base_url: str, output_dir: str = "./sitemaps"):
        super().__init__(base_url, output_dir)
        self.priority_rules = []
        
    def add_priority_rule(self, pattern: str, priority: float, 
                         changefreq: ChangeFrequency):
        """Add a rule for URL prioritization."""
        self.priority_rules.append({
            'pattern': pattern,
            'priority': priority,
            'changefreq': changefreq
        })
    
    def calculate_priority(self, url: str) -> tuple:
        """Calculate priority and changefreq based on rules."""
        import re
        
        for rule in self.priority_rules:
            if re.match(rule['pattern'], url):
                return rule['priority'], rule['changefreq']
        
        # Default priority based on URL depth
        depth = url.count('/') - 3  # Subtract protocol slashes
        priority = max(0.1, 1.0 - (depth * 0.1))
        return priority, ChangeFrequency.WEEKLY
    
    def generate_prioritized_sitemaps(self, urls: List[str], 
                                       page_data: dict = None) -> List[str]:
        """Generate sitemaps with URLs sorted by priority."""
        
        sitemap_urls = []
        
        for url in urls:
            priority, changefreq = self.calculate_priority(url)
            
            # Get additional data if provided
            lastmod = None
            images = None
            if page_data and url in page_data:
                lastmod = page_data[url].get('lastmod')
                images = page_data[url].get('images')
            
            sitemap_urls.append(SitemapURL(
                loc=url,
                lastmod=lastmod,
                priority=priority,
                changefreq=changefreq,
                images=images
            ))
        
        # Sort by priority (highest first)
        sitemap_urls.sort(key=lambda x: x.priority or 0.5, reverse=True)
        
        # Split into chunks
        generated_files = []
        chunk_size = self.MAX_URLS_PER_SITEMAP
        
        for i in range(0, len(sitemap_urls), chunk_size):
            chunk = sitemap_urls[i:i + chunk_size]
            filename = f"sitemap-{i // chunk_size + 1}"
            self.generate_sitemap(chunk, filename)
            generated_files.append(f"{filename}.xml")
        
        # Generate index
        self.generate_sitemap_index(generated_files)
        
        return generated_files


# Example: E-commerce sitemap generation
def generate_ecommerce_sitemaps():
    """Generate sitemaps for an e-commerce site."""
    generator = PrioritizedSitemapGenerator(
        "https://store.example.com",
        "./sitemaps"
    )
    
    # Define priority rules
    generator.add_priority_rule(
        r"^https://store\.example\.com/$",
        priority=1.0,
        changefreq=ChangeFrequency.DAILY
    )
    
    generator.add_priority_rule(
        r"^https://store\.example\.com/category/[^/]+/$",
        priority=0.9,
        changefreq=ChangeFrequency.DAILY
    )
    
    generator.add_priority_rule(
        r"^https://store\.example\.com/product/[^/]+$",
        priority=0.8,
        changefreq=ChangeFrequency.WEEKLY
    )
    
    generator.add_priority_rule(
        r"^https://store\.example\.com/brand/[^/]+/$",
        priority=0.7,
        changefreq=ChangeFrequency.WEEKLY
    )
    
    generator.add_priority_rule(
        r"^https://store\.example\.com/blog/.*",
        priority=0.6,
        changefreq=ChangeFrequency.MONTHLY
    )
    
    # Sample URLs
    urls = [
        "https://store.example.com/",
        "https://store.example.com/category/electronics/",
        "https://store.example.com/category/clothing/",
        "https://store.example.com/product/laptop-pro-15",
        "https://store.example.com/product/wireless-headphones",
        "https://store.example.com/brand/apple/",
        "https://store.example.com/blog/buying-guide-2024",
    ]
    
    # Page data with lastmod and images
    page_data = {
        "https://store.example.com/product/laptop-pro-15": {
            "lastmod": datetime.now() - timedelta(days=2),
            "images": [
                {"loc": "https://store.example.com/images/laptop-1.jpg", "title": "Laptop Front View"},
                {"loc": "https://store.example.com/images/laptop-2.jpg", "title": "Laptop Side View"},
            ]
        }
    }
    
    files = generator.generate_prioritized_sitemaps(urls, page_data)
    print(f"Generated sitemaps: {files}")
```
