### GitLab CI/CD Pipeline with Environments

```yaml
# .gitlab-ci.yml
stages:
  - build
  - test
  - security
  - package
  - deploy-dev
  - deploy-staging
  - deploy-uat
  - deploy-prod

variables:
  DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR: "/certs"
  IMAGE_NAME: $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE
  KUBERNETES_VERSION: "1.28"

# ==============================================================================
# TEMPLATES
# ==============================================================================
.docker-build:
  image: docker:24-dind
  services:
    - docker:24-dind
  before_script:
    - docker login -u $CI_REGISTRY_USER -p $CI_REGISTRY_PASSWORD $CI_REGISTRY

.deploy-template:
  image: 
    name: bitnami/kubectl:$KUBERNETES_VERSION
    entrypoint: [""]
  before_script:
    - mkdir -p ~/.kube
    - echo "$KUBECONFIG" | base64 -d > ~/.kube/config
    - kubectl cluster-info

# ==============================================================================
# BUILD STAGE
# ==============================================================================
build:
  stage: build
  extends: .docker-build
  script:
    - VERSION=${CI_COMMIT_TAG:-$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA}
    - |
      docker build \
        --build-arg VERSION=$VERSION \
        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT=$CI_COMMIT_SHA \
        --build-arg BUILD_TIME=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
        --cache-from $IMAGE_NAME:latest \
        -t $IMAGE_NAME:$CI_COMMIT_SHA \
        -t $IMAGE_NAME:$VERSION \
        .
    - docker push $IMAGE_NAME:$CI_COMMIT_SHA
    - docker push $IMAGE_NAME:$VERSION
    - |
      if [ "$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH" == "main" ]; then
        docker tag $IMAGE_NAME:$CI_COMMIT_SHA $IMAGE_NAME:latest
        docker push $IMAGE_NAME:latest
      fi
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG

# ==============================================================================
# TEST STAGE
# ==============================================================================
unit-tests:
  stage: test
  image: golang:1.21
  script:
    - go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
    - go tool cover -func=coverage.out
  coverage: '/total:\s+\(statements\)\s+(\d+.\d+)%/'
  artifacts:
    reports:
      coverage_report:
        coverage_format: cobertura
        path: coverage.xml
    paths:
      - coverage.out
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH

integration-tests:
  stage: test
  image: golang:1.21
  services:
    - name: postgres:15
      alias: postgres
    - name: redis:7
      alias: redis
  variables:
    POSTGRES_DB: testdb
    POSTGRES_USER: test
    POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
    DATABASE_URL: "postgres://test:test@postgres:5432/testdb?sslmode=disable"
    REDIS_URL: "redis://redis:6379"
  script:
    - go test -v -tags=integration -timeout=15m ./tests/integration/...
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH =~ /^(main|develop|release\/.*)$/

# ==============================================================================
# SECURITY STAGE
# ==============================================================================
sast:
  stage: security
  image: returntocorp/semgrep
  script:
    - semgrep scan --config auto --sarif -o semgrep.sarif .
  artifacts:
    reports:
      sast: semgrep.sarif
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH

container-scan:
  stage: security
  image:
    name: aquasec/trivy:latest
    entrypoint: [""]
  script:
    - trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity HIGH,CRITICAL $IMAGE_NAME:$CI_COMMIT_SHA
  dependencies:
    - build
  rules:
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH

dependency-scan:
  stage: security
  image: golang:1.21
  script:
```

### Argo Rollouts Configuration

```yaml
# deploy/k8s/rollout.yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: ghcr.io/org/app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/live
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
          env:
            - name: VERSION
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: metadata.labels['app.kubernetes.io/version']
  strategy:
    canary:
      # Canary steps
      steps:
        - setWeight: 5
        - pause: { duration: 5m }
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: success-rate
            args:
              - name: service-name
                value: app
        - setWeight: 25
        - pause: { duration: 5m }
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: success-rate
        - setWeight: 50
        - pause: { duration: 10m }
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: success-rate
              - templateName: latency
        - setWeight: 75
        - pause: { duration: 10m }
        - setWeight: 100
      
      # Traffic routing
      canaryService: app-canary
      stableService: app-stable
      trafficRouting:
        istio:
          virtualServices:
            - name: app-vsvc
              routes:
                - primary
        # Alternative: nginx
        # nginx:
        #   stableIngress: app-stable-ingress
        #   additionalIngressAnnotations:
        #     canary-by-header: X-Canary
      
      # Anti-affinity for canary pods
      antiAffinity:
        preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          weight: 100
      
      # Automatic rollback on failure
      autoPromotionEnabled: false
      scaleDownDelaySeconds: 30
      
      # Analysis configuration
      analysis:
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        unsuccessfulRunHistoryLimit: 3

---
# Analysis Template - Success Rate
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: success-rate
  namespace: production
spec:
  args:
    - name: service-name
  metrics:
    - name: success-rate
      interval: 1m
      count: 5
      successCondition: result[0] >= 0.99
      failureCondition: result[0] < 0.95
      failureLimit: 2
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{
              service="{{args.service-name}}",
              status!~"5.."
            }[5m])) 
            / 
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{
              service="{{args.service-name}}"
            }[5m]))

---
# Analysis Template - Latency
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: latency
  namespace: production
spec:
  metrics:
    - name: latency-p99
      interval: 1m
      count: 5
      successCondition: result[0] <= 500
      failureCondition: result[0] > 1000
      failureLimit: 2
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            histogram_quantile(0.99,
              sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{
                service="app"
              }[5m])) by (le)
            ) * 1000
    
    - name: error-rate
      interval: 1m
      count: 5
      successCondition: result[0] <= 0.01
      failureCondition: result[0] > 0.05
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus.monitoring:9090
          query: |
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{
              service="app",
              status=~"5.."
            }[5m])) 
            / 
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{
              service="app"
            }[5m]))

---
# Virtual Service for Istio Traffic Routing
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: app-vsvc
  namespace: production
spec:
  hosts:
    - app.example.com
  gateways:
    - app-gateway
  http:
    - name: primary
      route:
        - destination:
            host: app-stable
            port:
              number: 80
          weight: 100
        - destination:
            host: app-canary
            port:
              number: 80
          weight: 0
```

```yaml
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

NEW_VERSION="${1:?Version required}"
NEW_COLOR="${2:-}"

# Determine current active color
ACTIVE_COLOR=$(kubectl get svc app-active -n $NAMESPACE \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector.color}' 2>/dev/null || echo "blue")

# Determine target color
if [ -z "$NEW_COLOR" ]; then
  NEW_COLOR=$([[ "$ACTIVE_COLOR" == "blue" ]] && echo "green" || echo "blue")
fi

echo "Current active: $ACTIVE_COLOR"
echo "Deploying to: $NEW_COLOR"
echo "Version: $NEW_VERSION"

# Update target deployment with new image
kubectl set image deployment/app-$NEW_COLOR \
  app=ghcr.io/org/app:$NEW_VERSION \
  -n $NAMESPACE

# Scale up target deployment
kubectl scale deployment/app-$NEW_COLOR --replicas=5 -n $NAMESPACE

# Wait for rollout
echo "Waiting for $NEW_COLOR deployment to be ready..."
kubectl rollout status deployment/app-$NEW_COLOR -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s

# Run smoke tests against new deployment
echo "Running smoke tests..."
kubectl run smoke-test-$$ --rm -i --restart=Never \
  --image=curlimages/curl:latest \
  -n $NAMESPACE \
  -- curl -sf http://app-$NEW_COLOR:8080/health

# Switch traffic
echo "Switching traffic to $NEW_COLOR..."
kubectl patch svc app-active -n $NAMESPACE \
  -p "{\"spec\":{\"selector\":{\"color\":\"$NEW_COLOR\"}}}"

# Verify switch
sleep 5
CURRENT=$(kubectl get svc app-active -n $NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector.color}')
if [ "$CURRENT" != "$NEW_COLOR" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: Traffic switch failed!"
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ Traffic successfully switched to $NEW_COLOR"

# Keep old deployment for quick rollback
echo "Old deployment ($ACTIVE_COLOR) kept for rollback capability"
echo "Run 'kubectl scale deployment/app-$ACTIVE_COLOR --replicas=0 -n $NAMESPACE' to scale down"
```

### Comprehensive Rollback Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/rollback.sh
# Comprehensive rollback script supporting multiple deployment strategies

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-production}"
APP_NAME="${APP_NAME:-app}"
DEPLOYMENT_TYPE="${DEPLOYMENT_TYPE:-rollout}"  # rollout, blue-green, helm
SLACK_WEBHOOK="${SLACK_WEBHOOK:-}"
REVISION="${1:-}"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m'

log_info() { echo -e "${GREEN}[INFO]${NC} $1"; }
log_warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"; }
log_error() { echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"; }

send_notification() {
    local status=$1
    local message=$2
    
    if [ -n "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" ]; then
        curl -s -X POST "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" \
            -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
            -d "{
                \"text\": \"$status Rollback in $NAMESPACE\",
                \"attachments\": [{
                    \"color\": \"$([ \"$status\" = \"✅\" ] && echo \"good\" || echo \"danger\")\",
                    \"fields\": [{
                        \"title\": \"Details\",
                        \"value\": \"$message\",
                        \"short\": false
                    }]
                }]
            }"
    fi
}

rollback_argo_rollout() {
    log_info "Rolling back Argo Rollout..."
    
    # Get current and previous revision info
    CURRENT_REV=$(kubectl argo rollouts get rollout $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE -o json | jq -r '.status.currentPodHash')
    
    if [ -n "$REVISION" ]; then
        log_info "Rolling back to specific revision: $REVISION"
        kubectl argo rollouts undo $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --to-revision=$REVISION
    else
        log_info "Rolling back to previous version"
        kubectl argo rollouts undo $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE
    fi
    
    # Wait for rollback to complete
    log_info "Waiting for rollback to complete..."
    kubectl argo rollouts status $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s
    
    NEW_REV=$(kubectl argo rollouts get rollout $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE -o json | jq -r '.status.currentPodHash')
    
    log_info "Rollback completed: $CURRENT_REV -> $NEW_REV"
    send_notification "✅" "Argo Rollout rolled back from $CURRENT_REV to $NEW_REV"
}

rollback_blue_green() {
    log_info "Rolling back Blue-Green deployment..."
    
    # Get current active color
    ACTIVE_COLOR=$(kubectl get svc ${APP_NAME}-active -n $NAMESPACE \
        -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector.color}')
    
    # Switch to other color
    ROLLBACK_COLOR=$([[ "$ACTIVE_COLOR" == "blue" ]] && echo "green" || echo "blue")
    
    # Verify rollback deployment is available
    AVAILABLE=$(kubectl get deployment ${APP_NAME}-${ROLLBACK_COLOR} -n $NAMESPACE \
        -o jsonpath='{.status.availableReplicas}' 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    
    if [ "$AVAILABLE" -eq 0 ]; then
        log_error "Rollback deployment ${APP_NAME}-${ROLLBACK_COLOR} has no available replicas!"
        log_info "Attempting to scale up previous deployment..."
        
        kubectl scale deployment ${APP_NAME}-${ROLLBACK_COLOR} \
            --replicas=5 -n $NAMESPACE
        
        kubectl rollout status deployment/${APP_NAME}-${ROLLBACK_COLOR} \
            -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s
    fi
    
    # Switch traffic
    log_info "Switching traffic from $ACTIVE_COLOR to $ROLLBACK_COLOR..."
    kubectl patch svc ${APP_NAME}-active -n $NAMESPACE \
        -p "{\"spec\":{\"selector\":{\"color\":\"$ROLLBACK_COLOR\"}}}"
    
    # Verify
    sleep 5
    CURRENT=$(kubectl get svc ${APP_NAME}-active -n $NAMESPACE \
        -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector.color}')
    
    if [ "$CURRENT" != "$ROLLBACK_COLOR" ]; then
        log_error "Traffic switch verification failed!"
        exit 1
    fi
    
    log_info "Traffic successfully switched to $ROLLBACK_COLOR"
    send_notification "✅" "Blue-Green switched from $ACTIVE_COLOR to $ROLLBACK_COLOR"
}

rollback_helm() {
    log_info "Rolling back Helm release..."
    
    # Get current revision
    CURRENT=$(helm history $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE -o json | jq -r '.[-1].revision')
    
    if [ -n "$REVISION" ]; then
        TARGET=$REVISION
    else
        # Get previous successful revision
        TARGET=$(helm history $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE -o json | \
            jq -r '[.[] | select(.status=="deployed")] | .[-2].revision')
    fi
    
    if [ -z "$TARGET" ] || [ "$TARGET" == "null" ]; then
        log_error "No previous revision found for rollback!"
        helm history $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE
        exit 1
    fi
    
    log_info "Rolling back from revision $CURRENT to $TARGET..."
    helm rollback $APP_NAME $TARGET -n $NAMESPACE --wait --timeout=5m
    
    log_info "Helm rollback completed"
    send_notification "✅" "Helm release rolled back from revision $CURRENT to $TARGET"
}

rollback_kubectl() {
    log_info "Rolling back Kubernetes deployment..."
    
    if [ -n "$REVISION" ]; then
        log_info "Rolling back to revision $REVISION..."
        kubectl rollout undo deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --to-revision=$REVISION
    else
        log_info "Rolling back to previous version..."
        kubectl rollout undo deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE
    fi
    
    kubectl rollout status deployment/$APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE --timeout=300s
    
    CURRENT_IMAGE=$(kubectl get deployment $APP_NAME -n $NAMESPACE \
        -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
    
    log_info "Deployment rolled back to: $CURRENT_IMAGE"
    send_notification "✅" "Deployment rolled back to $CURRENT_IMAGE"
}

verify_rollback() {
    log_info "Verifying rollback health..."
    
    # Wait for pods to be ready
    sleep 10
    
    # Check pod status
    NOT_READY=$(kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=$APP_NAME \
        -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status}' | \
        grep -c "False" || true)
    
    if [ "$NOT_READY" -gt 0 ]; then
        log_warn "$NOT_READY pods are not ready"
    fi
    
    # Run health check
    POD=$(kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=$APP_NAME \
        -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
    
    kubectl exec -n $NAMESPACE $POD -- \
        wget -q -O- http://localhost:8080/health/ready || {
        log_error "Health check failed after rollback!"
        exit 1
    }
    
    log_info "Rollback verification successful"
}

main() {
    log_info "Starting rollback for $APP_NAME in $NAMESPACE"
    log_info "Deployment type: $DEPLOYMENT_TYPE"
    
    case $DEPLOYMENT_TYPE in
        rollout|argo)
            rollback_argo_rollout
            ;;
        blue-green|bluegreen)
            rollback_blue_green
            ;;
        helm)
            rollback_helm
            ;;
        kubectl|deployment)
            rollback_kubectl
            ;;
        *)
            log_error "Unknown deployment type: $DEPLOYMENT_TYPE"
            echo "Supported types: rollout, blue-green, helm, kubectl"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
    
    verify_rollback
    log_info "Rollback completed successfully"
}

main "$@"
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/production-deploy.yml
name: Production Deployment with Approvals

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Version to deploy'
        required: true
        type: string
      skip_canary:
        description: 'Skip canary analysis'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

jobs:
  # Pre-deployment checks
  pre-checks:
    name: Pre-Deployment Checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      can_deploy: ${{ steps.check.outputs.can_deploy }}
      reason: ${{ steps.check.outputs.reason }}
    steps:
      - name: Check deployment window
        id: check
        run: |
          # Get current time in UTC
          HOUR=$(date -u +%H)
          DAY=$(date -u +%u)  # 1=Monday, 7=Sunday
          
          CAN_DEPLOY="true"
          REASON=""
          
          # Check if it's a weekend
          if [ "$DAY" -ge 6 ]; then
            CAN_DEPLOY="false"
            REASON="Weekend deployments are not allowed"
          fi
          
          # Check deployment hours (09:00-16:00 UTC)
          if [ "$HOUR" -lt 9 ] || [ "$HOUR" -ge 16 ]; then
            CAN_DEPLOY="false"
            REASON="Outside deployment hours (09:00-16:00 UTC)"
          fi
          
          # Check for deployment freeze
          FREEZE_FILE=".github/deployment-freeze.json"
          if [ -f "$FREEZE_FILE" ]; then
            FREEZE_END=$(jq -r '.freeze_until // empty' "$FREEZE_FILE")
            if [ -n "$FREEZE_END" ]; then
              if [ "$(date -u +%s)" -lt "$(date -d "$FREEZE_END" +%s)" ]; then
                CAN_DEPLOY="false"
                REASON="Deployment freeze until $FREEZE_END"
              fi
            fi
          fi
          
          echo "can_deploy=$CAN_DEPLOY" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "reason=$REASON" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          
          if [ "$CAN_DEPLOY" = "false" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Deployment blocked: $REASON"
          fi

      - name: Validate version exists
        run: |
          # Check if the image version exists in registry
          if ! docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ inputs.version }} > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::error::Version ${{ inputs.version }} not found in registry"
            exit 1
          fi

  # Automated quality gates
  quality-gates:
    name: Quality Gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [pre-checks]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check test coverage
        run: |
          # Fetch coverage from Codecov API or stored artifact
          COVERAGE=$(curl -s "https://codecov.io/api/v2/github/${{ github.repository }}/commits/${{ github.sha }}" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}" | jq -r '.coverage')
          
          if (( $(echo "$COVERAGE < 80" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "::error::Test coverage $COVERAGE% is below 80% threshold"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ Test coverage: $COVERAGE%"

      - name: Check security scan results
        run: |
          # Query security scan results
          CRITICAL=$(gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/code-scanning/alerts \
            --jq '[.[] | select(.state=="open" and .rule.security_severity_level=="critical")] | length')
          
          if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$CRITICAL critical security vulnerabilities found"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ No critical security vulnerabilities"
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Verify staging deployment health
        run: |
          # Check staging environment health
          HEALTH=$(curl -sf https://staging.example.com/health || echo "unhealthy")
          if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
            echo "::error::Staging environment is not healthy"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ Staging environment healthy"

  # Manual approval gate
  approval:
    name: Production Approval
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [pre-checks, quality-gates]
    if: needs.pre-checks.outputs.can_deploy == 'true'
    environment:
      name: production-approval
    steps:
      - name: Approval received
        run: |
          echo "✅ Production deployment approved by ${{ github.actor }}"
          echo "Version: ${{ inputs.version }}"

  # Production deployment
  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Production
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [approval]
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://app.example.com
    concurrency:
      group: production-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure kubectl
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.kube
          echo "${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG_PROD }}" | base64 -d > ~/.kube/config

      - name: Create deployment record
        run: |
          # Record deployment in database/API
          curl -X POST "https://api.example.com/deployments" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{
              "version": "${{ inputs.version }}",
              "environment": "production",
              "deployer": "${{ github.actor }}",
              "commit": "${{ github.sha }}",
              "workflow_run": "${{ github.run_id }}"
            }'

      - name: Deploy with Argo Rollouts
        run: |
          kubectl argo rollouts set image app \
            app=ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ inputs.version }} \
            -n production

      - name: Monitor canary
        if: ${{ !inputs.skip_canary }}
        run: |
          # Monitor canary deployment
          kubectl argo rollouts status app -n production --timeout=30m

      - name: Notify success
        if: success()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "✅ Production deployment successful",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "fields": [
                    {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Version:* ${{ inputs.version }}"},
                    {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Deployed by:* ${{ github.actor }}"},
                    {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Environment:* Production"}
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}

      - name: Notify failure
        if: failure()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "❌ Production deployment FAILED",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "Production deployment failed!\n*Version:* ${{ inputs.version }}\n*Run:* ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```

```yaml
                latest

          - task: GoTool@0
            inputs:
              version: '1.21'

          - script: |
              go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...

          - task: PublishCodeCoverageResults@1
            inputs:

  # Deploy to Development
  - stage: DeployDev
    displayName: 'Deploy to Development'
    dependsOn: Build
    condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/develop'))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployDev
        displayName: 'Deploy to Dev'
        environment: 'development'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: KubernetesManifest@0
                  inputs:
                    action: 'deploy'
                    kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Dev'
                    namespace: 'development'
                    manifests: |
                      $(Pipeline.Workspace)/manifests/deployment.yaml
                    containers: |
                      $(containerRegistry)/$(imageRepository):$(tag)

  # Deploy to Staging
  - stage: DeployStaging
    displayName: 'Deploy to Staging'
    dependsOn: Build
    condition: and(succeeded(), or(eq(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/main'), startsWith(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/release/')))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployStaging
        displayName: 'Deploy to Staging'

        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        strategy:

            deploy:

                - task: HelmDeploy@0

                    kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Staging'
                    namespace: 'staging'
                    command: 'upgrade'
                    chartType: 'FilePath'
                    chartPath: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/helm/app'
                    releaseName: 'app'
                    overrideValues: 'image.tag=$(tag)'
                    waitForExecution: true

  # Deploy to UAT (with approval)
  - stage: DeployUAT
    displayName: 'Deploy to UAT'
    dependsOn: DeployStaging
    condition: succeeded()
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployUAT
        displayName: 'Deploy to UAT'
        environment: 'uat'  # Environment with approval gate configured
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: HelmDeploy@0
                  inputs:
                    connectionType: 'Kubernetes Service Connection'
                    kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-UAT'
                    namespace: 'uat'
                    command: 'upgrade'
                    chartType: 'FilePath'
                    chartPath: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/helm/app'
                    releaseName: 'app'
                    overrideValues: 'image.tag=$(tag)'

  # Deploy to Production (with multiple approvals)
  - stage: DeployProduction
    displayName: 'Deploy to Production'
    dependsOn: DeployUAT
    condition: and(succeeded(), startsWith(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/tags/v'))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployProdCanary
        displayName: 'Canary Deployment'
        environment: 'production'  # Environment with approval + business hours check
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        strategy:
          canary:
            increments: [10, 25, 50]
            preDeploy:
              steps:
                - script: |
                    echo "Pre-deployment checks..."
                    # Verify deployment window
                    HOUR=$(date -u +%H)
                    if [ "$HOUR" -lt 9 ] || [ "$HOUR" -ge 16 ]; then
                      echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Outside deployment window"
                      exit 1
                    fi
                  displayName: 'Check deployment window'
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: KubernetesManifest@0
                  inputs:
                    action: 'deploy'
                    kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Production'
                    namespace: 'production'
                    strategy: 'canary'
                    percentage: $(strategy.increment)
                    manifests: |
                      $(Pipeline.Workspace)/manifests/deployment.yaml
                    containers: |
                      $(containerRegistry)/$(imageRepository):$(tag)
            postRouteTraffic:
              steps:
                - script: |
                    echo "Running smoke tests..."
                    ./scripts/smoke-test.sh https://app.example.com
                  displayName: 'Smoke Tests'
                - script: |
                    echo "Checking metrics..."
                    # Query Prometheus for error rate
                    ERROR_RATE=$(curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_errors_total[5m])" | jq '.data.result[0].value[1]')
                    if (( $(echo "$ERROR_RATE > 0.01" | bc -l) )); then
                      echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]High error rate: $ERROR_RATE"
                      exit 1
                    fi
                  displayName: 'Check Error Rate'
            on:
              failure:
                steps:
                  - task: KubernetesManifest@0
                    inputs:
                      action: 'reject'
                      kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Production'
                      namespace: 'production'
                      strategy: 'canary'
                  - script: |
                      echo "Deployment failed, sending notification..."
                    displayName: 'Notify Failure'
              success:
                steps:
                  - task: KubernetesManifest@0
                    inputs:
                      action: 'promote'
                      kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Production'
                      namespace: 'production'
                      strategy: 'canary'
                  - script: |
                      echo "Deployment successful!"
                    displayName: 'Notify Success'
```

```groovy
                            -t ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${GIT_COMMIT_SHORT} \
                            .
                        
                        docker push ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION}
                        docker push ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${GIT_COMMIT_SHORT}
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('Deploy to Development') {
            when {
                branch 'develop'
            }
            steps {
                container('kubectl') {
                    sh '''
                        mkdir -p ~/.kube
                        cp $KUBECONFIG_DEV ~/.kube/config
                        
                        kubectl set image deployment/app \
                            app=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION} \
                            -n development
                        
                        kubectl rollout status deployment/app \
                            -n development --timeout=300s
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('Deploy to Staging') {
            when {
                anyOf {
                    branch 'main'
                    branch pattern: 'release/*', comparator: 'GLOB'
                }
            }
            steps {
                container('kubectl') {
                    sh '''
                        mkdir -p ~/.kube
                        cp $KUBECONFIG_STAGING ~/.kube/config
                        
                        # Blue-Green deployment
                        ACTIVE=$(kubectl get svc app-active -n staging -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector.color}' || echo "blue")
                        TARGET=$([[ "$ACTIVE" == "blue" ]] && echo "green" || echo "blue")
                        
                        kubectl set image deployment/app-$TARGET \
                            app=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION} \
                            -n staging
                        
                        kubectl scale deployment/app-$TARGET --replicas=3 -n staging
                        kubectl rollout status deployment/app-$TARGET -n staging --timeout=300s
                        
                        # Switch traffic
                        kubectl patch svc app-active -n staging \
                            -p "{\\"spec\\":{\\"selector\\":{\\"color\\":\\"$TARGET\\"}}}"
                    '''
                }
            }
        }

        stage('E2E Tests') {
            when {
                anyOf {
                    branch 'main'
                    branch pattern: 'release/*', comparator: 'GLOB'
                }
            }
            steps {
                sh '''
                    cd tests/e2e
                    npm ci
                    npm run test:staging
                '''
            }
        }

        stage('Deploy to Production') {
            when {
                buildingTag()
            }
            options {
                timeout(time: 30, unit: 'MINUTES')
            }
            input {
                message 'Deploy to production?'
                ok 'Deploy'
                submitter 'release-managers,sre-team'
                parameters {
                    choice(
                        name: 'DEPLOY_STRATEGY',
                        choices: ['canary', 'blue-green', 'rolling'],
                        description: 'Deployment strategy'
                    )
                }
            }
            steps {
                container('kubectl') {
                    script {
                        sh '''
                            mkdir -p ~/.kube
                            cp $KUBECONFIG_PROD ~/.kube/config
                        '''
                        
                        if (env.DEPLOY_STRATEGY == 'canary') {
                            sh '''
                                kubectl argo rollouts set image app \
                                    app=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION} \
                                    -n production
                                
                                kubectl argo rollouts status app \
                                    -n production --timeout=30m
                            '''
                        } else {
                            sh '''
                                kubectl set image deployment/app \
                                    app=${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${VERSION} \
                                    -n production
                                
                                kubectl rollout status deployment/app \
                                    -n production --timeout=300s
                            '''
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            post {
                success {
                    slackSend(
                        channel: '#deployments',
                        color: 'good',
                        message: "✅ Production deployment successful\nVersion: ${VERSION}\nStrategy: ${DEPLOY_STRATEGY}"
                    )
                }
                failure {
                    slackSend(
                        channel: '#deployments',
                        color: 'danger',
                        message: "❌ Production deployment FAILED\nVersion: ${VERSION}\n${BUILD_URL}"
                    )
                }
            }
        }
    }

    post {
        always {
            cleanWs()
        }
        failure {
            slackSend(
                channel: '#ci-alerts',
                color: 'danger',
                message: "Pipeline failed: ${env.JOB_NAME} #${env.BUILD_NUMBER}\n${env.BUILD_URL}"
            )
        }
    }
}
```

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix
import seaborn as sns

# TensorFlow/Keras imports
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.layers import (
    Embedding, LSTM, Dense, Dropout, 
    Bidirectional, SpatialDropout1D
)
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.text import Tokenizer
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence import pad_sequences
from tensorflow.keras.callbacks import EarlyStopping, ModelCheckpoint
from tensorflow.keras.utils import plot_model

# Set random seed for reproducibility
np.random.seed(42)
tf.random.set_seed(42)


class SentimentLSTM:
    """LSTM-based Sentiment Classification Model"""
    
    def __init__(self, max_words=10000, max_len=200, embedding_dim=128):
        """
        Initialize the sentiment classifier.
        
        Args:
            max_words: Maximum vocabulary size
            max_len: Maximum sequence length
            embedding_dim: Dimension of word embeddings
        """
        self.max_words = max_words
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.embedding_dim = embedding_dim
        self.tokenizer = Tokenizer(num_words=max_words, oov_token='<OOV>')
        self.model = None
        self.history = None
        
    def preprocess_text(self, texts):
        """
        Basic text preprocessing.
        
        Args:
            texts: List of text strings
            
        Returns:
            Preprocessed texts
        """
        import re
        
        processed = []
        for text in texts:
            # Convert to lowercase
            text = text.lower()
            # Remove HTML tags
            text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', text)
            # Remove special characters but keep basic punctuation
            text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z\s]', '', text)
            # Remove extra whitespace
            text = ' '.join(text.split())
            processed.append(text)
        
        return processed
    
    def prepare_data(self, texts, labels, test_size=0.2):
        """
        Tokenize and pad sequences, then split data.
        
        Args:
            texts: List of text strings
            labels: List of labels (0 or 1)
            test_size: Proportion for test set
            
        Returns:
            X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test
        """
        # Preprocess texts
        texts = self.preprocess_text(texts)
        
        # Fit tokenizer on texts
        self.tokenizer.fit_on_texts(texts)
        
        # Convert texts to sequences
        sequences = self.tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(texts)
        
        # Pad sequences
        X = pad_sequences(sequences, maxlen=self.max_len, padding='post', truncating='post')
        y = np.array(labels)
        
        # Split data
        X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
            X, y, test_size=test_size, random_state=42, stratify=y
        )
        
        print(f"Vocabulary size: {len(self.tokenizer.word_index)}")
        print(f"Training samples: {len(X_train)}")
        print(f"Testing samples: {len(X_test)}")
        
        return X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test
    
    def build_model(self, model_type='bidirectional'):
        """
        Build the LSTM model architecture.
        
        Args:
            model_type: 'simple', 'stacked', or 'bidirectional'
        """
        self.model = Sequential(name=f'{model_type}_lstm')
        
        # Embedding layer
        self.model.add(Embedding(
            input_dim=self.max_words,
            output_dim=self.embedding_dim,
            input_length=self.max_len,
            name='embedding'
        ))
        
        # Spatial dropout after embedding
        self.model.add(SpatialDropout1D(0.2, name='spatial_dropout'))
        
        if model_type == 'simple':
            # Simple single LSTM layer
            self.model.add(LSTM(64, name='lstm'))
            
        elif model_type == 'stacked':
            # Stacked LSTM layers
            self.model.add(LSTM(128, return_sequences=True, name='lstm_1'))
            self.model.add(Dropout(0.3, name='dropout_1'))
            self.model.add(LSTM(64, name='lstm_2'))
            
        elif model_type == 'bidirectional':
            # Bidirectional LSTM
            self.model.add(Bidirectional(
                LSTM(64, return_sequences=True), 
                name='bidirectional_1'
            ))
            self.model.add(Dropout(0.3, name='dropout_1'))
            self.model.add(Bidirectional(
                LSTM(32), 
                name='bidirectional_2'
            ))
        
        # Dense layers
        self.model.add(Dropout(0.4, name='dropout_final'))
        self.model.add(Dense(64, activation='relu', name='dense_1'))
        self.model.add(Dropout(0.3, name='dropout_dense'))
        self.model.add(Dense(1, activation='sigmoid', name='output'))
        
        # Compile model
        self.model.compile(
            optimizer='adam',
            loss='binary_crossentropy',
            metrics=['accuracy']
        )
        
        print(self.model.summary())
        return self.model
    
    def train(self, X_train, y_train, X_val=None, y_val=None, 
              epochs=20, batch_size=64):
        """
        Train the model.
        
        Args:
            X_train, y_train: Training data
            X_val, y_val: Validation data (optional)
            epochs: Number of training epochs
            batch_size: Batch size
        """
        # Callbacks
        callbacks = [
            EarlyStopping(
                monitor='val_loss',
                patience=3,
                restore_best_weights=True,
                verbose=1
            ),
            ModelCheckpoint(
                'best_model.keras',
                monitor='val_accuracy',
                save_best_only=True,
                verbose=1
            )
        ]
        
        # Determine validation data
        if X_val is not None and y_val is not None:
            validation_data = (X_val, y_val)
        else:
            validation_data = None
            
        # Train
        self.history = self.model.fit(
            X_train, y_train,
            epochs=epochs,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            validation_split=0.15 if validation_data is None else 0.0,
            validation_data=validation_data,
            callbacks=callbacks,
            verbose=1
        )
        
        return self.history
    
    def evaluate(self, X_test, y_test):
        """
        Evaluate the model on test data.
        
        Args:
            X_test: Test features
            y_test: Test labels
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with evaluation metrics
        """
        # Get predictions
        y_pred_proba = self.model.predict(X_test)
        y_pred = (y_pred_proba > 0.5).astype(int).flatten()
        
        # Calculate metrics
        loss, accuracy = self.model.evaluate(X_test, y_test, verbose=0)
        
        print("\n" + "="*50)
        print("MODEL EVALUATION")
        print("="*50)
        print(f"Test Loss: {loss:.4f}")
        print(f"Test Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
        print("\nClassification Report:")
        print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, 
              target_names=['Negative', 'Positive']))
        
        return {
            'loss': loss,
            'accuracy': accuracy,
            'predictions': y_pred,
            'probabilities': y_pred_proba
        }
    
    def predict_sentiment(self, texts):
        """
        Predict sentiment for new texts.
        
        Args:
            texts: List of text strings
            
        Returns:
            Predictions and probabilities
        """
        # Preprocess
        texts = self.preprocess_text(texts)
        
        # Convert to sequences
        sequences = self.tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(texts)
        padded = pad_sequences(sequences, maxlen=self.max_len, 
                               padding='post', truncating='post')
        
        # Predict
        probabilities = self.model.predict(padded, verbose=0)
        predictions = (probabilities > 0.5).astype(int).flatten()
        
        results = []
        for text, pred, prob in zip(texts, predictions, probabilities):
            sentiment = 'Positive' if pred == 1 else 'Negative'
            confidence = prob[0] if pred == 1 else 1 - prob[0]
            results.append({
                'text': text[:50] + '...' if len(text) > 50 else text,
                'sentiment': sentiment,
                'confidence': float(confidence)
            })
        
        return results
    
    def plot_training_history(self):
        """Plot training history."""
        if self.history is None:
            print("No training history available.")
            return
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))
        
        # Accuracy plot
        axes[0].plot(self.history.history['accuracy'], label='Training', linewidth=2)
        axes[0].plot(self.history.history['val_accuracy'], label='Validation', linewidth=2)
        axes[0].set_title('Model Accuracy', fontsize=14)
        axes[0].set_xlabel('Epoch')
        axes[0].set_ylabel('Accuracy')
        axes[0].legend()
        axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Loss plot
        axes[1].plot(self.history.history['loss'], label='Training', linewidth=2)
        axes[1].plot(self.history.history['val_loss'], label='Validation', linewidth=2)
        axes[1].set_title('Model Loss', fontsize=14)
        axes[1].set_xlabel('Epoch')
        axes[1].set_ylabel('Loss')
        axes[1].legend()
        axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig('training_history.png', dpi=150)
        plt.show()
    
    def plot_confusion_matrix(self, y_true, y_pred):
        """Plot confusion matrix."""
        cm = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)
        
        plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
        sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues',
                    xticklabels=['Negative', 'Positive'],
                    yticklabels=['Negative', 'Positive'])
        plt.title('Confusion Matrix', fontsize=14)
        plt.xlabel('Predicted')
        plt.ylabel('Actual')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig('confusion_matrix.png', dpi=150)
        plt.show()

class AttentionLayer(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    """Custom Attention Layer for LSTM."""
    
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super(AttentionLayer, self).__init__(**kwargs)
    
    def build(self, input_shape):
        self.W = self.add_weight(
            name='attention_weight',
            shape=(input_shape[-1], 1),
            initializer='glorot_uniform',
            trainable=True
        )
        self.b = self.add_weight(
            name='attention_bias',
            shape=(input_shape[1], 1),
            initializer='zeros',
            trainable=True
        )
        super(AttentionLayer, self).build(input_shape)
    
    def call(self, x):
        # Compute attention scores
        e = tf.tanh(tf.tensordot(x, self.W, axes=1) + self.b)
        a = tf.nn.softmax(e, axis=1)
        output = tf.reduce_sum(x * a, axis=1)
        return output


def build_lstm_with_attention(vocab_size, max_len, embedding_dim=128, num_classes=3):
    """Build LSTM model with attention mechanism."""
    
    inputs = tf.keras.Input(shape=(max_len,))
    
    # Embedding
    x = Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim)(inputs)
    x = SpatialDropout1D(0.2)(x)
    
    # Bidirectional LSTM
    x = Bidirectional(LSTM(64, return_sequences=True))(x)
    x = Dropout(0.3)(x)
    
    # Attention layer
    x = AttentionLayer()(x)
    
    # Dense layers
    x = Dense(64, activation='relu')(x)
    x = Dropout(0.4)(x)
    
    # Output layer

        loss = 'binary_crossentropy'
    else:
        outputs = Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax')(x)
        loss = 'sparse_categorical_crossentropy'
    
    model = tf.keras.Model(inputs, outputs)
    model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss=loss, metrics=['accuracy'])
```

## Introduction: Why Design Matters

A well-designed experiment is the foundation of credible science. Poor design cannot be fixed by sophisticated analysis—the phrase "garbage in, garbage out" applies directly. This guide covers the core principles that protect against bias and maximize the information gained from your research.

---

## 1. Randomization

### What It Is
Randomization is the random allocation of experimental units (subjects, plots, samples) to treatment conditions. It is the single most important feature distinguishing a true experiment from an observational study.

### Why It Matters
- **Eliminates systematic bias**: Ensures no hidden variable determines who gets which treatment
- **Balances unknown confounders**: Variables you didn't measure or don't know about are probabilistically distributed equally across groups
- **Justifies statistical inference**: Creates the probabilistic basis for p-values and confidence intervals

### Methods of Randomization

**Simple Randomization**
```
# Python example: simple randomization
import random

subjects = ['S1', 'S2', 'S3', 'S4', 'S5', 'S6', 'S7', 'S8']
random.shuffle(subjects)
treatment = subjects[:4]
control = subjects[4:]
print(f"Treatment group: {treatment}")
print(f"Control group: {control}")
```

**Stratified Randomization**
Randomize within strata to ensure balance on key variables.

```
# Stratified by sex
males = ['M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4']
females = ['F1', 'F2', 'F3', 'F4']

random.shuffle(males)
random.shuffle(females)

treatment = males[:2] + females[:2]  # 2 males, 2 females
control = males[2:] + females[2:]    # 2 males, 2 females
```

**Block Randomization**
Ensures equal group sizes after every k subjects (useful for sequential enrollment).

```
# Block size of 4: guarantees 2 treatment, 2 control per block
block = ['T', 'T', 'C', 'C']
random.shuffle(block)
# Result might be: ['C', 'T', 'C', 'T']
```

### Example: Clinical Trial

**Poor design**: Assign the first 50 patients to receive the new drug, next 50 to placebo.
- Problem: Early patients may differ systematically from later patients (seasonality, changing referral patterns, physician learning)

**Good design**: Use computer-generated random numbers to assign each patient at enrollment.
- Each patient has equal, independent probability of each assignment
- Document the randomization seed for reproducibility

---

## 2. Blinding (Masking)

### Levels of Blinding

| Level | Who is Blinded | Purpose |
|-------|---------------|---------|
| Single-blind | Participants only | Prevents placebo effects, demand characteristics |
| Double-blind | Participants AND researchers | Also prevents researcher bias in treatment delivery and outcome measurement |
| Triple-blind | Participants, researchers, AND analysts | Also prevents bias in data analysis |

### Why Each Level Matters

**Participant blinding** prevents:
- Placebo effects (expecting benefit → experiencing benefit)
- Nocebo effects (expecting harm → experiencing harm)
- Differential dropout (control group leaves due to disappointment)
- Reporting bias (treatment group reports more positively)

**Researcher blinding** prevents:
- Differential treatment (unconsciously giving more attention to treatment group)
- Biased outcome assessment (seeing improvement you expect to see)
- Leading questions in interviews

**Analyst blinding** prevents:
- Selective analysis approaches favoring desired outcomes
- "Trying different things until it works"

### Example: Drug Trial Design

```
Design for testing anti-anxiety medication:

1. Pharmacy prepares identical capsules:
   - Active: contains medication
   - Placebo: contains inert filler
   
2. Capsules coded (A, B) - code held by pharmacist only

3. Study nurse (blinded) administers capsules per randomization schedule

4. Outcome assessor (blinded) rates anxiety using structured interview

5. Statistician (blinded) analyzes "Group A vs Group B"

6. Code broken ONLY after analysis is locked
```

### When Blinding Is Impossible

Some interventions cannot be blinded (surgery vs. medication, psychotherapy vs. medication). Solutions:
- **Blinded outcome assessment**: Assessor doesn't know treatment assignment
- **Objective outcomes**: Use blood tests, imaging, administrative records
- **Active controls**: Compare two active treatments rather than treatment vs. nothing

---

## 3. Blocking

### What It Is
Blocking groups experimental units that are similar to each other, then randomizes treatments within each block. This controls for known sources of variability.

### The Logic
Variability between blocks is removed from the error term → more precise treatment effect estimates → higher statistical power.

### Common Blocking Factors

| Field | Common Blocking Factors |
|-------|------------------------|
| Agriculture | Field location, soil type, slope |
| Clinical trials | Study site, age group, disease severity |
| Psychology | Time of day, experimenter, testing room |
| Manufacturing | Machine, shift, raw material batch |

### Example: Agricultural Field Trial

Testing 4 fertilizer types (A, B, C, D) across a field with known fertility gradient.

**Without blocking (Completely Randomized Design)**:
```
Field layout (random assignment):
┌───┬───┬───┬───┐
│ A │ A │ B │ D │  (poor soil)
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│ C │ B │ A │ C │  (medium soil)
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│ D │ D │ C │ B │  (rich soil)
└───┴───┴───┴───┘
Problem: Fertilizer D happens to be on rich soil more often.
Any "D effect" might just be soil fertility.
```

**With blocking (Randomized Complete Block Design)**:
```
Each row is a block (soil type). Each treatment appears once per block:
┌───┬───┬───┬───┐
│ B │ D │ A │ C │  Block 1 (poor soil)
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│ A │ C │ D │ B │  Block 2 (medium soil)
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│ C │ A │ B │ D │  Block 3 (rich soil)
└───┴───┴───┴───┘
Every fertilizer tested equally in each soil type.
Soil differences are statistically controlled.
```

### Matched Pairs: A Special Case

When you have only two treatments, pair similar units and randomize within pairs.

**Example**: Testing a reading intervention
```
Pair students by pre-test reading score:
Pair 1: Student A (score 45) and Student B (score 46)
  → Flip coin: A gets intervention, B gets control
  
Pair 2: Student C (score 62) and Student D (score 61)
  → Flip coin: D gets intervention, C gets control

Analysis: Compare differences within pairs
```

### Within-Subject Blocking (Repeated Measures)

Each subject serves as their own block, receiving all treatments.

```
Crossover Design for migraine medication:

Period 1          Washout      Period 2
---------         -------      ---------
Subject 1: Drug A    →            Drug B
Subject 2: Drug B    →            Drug A
Subject 3: Drug A    →            Drug B
Subject 4: Drug B    →            Drug A

Advantage: Controls for all stable individual differences
Disadvantage: Carryover effects may persist
```

---

## 4. Factorial Designs

### What They Are
Factorial designs study two or more factors simultaneously, with every combination of factor levels included.

### Notation
A 2×3 factorial has:
- Factor A with 2 levels
- Factor B with 3 levels
- 2 × 3 = 6 treatment combinations

### Why Use Factorials?

**Efficiency**: Test multiple factors in one experiment rather than separate experiments.

**Interactions**: Discover whether the effect of one factor depends on the level of another.

### Example: 2×2 Factorial in Education

**Research question**: How do teaching method and class size affect test scores?

**Factors**:
- Teaching method: Traditional lecture vs. Active learning
- Class size: Small (20) vs. Large (60)

**Design**:
```
                    Small Class     Large Class
                    -----------     -----------
Traditional         Condition 1     Condition 2
                    (n=25)          (n=25)
                    
Active Learning     Condition 3     Condition 4
                    (n=25)          (n=25)
```

**Possible results and interpretations**:

```
Scenario A: No interaction (additive effects)
                    Small    Large
Traditional         60       55      ← Large classes -5 points
Active Learning     75       70      ← Large classes -5 points
                    ↑        ↑
                    Active +15 in both cases

Main effect of Method: +15 points for active learning
Main effect of Size: -5 points for large classes
The effects simply add together: Active + Small = 60+15=75 ✓
```

```
Scenario B: Interaction present
                    Small    Large
Traditional         60       55      ← Large classes -5 points
Active Learning     75       60      ← Large classes -15 points
                    
Active learning helps more in small classes (+15) 
than in large classes (+5).
Cannot describe effects without considering the other factor.
```

### Visualizing Interactions

```
Test Scores

80 |           
   |     ●------● Small + Active = Best
75 |    /      
   |   /        
70 |  ●        ○------○ Large + Active
   |   \      /
65 |    \    /
   |     \  /
60 |      ●------● Small + Traditional
55 |             ○ Large + Traditional
   |________________________
     Traditional    Active
     
Parallel lines = No interaction
Non-parallel lines = Interaction present
```

### 2^k Factorial Designs

Common in industrial/engineering research. All factors have 2 levels (often coded as -1 and +1).

**Example: 2³ design for chemical yield**
```
Factor A: Temperature (Low=-1, High=+1)
Factor B: Pressure (Low=-1, High=+1)  
Factor C: Catalyst (Type X=-1, Type Y=+1)

Run | A  | B  | C  | Yield
----|----|----|----|----- 
1   | -1 | -1 | -1 | 45
2   | +1 | -1 | -1 | 52
3   | -1 | +1 | -1 | 48
4   | +1 | +1 | -1 | 63
5   | -1 | -1 | +1 | 51
6   | +1 | -1 | +1 | 59
7   | -1 | +1 | +1 | 54
8   | +1 | +1 | +1 | 72

8 runs test 3 main effects + 3 two-way interactions + 1 three-way interaction
```

### Fractional Factorials

When full factorial is too expensive, use a fraction.

**2^(k-p) design**: Uses 2^(k-p) runs instead of 2^k runs.

Trade-off: Some effects become **aliased** (confounded with each other).

## 5. Power and Sample Size

### Key Concepts

**Statistical Power**: Probability of detecting an effect when it truly exists.
- Power = 1 - β (where β = Type II error rate)
- Convention: aim for power ≥ 0.80

**The Power Equation** involves four quantities (know any three, solve for the fourth):

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. Effect Size (d, Cohen's d, R², η², etc.)               │
│  2. Sample Size (n)                                        │
│  3. Significance Level (α, typically 0.05)                 │
│  4. Power (1 - β, typically 0.80)                         │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Effect Size Conventions (Cohen's d)

| d | Interpretation | Example |
|---|---------------|---------|
| 0.2 | Small | Subtle psychological effects |
| 0.5 | Medium | Noticeable practical difference |
| 0.8 | Large | Obvious, dramatic difference |

### Sample Size Formulas

**For two-group comparison (equal n per group)**:

```
n per group = 2 × [(z_α/2 + z_β)² × σ²] / δ²

Where:
  z_α/2 = 1.96 for α = 0.05 (two-tailed)
  z_β = 0.84 for power = 0.80
  σ = standard deviation
  δ = minimum detectable difference
```

**Quick reference table (two groups, α=0.05, power=0.80)**:

| Effect Size (d) | n per group | Total N |
|----------------|-------------|---------|
| 0.2 (small)    | 393         | 786     |
| 0.5 (medium)   | 64          | 128     |
| 0.8 (large)    | 26          | 52      |

### Power Analysis in R

```r
# Two-sample t-test power analysis
library(pwr)

# Q: "What sample size to detect d=0.5 with 80% power?"
pwr.t.test(d = 0.5, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80, type = "two.sample")
# Result: n = 63.77 per group → use 64 per group

# Q: "What power do I have with n=30 per group, expecting d=0.6?"
pwr.t.test(n = 30, d = 0.6, sig.level = 0.05, type = "two.sample")
# Result: power = 0.61 (underpowered!)

# ANOVA: 4 groups, medium effect size (f=0.25)
pwr.anova.test(k = 4, f = 0.25, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80)
# Result: n = 45 per group

# Correlation
pwr.r.test(r = 0.3, sig.level = 0.05, power = 0.80)
# Result: n = 84 total
```

### Power Analysis in Python

```python
from statsmodels.stats.power import TTestIndPower

analysis = TTestIndPower()

# Find required n for d=0.5, alpha=0.05, power=0.80
n = analysis.solve_power(effect_size=0.5, alpha=0.05, power=0.80)
print(f"Required n per group: {n:.0f}")  # Output: 64

# Find power for given n and effect size
power = analysis.solve_power(effect_size=0.5, nobs1=30, alpha=0.05)
print(f"Power: {power:.2f}")  # Output: 0.48
```

### Common Mistakes in Power Analysis

1. **Computing post-hoc power** using the observed effect size (circular reasoning)
2. **Using unrealistic effect sizes** based on pilot studies (overestimates)
3. **Forgetting attrition**: If you expect 20% dropout, recruit n/0.8
4. **Ignoring clustering**: Patients within doctors, students within classrooms require adjusted formulas

## 6. Confounding

### What It Is

A **confound** is a variable that:
1. Is associated with the treatment/exposure
2. Is associated with the outcome
3. Is NOT on the causal pathway from treatment to outcome

Confounding makes it impossible to determine whether the treatment or the confound caused the observed effect.

### Visual Representation

```
          Confound (C)
           ↙     ↘
    Treatment (T) → Outcome (Y)
    
If C → T and C → Y, then the T-Y association may be spurious
```

### Classic Examples

**Example 1: Ice cream and drowning**
```
        Hot Weather
         ↙      ↘
  Ice Cream ←?→ Drowning

Observation: Ice cream sales correlate with drowning deaths
Reality: Hot weather causes both (more swimming + more ice cream)
Ice cream doesn't cause drowning
```

**Example 2: Hospital quality paradox**
```
        Disease Severity
          ↙        ↘
  Hospital Choice → Death

Better hospitals may have higher mortality rates because they 
receive sicker patients. Severity confounds the hospital-death relationship.
```

### Controlling for Confounders

**At design stage** (preferred):
| Method | How it works |
|--------|-------------|
| Randomization | Distributes all confounders equally across groups |
| Restriction | Limit study to one level of confounder (e.g., only males) |
| Matching | Pair treated/control units on confounder values |
| Blocking | Randomize within levels of the confounder |

**At analysis stage**:
| Method | How it works |
|--------|-------------|
| Stratification | Analyze separately within confounder levels |
| Regression | Include confounder as covariate |
| Propensity scores | Match/weight by probability of treatment |

### Example: Analyzing with Confounders

```r
# Naive analysis (ignoring confounder)
model_naive <- lm(outcome ~ treatment, data = mydata)

# Adjusted analysis (including confounder)
model_adjusted <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + confounder, data = mydata)

# Compare results
summary(model_naive)$coefficients["treatment", ]
summary(model_adjusted)$coefficients["treatment", ]

# If treatment effect changes substantially, confounding was present
```

### Causal Diagrams (DAGs)

Directed Acyclic Graphs help identify what to control for:

```
Example: Does exercise reduce depression?

Age → Exercise ← Motivation
 ↓        ↓           ↓
 └──→ Depression ←────┘
 
Age and Motivation are confounders (backdoor paths)
→ Control for Age and Motivation

But NOT: Exercise → Sleep → Depression
Sleep is a mediator (on the causal path)
→ Don't control for Sleep if you want total effect
```

### Unmeasured Confounding

The biggest threat to causal inference. Even with statistical adjustment, you cannot control for variables you didn't measure.

**Sensitivity analysis**: Ask "How strong would an unmeasured confounder need to be to explain away the observed effect?"

## 7. Analysis Plans

### What Is a Pre-Specified Analysis Plan?

A detailed document written BEFORE data collection (or at minimum, before looking at the data) that specifies:

1. Primary outcome(s)
2. Primary analysis method
3. Secondary analyses
4. How covariates will be handled
5. Subgroup analyses
6. How missing data will be addressed
7. Criteria for statistical significance

### Why Pre-Specify?

**Problem**: Researcher degrees of freedom
```
Same dataset, many defensible choices:
- Include or exclude outliers?
- Transform the outcome?
- Which covariates to adjust for?
- Which subgroups to examine?
- One-tailed or two-tailed test?
- Parametric or non-parametric?

These choices can flip results from "significant" to "not significant"
```

**Solution**: Lock in choices BEFORE seeing the outcome data.

### Template Analysis Plan

```markdown
# Statistical Analysis Plan
## Study: Effect of Mindfulness App on Stress Reduction

### 1. Study Design
Randomized controlled trial, parallel groups, 1:1 allocation

### 2. Primary Outcome
Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) score at 8 weeks

### 3. Primary Analysis
Intention-to-treat analysis comparing mean PSS-10 scores between 
groups using ANCOVA with baseline PSS-10 as covariate.

    Model: PSS_week8 ~ Treatment + PSS_baseline

Significance threshold: α = 0.05, two-tailed
Effect size: Cohen's d with 95% CI

### 4. Secondary Outcomes
- Anxiety (GAD-7) at 8 weeks
- Sleep quality (PSQI) at 8 weeks
- App engagement (minutes/week)

### 5. Subgroup Analyses
Treatment effect stratified by:
- Baseline stress (high vs. low, median split)
- Age group (<40 vs. ≥40)
Interaction tests will be conducted; significance level α = 0.10

### 6. Missing Data
Primary: Complete case analysis
Sensitivity: Multiple imputation (m=20, PMM method)

### 7. Protocol Deviations
Per-protocol analysis as sensitivity (exclude those with <50% app usage)

### 8. Multiplicity
Secondary outcomes: Report unadjusted p-values; interpret with caution
Subgroups: Exploratory only, not confirmatory

---
Version: 1.0
Date: 2024-01-15
Locked prior to any outcome data collection
```

### Statistical Analysis Plan vs. Analysis Script

| Document | When Written | Contents |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| SAP (prose) | Before data collection | Describes planned analyses in words |
| Analysis script | Before unblinding | Actual code that will be executed |

**Gold standard**: Write and timestamp both before seeing outcomes.

---

## 8. Preregistration

### What Is Preregistration?

Formally documenting your hypotheses, design, and analysis plan in a public, time-stamped repository BEFORE data collection.

### Why Preregister?

| Problem | How Preregistration Helps |
|---------|--------------------------|
| HARKing (Hypothesizing After Results Known) | Hypotheses locked before data seen |
| Outcome switching | Primary outcome documented in advance |
| Selective reporting | All planned analyses on record |
| p-hacking | Analysis decisions made blindly |
| File drawer effect | Registered studies are discoverable |

### Where to Preregister

| Platform | Best For | URL |
|----------|----------|-----|
| OSF Registries | General research | osf.io |
| AsPredicted | Quick, simple format | aspredicted.org |
| ClinicalTrials.gov | Clinical trials (often required) | clinicaltrials.gov |
| PROSPERO | Systematic reviews | crd.york.ac.uk/prospero |
| AEA Registry | Economics | socialscienceregistry.org |

### What to Include

**Minimum requirements**:
```
1. Research questions and hypotheses
2. Study design (experiment? survey? observational?)
3. Planned sample size and stopping rule
4. All measured variables
5. Which variable(s) are primary outcomes
6. Analysis plan for primary hypothesis
7. Any data exclusion criteria
```

**Additional elements**:
```
8. Secondary analyses
9. Exploratory analyses (acknowledged as exploratory)
10. Power analysis justification
11. Data collection timeline
12. Known limitations
```

### Example: OSF Preregistration

```markdown
# Preregistration: Sleep Duration and Cognitive Performance

## Study Information
Title: Effect of Sleep Extension on Working Memory in College Students
Authors: [Blinded for review]
Date: March 1, 2024

## Hypotheses
H1: Participants in the sleep extension condition (8+ hours/night) 
    will score higher on the N-back task than control participants.
    
H2: The effect of sleep extension on N-back performance will be 
    mediated by self-reported alertness.

## Design Plan
**Study type**: Experiment - randomized with two groups
**Blinding**: Single-blind (participants know condition; assessor doesn't)
**Study design**: Between-subjects

## Sampling Plan
**Existing data**: No existing data
**Data collection procedures**: Recruit from introductory psychology
**Sample size**: 128 participants (64 per group)
**Sample size rationale**: Power analysis (d=0.5, α=.05, power=.80)
**Stopping rule**: Fixed sample; will conclude after analyzing 128 completers

## Variables
**Manipulated variable**: Sleep instruction (8+ hrs vs. usual sleep)
**Measured variables**: 
- N-back accuracy (primary DV)
- N-back reaction time (secondary)
- Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (mediator)
- Actigraphy-measured sleep duration (manipulation check)

**Indices**: N-back accuracy = (hits - false alarms) / total trials

## Analysis Plan
**Statistical models**: 
- H1: Independent samples t-test; Cohen's d reported
- H2: Mediation analysis (Hayes PROCESS macro, Model 4, 10000 bootstraps)

**Inference criteria**: α = .05, two-tailed

**Data exclusion**: Exclude if:
- Failed attention checks (>2 errors)
- Actigraphy shows <6 hrs sleep in extension condition
- Prior participation in related study

**Missing data**: Complete case for primary; sensitivity with MI

**Exploratory analyses** (clearly labeled):
- Moderating effect of chronotype
- Dose-response relationship with actual sleep hours
```

### Preregistration Timeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Develop hypothesis and design                                │
│ 2. Write preregistration                         ← Before this  │
│ 3. Submit preregistration (gets timestamp)          deadline    │
│─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ 4. Collect data                                  ← After this   │
│ 5. Analyze per preregistered plan                  point        │
│ 6. Report ALL preregistered analyses                            │
│ 7. Clearly label any non-preregistered analyses as exploratory  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Deviations from Preregistration

Deviations happen—the key is transparency:

```markdown
## Deviations from Preregistration

1. **Sample size**: Collected 118 instead of 128 due to semester end.
   - Sensitivity: Minimum detectable effect is now d=0.53

2. **Exclusion criterion added**: Discovered 3 participants used 
   stimulant medications; excluded post-hoc. Results without 
   exclusion reported in supplement.

3. **Analysis change**: Used Welch's t-test instead of Student's 
   t-test due to unequal variances (Levene's p < .01).
```

## Putting It All Together: Complete Example

### Study: Testing a New Teaching Method

```markdown
# Complete Experimental Design Document

## Research Question
Does interactive problem-based learning (PBL) improve statistics 
exam performance compared to traditional lectures?

## Design: Randomized Controlled Trial with Blocking

### Randomization
- Unit: Students (n = 200)
- Method: Stratified block randomization
  - Stratify by: Prior math courses (0-1 vs. 2+)
  - Block size: 8 within each stratum
- Implementation: Randomization sequence generated in R using 
  set.seed(12345) before recruitment begins

### Blinding
- Students: Cannot be blinded (know their instructional method)
- Graders: Blinded (exams identified by number only)
- Analyst: Blinded (groups coded A/B until analysis complete)

### Blocking
- Factor: Instructor (4 instructors)
- Each instructor teaches one PBL and one traditional section
- This controls for instructor effects

### Factorial Element
- 2 × 2 design crossing:
  - Teaching method (PBL vs. Traditional)
  - Practice tests (Provided vs. Not provided)
- Allows testing of interaction

### Sample Size Justification
- Expected effect size: d = 0.5 (based on meta-analysis)
- α = 0.05, Power = 0.80
- Required n = 64 per cell × 4 cells = 256
- Expect 20% attrition → recruit 320
- Per instructor: 80 students (40 per method)

### Potential Confounders
| Confounder | How Addressed |
|------------|---------------|
| Prior math ability | Stratified randomization |
| Instructor quality | Blocking (each instructor does both) |
| Time of day | Classes randomly assigned to time slots |
| Student motivation | Measured; covariate in analysis |

### Analysis Plan
**Primary analysis**:
2 × 2 ANCOVA
- DV: Final exam score (0-100)
- IVs: Teaching method, Practice tests, Interaction
- Covariate: Prior GPA, Motivation score

**Model**:
Exam ~ Method + PracticeTest + Method:PracticeTest + PriorGPA + Motivation

**Secondary analyses**:
- Instructor random effect (mixed model)
- Per-protocol analysis (attendance ≥ 80%)

### Preregistration
- Platform: OSF
- Date: January 15, 2024
- Link: https://osf.io/xxxxx
- Includes: Hypotheses, design, materials, analysis code
```

## Summary Checklist

Before running any experiment, verify:

### Design
- [ ] Treatments clearly defined
- [ ] Appropriate control condition
- [ ] Randomization method specified
- [ ] Randomization implemented correctly (reproducible)
- [ ] Blinding implemented where possible
- [ ] Blocking used for known sources of variation

### Power
- [ ] Effect size estimate justified
- [ ] Sample size sufficient for 80%+ power
- [ ] Attrition buffer included
- [ ] Stopping rule defined

### Confounding
- [ ] Major confounders identified
- [ ] DAG constructed (optional but helpful)
- [ ] Confounders controlled by design or planned covariates

### Analysis
- [ ] Primary outcome specified
- [ ] Analysis method matches design
- [ ] Multiple comparison strategy defined
- [ ] Missing data approach specified

### Transparency
- [ ] Preregistration completed and timestamped
- [ ] Analysis script written before unblinding
- [ ] Deviation reporting plan in place

## 4. Venture Math: Working Backwards

```
├── Capital for Investment = ~$80M
```

### Single Investment Math

```
THE VC'S CALCULATION
────────────────────

Question: "If I invest $2M, what do I need to believe?"

Step 1: Required Return
         $2M × 10x = $20M exit value (for this investment)

Step 2: Account for Dilution
         Assuming 50% dilution over future rounds:
         $20M ÷ 50% = $40M needed at 20% ownership
         
Step 3: Implied Exit
         $40M ÷ 20% = $200M company exit value

Step 4: Probability Adjustment
         If 20% chance of success:
         $200M ÷ 20% = $1B "expected" exit in success case
         
CONCLUSION: VC needs to believe this could be a 
            $200M-1B outcome to invest $2M
```

### How Dilution Works

```

────────────────────────────────────

Before Series A:                    After Series A:
Founders: 80%                       Founders: 60%    ← Diluted by 25%
Seed Investors: 20%                 Seed: 15%        ← Diluted by 25%
                                    Series A: 25%    ← New money
─────────────                       ─────────────
Total: 100%                         Total: 100%

Formula:
                                           New Shares Issued
Dilution % = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Existing Shares + New Shares Issued

If $5M raised at $15M pre-money ($20M post-money):
Dilution = $5M ÷ $20M = 25%
```

```
│ - $1.5M option pool = $8.5M effective pre-money │
│                                                  │
│ $8.5M + $2.5M = $11M post-money                 │
│ Investor gets: $2.5M ÷ $11M = 22.7%             │
│                                                  │
```

```
SAFE MECHANICS (Simple Agreement for Future Equity)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Key Terms:
├── Valuation Cap: Maximum price for conversion
├── Discount: % off next round price (typically 15-25%)
└── MFN: Most Favored Nation (match better terms)

CONVERSION EXAMPLE:

SAFE Terms: $5M cap, 20% discount
Series A: $10M pre-money, $1.00/share

Conversion Price = LOWER OF:
├── Cap: $5M ÷ 10M shares = $0.50/share
└── Discount: $1.00 × (1-20%) = $0.80/share

SAFE converts at $0.50/share (cap applies)

$500K SAFE → 1,000,000 shares
vs. Series A investors who get 500,000 shares at $1.00
```

## Quick Reference Formulas

```
────────────────────────

Post-Money = Pre-Money + Investment

Ownership % = Investment ÷ Post-Money

Effective Pre-Money = Headline Pre-Money - Option Pool Value

Dilution = New Shares ÷ (Old Shares + New Shares)

Future Ownership = Current % × (1 - Dilution₁) × (1 - Dilution₂) × ...

Shares Issued = Investment ÷ Price Per Share

Price Per Share = Pre-Money ÷ Pre-Money Shares Outstanding
```

## Understanding Growth Loops

### What Are Growth Loops?

Growth loops are self-reinforcing systems where the output of one cycle becomes the input for the next, creating compounding growth.

```python
    OUTPUT = "output"
    DISTRIBUTION = "distribution"

@dataclass
class LoopStage:
    """Individual stage in a growth loop"""
    id: str
    name: str
    stage_type: StageType
    description: str
    conversion_rate: float = 0.0
    time_to_complete: timedelta = timedelta(hours=0)
    
    # Metrics for this stage
    primary_metric: str = ""
    secondary_metrics: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    # Dependencies
    prerequisites: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    blockers: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    # Optimization levers
    optimization_levers: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

@dataclass
class GrowthLoop:
    """Complete growth loop definition"""
    id: str
    name: str
    loop_type: LoopType
    description: str
    stages: List[LoopStage]
    
    # Loop characteristics
    cycle_time: timedelta = timedelta(days=7)
    k_factor: float = 0.0  # Viral coefficient
    retention_rate: float = 0.0
    
    # Business impact
    revenue_per_cycle: float = 0.0
    cost_per_cycle: float = 0.0
    
    def calculate_loop_efficiency(self) -> float:
        """Calculate overall loop conversion efficiency"""
        efficiency = 1.0
        for stage in self.stages:
            efficiency *= stage.conversion_rate
        return efficiency
    
    def calculate_payback_cycles(self, cac: float) -> int:
        """Calculate cycles needed to payback CAC"""
        net_revenue = self.revenue_per_cycle - self.cost_per_cycle
        if net_revenue <= 0:
            return -1  # Never pays back
        return int(cac / net_revenue) + 1
    
    def project_growth(self, initial_users: int, cycles: int) -> List[int]:
        """Project user growth over multiple cycles"""
        users = [initial_users]
        for _ in range(cycles):
            new_users = int(users[-1] * self.k_factor * self.retention_rate)
            users.append(users[-1] + new_users)
        return users
```
