## 4. Distributed Tracing

### OpenTelemetry Tracing Setup

```typescript
// src/observability/tracing/tracer.ts
import { NodeSDK } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-node';
import { getNodeAutoInstrumentations } from '@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node';
import { OTLPTraceExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http';
import { OTLPMetricExporter } from '@opentelemetry/exporter-metrics-otlp-http';
import { Resource } from '@opentelemetry/resources';
import { SemanticResourceAttributes } from '@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions';
import { 
  BatchSpanProcessor, 
  ConsoleSpanExporter,
  SimpleSpanProcessor 
} from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base';
import { 
  PeriodicExportingMetricReader,
  ConsoleMetricExporter 
} from '@opentelemetry/sdk-metrics';
import { 
  trace, 
  context, 
  SpanKind, 
  SpanStatusCode,
  Span,
  Tracer,
  propagation,
  Context,
} from '@opentelemetry/api';
import { W3CTraceContextPropagator } from '@opentelemetry/core';
import { 
  ParentBasedSampler,
  TraceIdRatioBasedSampler,
  AlwaysOnSampler,
  AlwaysOffSampler,
} from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base';

export interface TracingConfig {
  serviceName: string;
  serviceVersion: string;
  environment: string;
  otlpEndpoint?: string;
  samplingRatio?: number;
  enableConsoleExport?: boolean;
}

export class TracingManager {
  private sdk: NodeSDK;
  private tracer: Tracer;
  private config: TracingConfig;

  constructor(config: TracingConfig) {
    this.config = config;
    
    // Create resource
    const resource = new Resource({
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_NAME]: config.serviceName,
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_VERSION]: config.serviceVersion,
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT]: config.environment,
      [SemanticResourceAttributes.SERVICE_INSTANCE_ID]: process.env.HOSTNAME || 'local',
    });

    // Configure sampler
    const sampler = this.createSampler(config.samplingRatio);

    // Configure trace exporter
    const traceExporter = config.otlpEndpoint
      ? new OTLPTraceExporter({ url: `${config.otlpEndpoint}/v1/traces` })
      : new ConsoleSpanExporter();

    // Configure metric exporter
    const metricExporter = config.otlpEndpoint
      ? new OTLPMetricExporter({ url: `${config.otlpEndpoint}/v1/metrics` })
      : new ConsoleMetricExporter();

    // Initialize SDK
    this.sdk = new NodeSDK({
      resource,
      traceExporter,
      metricReader: new PeriodicExportingMetricReader({
        exporter: metricExporter,
        exportIntervalMillis: 60000,
      }),
      sampler,
      instrumentations: [
        getNodeAutoInstrumentations({
          '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http': {
            requestHook: (span, request) => {
              span.setAttribute('http.request_id', request.headers?.['x-request-id'] || '');
            },
          },
          '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-express': {
            enabled: true,
          },
          '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-pg': {
            enabled: true,
            enhancedDatabaseReporting: true,
          },
          '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-redis': {
            enabled: true,
          },
          '@opentelemetry/instrumentation-mongodb': {
            enabled: true,
          },
        }),
      ],
    });

    // Set up propagation
    propagation.setGlobalPropagator(new W3CTraceContextPropagator());

    this.tracer = trace.getTracer(config.serviceName, config.serviceVersion);
  }

  private createSampler(ratio?: number) {
    if (ratio === undefined || ratio === 1) {
      return new AlwaysOnSampler();
    }
    if (ratio === 0) {
      return new AlwaysOffSampler();
    }
    
    return new ParentBasedSampler({
      root: new TraceIdRatioBasedSampler(ratio),
    });
  }

  async start(): Promise<void> {
    await this.sdk.start();
    console.log('Tracing initialized');
  }

  async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
    await this.sdk.shutdown();
    console.log('Tracing shutdown');
  }

  getTracer(): Tracer {
    return this.tracer;
  }

  // Create a new span
  startSpan(
    name: string,
    options?: {
      kind?: SpanKind;
      attributes?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
      parent?: Context;
    }
  ): Span {
    const spanOptions = {
      kind: options?.kind || SpanKind.INTERNAL,
      attributes: options?.attributes,
    };

    const parentContext = options?.parent || context.active();
    return this.tracer.startSpan(name, spanOptions, parentContext);
  }

  // Execute function within a span
  async withSpan<T>(
    name: string,
    fn: (span: Span) => Promise<T>,
    options?: {
      kind?: SpanKind;
      attributes?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
    }
  ): Promise<T> {
    const span = this.startSpan(name, options);
    
    return context.with(trace.setSpan(context.active(), span), async () => {
      try {
        const result = await fn(span);
        span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
        return result;
      } catch (error) {
        span.setStatus({
          code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
          message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
        });
        
        if (error instanceof Error) {
          span.recordException(error);
        }
        
        throw error;
      } finally {
        span.end();
      }
    });
  }

  // Add event to current span
  addEvent(name: string, attributes?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): void {
    const span = trace.getActiveSpan();
    if (span) {
      span.addEvent(name, attributes);
    }
  }

  // Set attribute on current span
  setAttribute(key: string, value: string | number | boolean): void {
    const span = trace.getActiveSpan();
    if (span) {
      span.setAttribute(key, value);
    }
  }

  // Get current trace context for propagation
  getCurrentTraceContext(): { traceId: string; spanId: string } | null {
    const span = trace.getActiveSpan();
    if (!span) return null;
    
    const spanContext = span.spanContext();
    return {
      traceId: spanContext.traceId,
      spanId: spanContext.spanId,
    };
  }

  // Extract trace context from headers
  extractContext(headers: Record<string, string>): Context {
    return propagation.extract(context.active(), headers);
  }

  // Inject trace context into headers
  injectContext(headers: Record<string, string>): void {
    propagation.inject(context.active(), headers);
  }
}

// Decorator for automatic tracing
export function Trace(
  name?: string,
  options?: { kind?: SpanKind; attributes?: Record<string, string | number | boolean> }
) {
  return function (
    target: any,
    propertyKey: string,
    descriptor: PropertyDescriptor
  ) {
    const originalMethod = descriptor.value;
    const spanName = name || `${target.constructor.name}.${propertyKey}`;

    descriptor.value = async function (...args: any[]) {
      const tracer = trace.getTracer('decorator-tracer');
      const span = tracer.startSpan(spanName, {
        kind: options?.kind || SpanKind.INTERNAL,
        attributes: options?.attributes,
      });

      return context.with(trace.setSpan(context.active(), span), async () => {
        try {
          const result = await originalMethod.apply(this, args);
          span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
          return result;
        } catch (error) {
          span.setStatus({
            code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
            message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
          });
          if (error instanceof Error) {
            span.recordException(error);
          }
          throw error;
        } finally {
          span.end();
        }
      });
    };

    return descriptor;
  };
}

  private filter: (span: ReadableSpan) => boolean;

// Processor that captures error spans for alerting
export class ErrorCapturingProcessor implements SpanProcessor {
  private errors: Array<{
    traceId: string;
    spanId: string;
    name: string;
    error: string;
    timestamp: Date;
  }> = [];
  private maxErrors: number;
  private onError?: (error: any) => void;

  constructor(options: { maxErrors?: number; onError?: (error: any) => void } = {}) {
    this.maxErrors = options.maxErrors || 100;
    this.onError = options.onError;
  }

  onStart(span: Span, parentContext: Context): void {
    // No-op
  }

  onEnd(span: ReadableSpan): void {
    if (span.status.code === 2) { // ERROR status
      const errorInfo = {
        traceId: span.spanContext().traceId,
        spanId: span.spanContext().spanId,
        name: span.name,
        error: span.status.message || 'Unknown error',
        timestamp: new Date(),
      };

      this.errors.push(errorInfo);
      
      if (this.errors.length > this.maxErrors) {
        this.errors.shift();
      }

      if (this.onError) {
        this.onError(errorInfo);
      }
    }
  }

  getRecentErrors(): typeof this.errors {
    return [...this.errors];
  }

  shutdown(): Promise<void> {
    return Promise.resolve();
  }

  forceFlush(): Promise<void> {
    return Promise.resolve();
  }
}

// Create optimized batch processor with filtering
export function createOptimizedSpanProcessor(
  exporter: SpanExporter,
  options: {
    excludeHealthChecks?: boolean;
    excludeStaticAssets?: boolean;
    excludeShortSpans?: boolean;
    minDurationMs?: number;
  } = {}
): SpanProcessor {
  const batchProcessor = new BatchSpanProcessor(exporter, {
    maxQueueSize: 2048,
    maxExportBatchSize: 512,
    scheduledDelayMillis: 5000,
    exportTimeoutMillis: 30000,
  });

  const filter = (span: ReadableSpan): boolean => {
    const name = span.name.toLowerCase();
    const attributes = span.attributes;

    // Exclude health check spans
    if (options.excludeHealthChecks) {
      if (
        name.includes('health') ||
        name.includes('ready') ||
        name.includes('alive') ||
        attributes['http.route'] === '/health' ||
        attributes['http.route'] === '/ready'
      ) {
        return false;
      }
    }

    // Exclude static asset spans
    if (options.excludeStaticAssets) {
      const route = attributes['http.route'] as string;
      if (
        route?.startsWith('/static') ||
        route?.startsWith('/assets') ||
        /\.(js|css|png|jpg|gif|ico|woff|woff2)$/.test(route || '')
      ) {
        return false;
      }
    }

    // Exclude very short spans
    if (options.excludeShortSpans) {
      const durationMs = span.duration[0] * 1000 + span.duration[1] / 1000000;
      if (durationMs < (options.minDurationMs || 1)) {
        return false;
      }
    }

    return true;
  };

  return new FilteringSpanProcessor(batchProcessor, filter);
}

// Dashboard-ready aggregations
export class SignalAggregator {
  // Calculate error budget consumption
  static calculateErrorBudget(
    errorRate: number,
    slo: number,
    windowDays: number = 30
  ): {
    budgetTotal: number;
    budgetConsumed: number;
    budgetRemaining: number;
    burnRate: number;
  } {
    // Error budget = 1 - SLO
    // e.g., 99.9% SLO = 0.1% error budget
    const budgetTotal = 1 - slo;
    const budgetConsumed = errorRate;
    const budgetRemaining = Math.max(0, budgetTotal - budgetConsumed);
    
    // Burn rate: how fast are we consuming the budget
    // 1.0 = sustainable, >1.0 = burning faster than allowed
    const burnRate = budgetTotal > 0 ? budgetConsumed / budgetTotal : 0;

    return {
      budgetTotal,
      budgetConsumed,
      budgetRemaining,
      burnRate,
    };
  }

  // Apdex score calculation
  static calculateApdex(
    satisfiedCount: number,
    toleratingCount: number,
    frustratedCount: number
  ): number {
    const total = satisfiedCount + toleratingCount + frustratedCount;
    if (total === 0) return 1;
    
    // Apdex = (Satisfied + Tolerating/2) / Total
    return (satisfiedCount + toleratingCount / 2) / total;
  }

  // Calculate availability
  static calculateAvailability(
    totalRequests: number,
    successfulRequests: number
  ): number {
    if (totalRequests === 0) return 1;
    return successfulRequests / totalRequests;
  }
}

## 6. Instrumentation Strategies

### Auto-Instrumentation Wrapper

```typescript
// src/observability/instrumentation/auto-instrument.ts
import { trace, SpanKind, SpanStatusCode, Span, context } from '@opentelemetry/api';
import { metrics } from '../metrics/collector';
import { log } from '../logging/logger';

type AnyFunction = (...args: any[]) => any;
type AsyncFunction = (...args: any[]) => Promise<any>;

// Method decorator for automatic instrumentation
export function Instrument(options: {
  name?: string;
  kind?: SpanKind;
  recordMetrics?: boolean;
  logArgs?: boolean;
  logResult?: boolean;
  errorHandler?: (error: Error, span: Span) => void;
} = {}) {
  return function (
    target: any,
    propertyKey: string,
    descriptor: PropertyDescriptor
  ) {
    const originalMethod = descriptor.value;
    const className = target.constructor.name;
    const methodName = options.name || `${className}.${propertyKey}`;

    descriptor.value = async function (...args: any[]) {
      const tracer = trace.getTracer('auto-instrumentation');
      
      const span = tracer.startSpan(methodName, {
        kind: options.kind || SpanKind.INTERNAL,
        attributes: {
          'code.function': propertyKey,
          'code.namespace': className,
        },
      });

      const startTime = Date.now();

      // Log method entry
      if (options.logArgs) {
        log.debug(`Entering ${methodName}`, {
          args: args.map((arg, i) => ({
            [`arg${i}`]: typeof arg === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(arg).slice(0, 100) : arg,
          })),
        });
      }

      return context.with(trace.setSpan(context.active(), span), async () => {
        try {
          const result = await originalMethod.apply(this, args);
          
          span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
          
          // Log method exit
          if (options.logResult) {
            log.debug(`Exiting ${methodName}`, {
              result: typeof result === 'object' 
                ? JSON.stringify(result).slice(0, 100) 
                : result,
            });
          }

          // Record metrics
          if (options.recordMetrics) {
            const duration = (Date.now() - startTime) / 1000;
            metrics.httpRequestDuration.observe(
              { method: 'INTERNAL', route: methodName, status_code: '200' },
              duration
            );
          }

          return result;
        } catch (error) {
          span.setStatus({
            code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
            message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
          });

          if (error instanceof Error) {
            span.recordException(error);
            
            if (options.errorHandler) {
              options.errorHandler(error, span);
            }
          }

          // Record error metrics
          if (options.recordMetrics) {
            metrics.dbQueryErrors.inc({
              operation: methodName,
              table: 'N/A',
              error_type: error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'Unknown',
            });
          }

          throw error;
        } finally {
          span.end();
        }
      });
    };

    return descriptor;
  };
}

// Class decorator for instrumenting all methods
export function InstrumentClass(options: {
  prefix?: string;
  excludeMethods?: string[];
  includePrivate?: boolean;
} = {}) {
  return function <T extends { new (...args: any[]): {} }>(constructor: T) {
    const prototype = constructor.prototype;
    const methodNames = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(prototype).filter(
      name => name !== 'constructor' && typeof prototype[name] === 'function'
    );

    for (const methodName of methodNames) {
      // Skip excluded methods
      if (options.excludeMethods?.includes(methodName)) continue;
      
      // Skip private methods unless included
      if (!options.includePrivate && methodName.startsWith('_')) continue;

      const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(prototype, methodName);
      if (!descriptor) continue;

      const instrumentedDescriptor = Instrument({
        name: options.prefix ? `${options.prefix}.${methodName}` : undefined,
        recordMetrics: true,
      })(prototype, methodName, descriptor);

      Object.defineProperty(prototype, methodName, instrumentedDescriptor);
    }

    return constructor;
  };
}

// Database query instrumentation
export function instrumentDatabase<T extends object>(
  db: T,
  options: {
    dbType: string;
    host?: string;
    port?: number;
    database?: string;
  }
): T {
  const tracer = trace.getTracer('database-instrumentation');

  return new Proxy(db, {
    get(target: any, prop: string) {
      const original = target[prop];
      
      if (typeof original !== 'function') {
        return original;
      }

      // Instrument query methods
      if (['query', 'execute', 'run', 'find', 'findOne', 'insert', 'update', 'delete'].includes(prop)) {
        return async function (...args: any[]) {
          const span = tracer.startSpan(`${options.dbType}.${prop}`, {
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,
            attributes: {
              'db.system': options.dbType,
              'db.name': options.database,
              'net.peer.name': options.host,
              'net.peer.port': options.port,
              'db.operation': prop,
            },
          });

          // Add query as attribute (sanitized)
          if (typeof args[0] === 'string') {
            span.setAttribute('db.statement', sanitizeQuery(args[0]));
          }

          const timer = metrics.dbQueryDuration.startTimer({
            operation: prop,
            table: extractTableName(args[0]),
            status: 'pending',
          });

          try {
            const result = await original.apply(target, args);
            span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
            timer({ status: 'success' });
            return result;
          } catch (error) {
            span.setStatus({
              code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
              message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
            });
            
            if (error instanceof Error) {
              span.recordException(error);
            }
            
            timer({ status: 'error' });
            
            metrics.dbQueryErrors.inc({
              operation: prop,
              table: extractTableName(args[0]),
              error_type: error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'Unknown',
            });
            
            throw error;
          } finally {
            span.end();
          }
        };
      }

      return original.bind(target);
    },
  });
}

// HTTP client instrumentation
export function instrumentHttpClient<T extends object>(
  client: T,
  options: { serviceName: string }
): T {
  const tracer = trace.getTracer('http-client-instrumentation');

  return new Proxy(client, {
    get(target: any, prop: string) {
      const original = target[prop];
      
      if (typeof original !== 'function') {
        return original;
      }

      // Instrument HTTP methods
      if (['get', 'post', 'put', 'patch', 'delete', 'request'].includes(prop)) {
        return async function (...args: any[]) {
          const url = typeof args[0] === 'string' ? args[0] : args[0]?.url;
          const method = prop === 'request' ? args[0]?.method || 'GET' : prop.toUpperCase();
          
          const span = tracer.startSpan(`HTTP ${method}`, {
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,
            attributes: {
              'http.method': method,
              'http.url': url,
              'peer.service': options.serviceName,
            },
          });

          const timer = metrics.externalRequestDuration.startTimer({
            service: options.serviceName,
            endpoint: extractEndpoint(url),
            method,
            status_code: 'pending',
          });

          // Inject trace context into headers
          const headers: Record<string, string> = {};
          trace.getActiveSpan()?.spanContext();
          // propagation.inject would be used here

          try {
            const result = await original.apply(target, args);
            const statusCode = result.status || result.statusCode || 200;
            
            span.setAttribute('http.status_code', statusCode);
            span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
            timer({ status_code: statusCode.toString() });
            
            return result;
          } catch (error) {
            span.setStatus({
              code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
              message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error',
            });
            
            if (error instanceof Error) {
              span.recordException(error);
            }

            timer({ status_code: 'error' });
            
            metrics.externalRequestErrors.inc({
              service: options.serviceName,
              endpoint: extractEndpoint(url),
              error_type: error instanceof Error ? error.name : 'Unknown',
            });
            
            throw error;
          } finally {
            span.end();
          }
        };
      }

      return original.bind(target);
    },
  });
}

// Helper functions
function sanitizeQuery(query: string): string {
  // Remove sensitive data from queries
  return query
    .replace(/password\s*=\s*'[^']*'/gi, "password='***'")
    .replace(/secret\s*=\s*'[^']*'/gi, "secret='***'")
    .slice(0, 1000);
}

function extractTableName(query: any): string {
  if (typeof query !== 'string') return 'unknown';
  
  const match = query.match(/(?:FROM|INTO|UPDATE|TABLE)\s+([^\s,;()]+)/i);
  return match ? match[1].replace(/[`"[\]]/g, '') : 'unknown';
}

function extractEndpoint(url: string): string {
  try {
    const parsed = new URL(url);
    return parsed.pathname;
  } catch {
    return url.split('?')[0];
  }
}

## 7. Sampling Techniques

```typescript
// src/observability/sampling/sampler.ts
import {
  Sampler,
  SamplingDecision,
  SamplingResult,
  SpanKind,
  Attributes,
  Context,
  Link,
} from '@opentelemetry/api';
import { log } from '../logging/logger';

// Rate-limiting sampler with adaptive rate
export class AdaptiveRateLimitingSampler implements Sampler {
  private maxTracesPerSecond: number;
  private currentCount: number;
  private lastReset: number;
  private targetErrorRate: number;
  private recentErrors: number;
  private recentTotal: number;

  constructor(options: {
    maxTracesPerSecond: number;
    targetErrorRate?: number;
  }) {
    this.maxTracesPerSecond = options.maxTracesPerSecond;
    this.targetErrorRate = options.targetErrorRate || 0.01;
    this.currentCount = 0;
    this.lastReset = Date.now();
    this.recentErrors = 0;
    this.recentTotal = 0;
  }

  shouldSample(
    context: Context,
    traceId: string,
    spanName: string,
    spanKind: SpanKind,
    attributes: Attributes,
    links: Link[]
  ): SamplingResult {
    const now = Date.now();
    
    // Reset counter every second
    if (now - this.lastReset > 1000) {
      this.currentCount = 0;
      this.lastReset = now;
    }

    // Always sample if under rate limit
    if (this.currentCount < this.maxTracesPerSecond) {
      this.currentCount++;
      return {
        decision: SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED,
        attributes: {
          'sampling.rate': this.maxTracesPerSecond,
          'sampling.decision': 'rate_limited',
        },
      };
    }

    // Sample based on error rate if over limit
    // Increase sampling when errors are higher than target
    const currentErrorRate = this.recentTotal > 0 
      ? this.recentErrors / this.recentTotal 
      : 0;
    
    if (currentErrorRate > this.targetErrorRate) {
      return {
        decision: SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED,
        attributes: {
          'sampling.decision': 'error_rate_boost',
        },
      };
    }

    return {
      decision: SamplingDecision.NOT_RECORD,
      attributes: {},
    };
  }

  toString(): string {
    return `AdaptiveRateLimitingSampler{maxTracesPerSecond=${this.maxTracesPerSecond}}`;
  }

  recordError(): void {
    this.recentErrors++;
    this.recentTotal++;
    
    // Keep sliding window
    if (this.recentTotal > 1000) {
      this.recentErrors = Math.floor(this.recentErrors / 2);
      this.recentTotal = Math.floor(this.recentTotal / 2);
    }
  }

  recordSuccess(): void {
    this.recentTotal++;
    
    if (this.recentTotal > 1000) {
      this.recentErrors = Math.floor(this.recentErrors / 2);
      this.recentTotal = Math.floor(this.recentTotal / 2);
    }
  }
}

// Priority-based sampler
export class PrioritySampler implements Sampler {
  private config: {
    highPriorityPaths: string[];
    lowPriorityPaths: string[];
    defaultSamplingRate: number;
    highPrioritySamplingRate: number;
    lowPrioritySamplingRate: number;
  };

  constructor(config: Partial<typeof PrioritySampler.prototype.config> = {}) {
    this.config = {
      highPriorityPaths: config.highPriorityPaths || ['/api/payments', '/api/orders'],
      lowPriorityPaths: config.lowPriorityPaths || ['/health', '/metrics', '/static'],
      defaultSamplingRate: config.defaultSamplingRate || 0.1,
      highPrioritySamplingRate: config.highPrioritySamplingRate || 1.0,
      lowPrioritySamplingRate: config.lowPrioritySamplingRate || 0.01,
    };
  }

  shouldSample(
    context: Context,
    traceId: string,
    spanName: string,
    spanKind: SpanKind,
    attributes: Attributes,
    links: Link[]
  ): SamplingResult {
    const path = attributes['http.route'] as string || attributes['http.url'] as string || spanName;
    
    let samplingRate: number;
    let priority: string;

    // Check high priority paths
    if (this.config.highPriorityPaths.some(p => path.includes(p))) {
      samplingRate = this.config.highPrioritySamplingRate;
      priority = 'high';
    }
    // Check low priority paths
    else if (this.config.lowPriorityPaths.some(p => path.includes(p))) {
      samplingRate = this.config.lowPrioritySamplingRate;
      priority = 'low';
    }
    // Default rate
    else {
      samplingRate = this.config.defaultSamplingRate;
      priority = 'default';
    }

    // Use trace ID for consistent sampling
    const hash = this.hashTraceId(traceId);
    const shouldSample = hash < samplingRate;

    return {
      decision: shouldSample 
        ? SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED 
        : SamplingDecision.NOT_RECORD,
      attributes: {
        'sampling.priority': priority,
        'sampling.rate': samplingRate,
      },
    };
  }

  private hashTraceId(traceId: string): number {
    // Simple hash to get consistent sampling decision
    let hash = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < traceId.length; i++) {
      hash = ((hash << 5) - hash) + traceId.charCodeAt(i);
      hash = hash & hash;
    }
    return Math.abs(hash) / 2147483647; // Normalize to 0-1
  }

  toString(): string {
    return 'PrioritySampler';
  }
}

// Error-based sampler - always sample errors
export class ErrorBasedSampler implements Sampler {
  private baseSampler: Sampler;

  constructor(baseSampler: Sampler) {
    this.baseSampler = baseSampler;
  }

  shouldSample(
    context: Context,
    traceId: string,
    spanName: string,
    spanKind: SpanKind,
    attributes: Attributes,
    links: Link[]
  ): SamplingResult {
    // Always sample if there's an error indicator
    const statusCode = attributes['http.status_code'] as number;
    if (statusCode && statusCode >= 400) {
      return {
        decision: SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED,
        attributes: {
          'sampling.decision': 'error_always_sample',
        },
      };
    }

    // Check for error attribute
    if (attributes['error'] === true) {
      return {
        decision: SamplingDecision.RECORD_AND_SAMPLED,
        attributes: {
          'sampling.decision': 'error_always_sample',
        },
      };
    }

    // Delegate to base sampler
    return this.baseSampler.shouldSample(
      context,
      traceId,
      spanName,
      spanKind,
      attributes,
      links
    );
  }

  toString(): string {
    return `ErrorBasedSampler{base=${this.baseSampler.toString()}}`;
  }
}

// Tail-based sampling decision recorder
export class TailSamplingDecisionRecorder {
  private decisions: Map<string, {
    decision: boolean;
    reason: string;
    timestamp: number;
    spans: Array<{
      name: string;
      duration: number;
      status: string;
    }>;
  }>;
  private maxSize: number;
  private ttlMs: number;

  constructor(options: { maxSize?: number; ttlMs?: number } = {}) {
    this.decisions = new Map();
    this.maxSize = options.maxSize || 10000;
    this.ttlMs = options.ttlMs || 60000;
  }

  // Record span for potential tail sampling
  recordSpan(
    traceId: string,
    spanName: string,
    duration: number,
    status: string,
    isError: boolean
  ): void {
    let decision = this.decisions.get(traceId);
    
    if (!decision) {
      decision = {
        decision: false,
        reason: 'pending',
        timestamp: Date.now(),
        spans: [],
      };
      this.decisions.set(traceId, decision);
    }

    decision.spans.push({ name: spanName, duration, status });

    // Decide if this trace should be sampled
    if (isError) {
      decision.decision = true;
      decision.reason = 'error';
    } else if (duration > 5000) {
      decision.decision = true;
      decision.reason = 'slow_request';
    }

    this.cleanup();
  }

  // Get sampling decision for a trace
  getDecision(traceId: string): { shouldSample: boolean; reason: string } | null {
    const decision = this.decisions.get(traceId);
    if (!decision) return null;

    return {
      shouldSample: decision.decision,
      reason: decision.reason,
    };
  }

  // Finalize decision for a trace
  finalizeDecision(traceId: string): { shouldSample: boolean; reason: string } {
    const decision = this.decisions.get(traceId);
    
    if (!decision) {
      return { shouldSample: false, reason: 'no_data' };
    }

    // Apply final decision logic
    const totalDuration = decision.spans.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.duration, 0);
    const hasErrors = decision.spans.some(s => s.status === 'error');

    if (hasErrors) {
      return { shouldSample: true, reason: 'has_errors' };
    }

    if (totalDuration > 10000) {
      return { shouldSample: true, reason: 'slow_trace' };
    }

    if (decision.spans.length > 50) {
      return { shouldSample: true, reason: 'complex_trace' };
    }

    // Random sample for other traces
    const sampleRate = 0.1;
    if (Math.random() < sampleRate) {
      return { shouldSample: true, reason: 'random_sample' };
    }

    return { shouldSample: false, reason: 'not_interesting' };
  }

  private cleanup(): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    
    // Remove old entries
    for (const [traceId, decision] of this.decisions.entries()) {
      if (now - decision.timestamp > this.ttlMs) {
        this.decisions.delete(traceId);
      }
    }

    // Remove excess entries
    while (this.decisions.size > this.maxSize) {
      const firstKey = this.decisions.keys().next().value;
      this.decisions.delete(firstKey);
    }
  }
}

  gridPos: { h: number; w: number; x: number; y: number };
  targets?: Array<{
    expr: string;
    legendFormat?: string;
    format?: string;
  }>;
  fieldConfig?: any;
  options?: any;
}

export interface Dashboard {
  title: string;
  uid: string;
  tags: string[];
  refresh: string;
  panels: Panel[];
  templating?: {
    list: Array<{
      name: string;
      type: string;
      query?: string;
      datasource?: string;
    }>;
  };
}

export class DashboardBuilder {
  private dashboard: Dashboard;
  private currentY: number = 0;

  constructor(title: string, uid: string) {
    this.dashboard = {
      title,
      uid,
      tags: [],
      refresh: '30s',
      panels: [],
      templating: { list: [] },
    };
  }

  addTag(tag: string): this {
    this.dashboard.tags.push(tag);
    return this;
  }

  addVariable(name: string, query: string, datasource: string = 'Prometheus'): this {
    this.dashboard.templating!.list.push({
      name,
      type: 'query',
      query,
      datasource,
    });
    return this;
  }

  addRow(title: string): this {
    this.dashboard.panels.push({
      title,
      type: 'row',
      gridPos: { h: 1, w: 24, x: 0, y: this.currentY },
    });
    this.currentY += 1;
    return this;
  }

  addStatPanel(
    title: string,
    expr: string,
    options: {
      unit?: string;
      thresholds?: Array<{ color: string; value: number | null }>;
      width?: number;
    } = {}
  ): this {
    const width = options.width || 6;
    this.dashboard.panels.push({
      title,
      type: 'stat',
      gridPos: { h: 4, w: width, x: this.getNextX(width), y: this.currentY },
      targets: [{ expr, legendFormat: title }],
      fieldConfig: {
        defaults: {
          unit: options.unit || 'short',
          thresholds: {
            mode: 'absolute',
            steps: options.thresholds || [{ color: 'green', value: null }],
          },
        },
      },
    });
    return this;
  }

  addTimeSeriesPanel(
    title: string,
    targets: Array<{ expr: string; legendFormat: string }>,
    options: {
      height?: number;
      width?: number;
      unit?: string;
      stacking?: boolean;
    } = {}
  ): this {
    const width = options.width || 12;
    const height = options.height || 8;
    
    this.currentY = this.getNextRowY();
    
    this.dashboard.panels.push({
      title,
      type: 'timeseries',
      gridPos: { h: height, w: width, x: this.getNextX(width), y: this.currentY },
      targets,
      fieldConfig: {
        defaults: {
          unit: options.unit,
          custom: options.stacking ? { stacking: { mode: 'normal' } } : {},
        },
      },
    });
    return this;
  }

  addHeatmapPanel(
    title: string,
    expr: string,
    options: { width?: number; height?: number } = {}
  ): this {
    const width = options.width || 12;
    const height = options.height || 8;
    
    this.dashboard.panels.push({
      title,
      type: 'heatmap',
      gridPos: { h: height, w: width, x: this.getNextX(width), y: this.currentY },
      targets: [{ expr, format: 'heatmap', legendFormat: '{{le}}' }],
      options: { calculate: false },
    });
    return this;
  }

  private getNextX(width: number): number {
    // Simple layout: stack panels horizontally then vertically
    const lastPanel = this.dashboard.panels[this.dashboard.panels.length - 1];
    if (!lastPanel || lastPanel.type === 'row') return 0;
    
    const nextX = (lastPanel.gridPos.x + lastPanel.gridPos.w) % 24;
    if (nextX + width > 24) {
      this.currentY = lastPanel.gridPos.y + lastPanel.gridPos.h;
      return 0;
    }
    return nextX;
  }

  private getNextRowY(): number {
    const lastPanel = this.dashboard.panels[this.dashboard.panels.length - 1];
    if (!lastPanel) return 0;
    return lastPanel.gridPos.y + lastPanel.gridPos.h;
  }

  build(): Dashboard {
    return this.dashboard;
  }
}

// Usage example
export function createServiceDashboard(serviceName: string): Dashboard {
  return new DashboardBuilder(`${serviceName} Observability`, `${serviceName}-obs`)
    .addTag('production')
    .addTag('sre')
    .addVariable('service', `label_values(http_requests_total, service)`)
    .addVariable('environment', `label_values(http_requests_total, environment)`)
    
    // Overview row
    .addRow('⚡ Service Overview')
    .addStatPanel('Request Rate', 
      'sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="$service"}[5m]))',
      { unit: 'reqps', thresholds: [
        { color: 'green', value: null },
        { color: 'yellow', value: 1000 },
        { color: 'red', value: 5000 },
      ]})
    .addStatPanel('Error Rate',
      'sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="$service",status_code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="$service"}[5m])) * 100',
      { unit: 'percent', thresholds: [
        { color: 'green', value: null },
        { color: 'yellow', value: 1 },
        { color: 'red', value: 5 },
      ]})
    .addStatPanel('P99 Latency',
      'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="$service"}[5m])) by (le))',
      { unit: 's', thresholds: [
        { color: 'green', value: null },
        { color: 'yellow', value: 0.5 },
        { color: 'red', value: 1 },
      ]})
    .addStatPanel('Availability',
      '(1 - (sum(increase(http_requests_total{service="$service",status_code=~"5.."}[30d])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total{service="$service"}[30d])))) * 100',
      { unit: 'percent' })
    
    // Golden signals
    .addRow('📊 Golden Signals')
    .addHeatmapPanel('Latency Distribution',
      'sum(increase(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="$service"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)')
    .addTimeSeriesPanel('Traffic by Endpoint', [
      { expr: 'sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="$service"}[$__rate_interval])) by (route)', legendFormat: '{{route}}' }
    ])
    
    .build();
}

## 3. Lifestyle Therapy (Foundation of Treatment)

### Dietary Intervention

**Caloric Goals:**
- Deficit: 500–750 kcal/day → ~0.5–0.75 kg/week loss
- Women: 1,200–1,500 kcal/day
- Men: 1,500–1,800 kcal/day

**Acceptable Dietary Patterns:**
| Diet | Key Features |
|------|--------------|
| Mediterranean | Olive oil, fish, vegetables, moderate wine |
| DASH | Low sodium, fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy |
| Low-carbohydrate | <130 g carbs/day; effective for T2DM |
| Low-fat | <30% calories from fat |
| Intermittent fasting | Time-restricted eating (16:8, 5:2) |
| Very low-calorie diet (VLCD) | 800 kcal/day; medically supervised only |

**Key Principles:**
- Reduce ultra-processed foods and added sugars
- Eliminate sugar-sweetened beverages
- Increase fiber and vegetables
- Regular meal timing
- Mindful eating practices

### Physical Activity

| Phase | Recommendation |
|-------|----------------|
| Initial | 150 min/week moderate aerobic activity |
| Weight maintenance | 200–300 min/week |
| Resistance training | 2–3 sessions/week |
| Sedentary behavior | Break up prolonged sitting |

*Tailor to physical limitations; any activity is beneficial*

### Behavioral Therapy

**Core Components:**
- **Self-monitoring:** Food diaries, weight tracking, activity logs
- **Goal setting:** SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound)
- **Stimulus control:** Modify environment to reduce triggers
- **Cognitive restructuring:** Address negative thought patterns
- **Problem-solving:** Identify barriers, develop solutions
- **Stress management:** Alternative coping strategies

**Structured Programs:**
- Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP)
- Commercial programs with evidence (Weight Watchers, etc.)
- Individual or group counseling

**Expected Outcome:** 5–10% weight loss over 6 months

### Key Messages

**Disease Framework:**
- Obesity is a **chronic, relapsing disease**—not a personal failure
- Multifactorial etiology (genetic ~40–70%, environmental, behavioral)
- Requires long-term management, like diabetes or hypertension

**Goals and Expectations:**
- **5–10% weight loss** produces significant health benefits:
  - ↓ HbA1c by 0.5–1%
  - ↓ Blood pressure 5 mmHg
  - ↓ Triglycerides 40 mg/dL
  - ↓ OSA severity
  - ↓ Joint pain
- Weight loss is **non-linear**; plateaus are expected
- Focus on **metabolic health**, not just scale weight

### Pre-Pharmacotherapy Counseling
- Medications are adjuncts—lifestyle remains essential
- Expect gradual effect (weeks to months)
- Side effects often improve with time/titration
- **GLP-1 agonists:** Eat slowly, small portions, stop when full; severe nausea/vomiting should be reported
- **Qsymia:** Strict contraception required; REMS program
- **Contrave:** Report mood changes, suicidal thoughts
- Plan for **long-term use**; stopping often leads to weight regain

### Pre-Bariatric Surgery Counseling

**Expectations:**
- Surgery is a "tool"—requires lifelong commitment
- Dietary progression: Clear liquids → Full liquids → Puréed → Soft → Regular (6–8 weeks)
- **Protein goal:** 60–80 g/day minimum
- Eat slowly, chew thoroughly, stop at satiety
- Avoid drinking with meals (wait 30 min)
- Lifelong vitamin supplementation is **mandatory**

**Realistic Outcomes:**
- Weight loss occurs over 12–18 months, then stabilizes
- Some weight regain (10–15%) is common after nadir
- Diabetes/comorbidity improvement may occur rapidly
- Excess skin may require reconstructive surgery

**Psychosocial:**
- Relationship dynamics may change
- Support groups are highly beneficial
- Address transfer addictions (alcohol sensitivity post-RYGB)
- Mental health follow-up important

### Motivational Interviewing Approach
- Express **empathy** and avoid judgment
- Develop **discrepancy** between current behavior and goals
- Roll with **resistance**—don't argue
- Support **self-efficacy**—highlight past successes
- Use open-ended questions: "What would help you succeed?"

### Addressing Weight Regain
- Normalize—it's part of chronic disease management
- Investigate causes:
  - Dietary slip
  - Medication non-adherence
  - Mental health changes
  - Life stressors
- Reassess medications (intensify or change)
- Consider surgery if not previously done
- Re-engage with behavioral support

## Introduction and Motivation

Information theory, founded by Claude Shannon in 1948, answers fundamental questions:
- How do we quantify information?
- What are the ultimate limits of data compression?
- How fast can we reliably communicate over noisy channels?

---

# Part 1: Entropy — Measuring Uncertainty

## 1.1 The Information Content of a Single Event

**Intuition:** Rare events carry more "surprise" than common events.

When your friend says "the sun rose today," you learn little. But "there was a solar eclipse today" is highly informative precisely *because* it's rare.

**Desirable properties for an information measure I(p):**

1. **Monotonicity:** Rarer events → more information: I(p₁) > I(p₂) if p₁ < p₂
2. **Non-negativity:** I(p) ≥ 0
3. **Certainty gives zero info:** I(1) = 0
4. **Additivity:** Information from independent events adds

**Derivation of the logarithmic form:**

For independent events A and B:
$$I(p_A \cdot p_B) = I(p_A) + I(p_B)$$

This functional equation has the unique continuous solution:
$$I(p) = -\log p = \log\frac{1}{p}$$

**Proof sketch:** Let f(xy) = f(x) + f(y). Taking g(z) = f(eᶻ):
$$g(z_1 + z_2) = f(e^{z_1 + z_2}) = f(e^{z_1} \cdot e^{z_2}) = f(e^{z_1}) + f(e^{z_2}) = g(z_1) + g(z_2)$$

The only continuous solution to g(z₁ + z₂) = g(z₁) + g(z₂) is g(z) = cz, so f(x) = c·ln(x).

---

## 1.2 Entropy: Average Information

**Definition:** For a discrete random variable X with probability mass function p(x):

$$H(X) = -\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} p(x) \log p(x) = \mathbb{E}\left[\log\frac{1}{p(X)}\right]$$

We use log base 2, giving units of **bits**.

---

## 1.3 Worked Examples

### Example 1: Fair Coin
$$H(X) = -\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2}\log\frac{1}{2} = -\log\frac{1}{2} = 1 \text{ bit}$$

**Intuition:** One yes/no question determines the outcome.

### Example 2: Biased Coin (p = 0.9 heads)
$$H(X) = -0.9\log(0.9) - 0.1\log(0.1) \approx 0.469 \text{ bits}$$

Less uncertainty because we can mostly predict "heads."

### Example 3: Fair 8-Sided Die
$$H(X) = -\sum_{i=1}^{8} \frac{1}{8}\log\frac{1}{8} = \log 8 = 3 \text{ bits}$$

**Intuition:** Three binary questions determine the outcome (is it in {1,2,3,4}? is it in {1,2} or {5,6}? etc.)

### Example 4: Deterministic Variable
If P(X = a) = 1:
$$H(X) = -1 \cdot \log(1) = 0 \text{ bits}$$

No uncertainty means no information content.

---

## 1.4 Properties of Entropy

**Theorem (Entropy Properties):**

| Property | Statement |
|----------|-----------|
| Non-negativity | H(X) ≥ 0 |
| Maximum entropy | H(X) ≤ log|𝒳|, equality iff X is uniform |
| Concavity | H(αp + (1-α)q) ≥ αH(p) + (1-α)H(q) |

**Proof of Maximum Entropy:**

Using the log-sum inequality: For non-negative aᵢ, bᵢ:
$$\sum_i a_i \log\frac{a_i}{b_i} \geq \left(\sum_i a_i\right)\log\frac{\sum_i a_i}{\sum_i b_i}$$

Let aᵢ = p(xᵢ) and bᵢ = 1/|𝒳|:

$$\sum_i p(x_i)\log\frac{p(x_i)}{1/|\mathcal{X}|} \geq 1 \cdot \log\frac{1}{1} = 0$$

$$\sum_i p(x_i)\log p(x_i) + \sum_i p(x_i)\log|\mathcal{X}| \geq 0$$

$$-H(X) + \log|\mathcal{X}| \geq 0$$

$$H(X) \leq \log|\mathcal{X}|$$

Equality holds when p(xᵢ) = 1/|𝒳| for all i (uniform distribution). ∎

---

## 1.5 Binary Entropy Function

For a Bernoulli(p) random variable:

$$H_b(p) = -p\log p - (1-p)\log(1-p)$$

```
H_b(p)
  1 |      ****
    |    **    **
    |   *        *
    |  *          *
0.5 | *            *
    |*              *
    *                *
  0 +------------------
    0      0.5       1
              p
```

Maximum at p = 0.5, zero at p ∈ {0, 1}.

---

# Part 2: Joint and Conditional Entropy

## 2.1 Joint Entropy

For two random variables X and Y:

$$H(X, Y) = -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y) \log p(x,y)$$

**Example:** Consider this joint distribution:

|       | Y=0 | Y=1 |
|-------|-----|-----|
| X=0   | 1/4 | 1/4 |
| X=1   | 1/4 | 1/4 |

$$H(X,Y) = -4 \cdot \frac{1}{4}\log\frac{1}{4} = 2 \text{ bits}$$

---

## 2.2 Conditional Entropy

$$H(Y|X) = \sum_x p(x) H(Y|X=x) = -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(y|x)$$

**Interpretation:** Average remaining uncertainty about Y after learning X.

**Example:** Let Y = X (perfect correlation):
$$H(Y|X) = 0$$

Once we know X, there's no uncertainty about Y.

---

## 2.3 Chain Rule for Entropy

**Theorem:**
$$H(X, Y) = H(X) + H(Y|X) = H(Y) + H(X|Y)$$

**Proof:**
$$H(X,Y) = -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(x,y)$$
$$= -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log[p(x)p(y|x)]$$
$$= -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(x) - \sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(y|x)$$
$$= -\sum_x p(x)\log p(x) - \sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(y|x)$$
$$= H(X) + H(Y|X)$$

**General form:**
$$H(X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} H(X_i | X_1, \ldots, X_{i-1})$$

---

## 2.4 Key Inequality: Conditioning Reduces Entropy

**Theorem:** $H(Y|X) \leq H(Y)$ with equality iff X and Y are independent.

**Intuition:** On average, knowing something can't increase uncertainty.

**Proof:** 
$$H(Y) - H(Y|X) = I(X;Y) \geq 0$$

(We'll prove I(X;Y) ≥ 0 in the next section.)

---

# Part 3: Mutual Information

## 3.1 Definition and Intuition

**Mutual information** measures the information shared between two random variables.

$$I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X)$$

Equivalently:
$$I(X;Y) = \sum_{x,y} p(x,y) \log\frac{p(x,y)}{p(x)p(y)}$$

**Venn Diagram Representation:**

```
    ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
    │           H(X,Y)                │
    │  ┌──────────┬──────────┐        │
    │  │          │          │        │
    │  │   H(X|Y) │  I(X;Y)  │ H(Y|X) │
    │  │          │          │        │
    │  └──────────┴──────────┘        │
    │     ◄─── H(X) ───►              │
    │              ◄─── H(Y) ───►     │
    └─────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Key relationships:**
- I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y)
- I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) (uncertainty reduction about X from knowing Y)
- I(X;Y) = I(Y;X) (symmetric!)

---

## 3.2 Mutual Information as KL Divergence

$$I(X;Y) = D_{KL}(p(x,y) \| p(x)p(y))$$

where the KL divergence is:
$$D_{KL}(p \| q) = \sum_x p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$$

**Theorem:** $D_{KL}(p \| q) \geq 0$ with equality iff p = q.

**Proof (using Jensen's inequality):**
$$-D_{KL}(p \| q) = \sum_x p(x)\log\frac{q(x)}{p(x)} \leq \log\sum_x p(x)\frac{q(x)}{p(x)} = \log\sum_x q(x) = \log 1 = 0$$

The inequality is strict unless q(x)/p(x) is constant, i.e., p = q. ∎

**Corollary:** I(X;Y) ≥ 0, with equality iff X and Y are independent.

---

## 3.3 Worked Examples

### Example 1: Independent Variables
If X ⊥ Y: p(x,y) = p(x)p(y)

$$I(X;Y) = \sum_{x,y} p(x)p(y)\log\frac{p(x)p(y)}{p(x)p(y)} = 0$$

### Example 2: Deterministic Relationship
If Y = f(X) for some function f:

$$I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = H(Y) - 0 = H(Y)$$

Knowing X completely determines Y.

### Example 3: Noisy Channel
Let X ∈ {0,1} uniform, and Y = X ⊕ N where N is Bernoulli(ε), N ⊥ X.

- H(X) = 1 bit
- H(Y|X) = H(N) = H_b(ε)
- I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = 1 - H_b(ε)

When ε = 0 (no noise): I(X;Y) = 1 bit (perfect transmission)
When ε = 0.5 (pure noise): I(X;Y) = 0 bits (no information transmitted)

---

## 3.4 Data Processing Inequality

**Theorem:** If X → Y → Z forms a Markov chain (Z depends on X only through Y):
$$I(X;Z) \leq I(X;Y)$$

**Intuition:** Processing cannot create new information about X.

**Proof:**
By the chain rule for mutual information:
$$I(X;Y,Z) = I(X;Y) + I(X;Z|Y) = I(X;Z) + I(X;Y|Z)$$

For a Markov chain, I(X;Z|Y) = 0 (X and Z are conditionally independent given Y).

Therefore: I(X;Y) = I(X;Z) + I(X;Y|Z) ≥ I(X;Z) ∎

---

# Part 4: Channel Capacity

## 4.1 The Noisy Channel Model

```
    ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
 W  │ Encoder │  X  │ Channel │  Y  │ Decoder │  Ŵ
───►│         ├────►│  p(y|x) ├────►│         ├───►
    └─────────┘     └─────────┘     └─────────┘
```

- W: Message to send (uniform over {1, 2, ..., M})
- X: Channel input
- Y: Channel output (stochastic, governed by p(y|x))
- Ŵ: Decoded message

**Goal:** Maximize rate R = (log M)/n while keeping error probability low.

---

## 4.2 Channel Capacity Definition

**Definition:** The capacity of a channel is:

$$C = \max_{p(x)} I(X;Y)$$

The maximum is over all input distributions p(x).

---

## 4.3 Example: Binary Symmetric Channel (BSC)

```
        1-ε
    0 ─────── 0
      \     /
     ε \   / ε
        ╲ ╱
        ╱ ╲
     ε /   \ ε
      /     \
    1 ─────── 1
        1-ε
```

Each bit is flipped with probability ε.

**Capacity Derivation:**

$$I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X)$$

$$H(Y|X) = \sum_x p(x) H(Y|X=x) = H_b(\varepsilon)$$

(Each input sees the same binary noise.)

$$H(Y) \leq 1 \text{ bit}$$

with equality when Y is uniform, which occurs when X is uniform.

Therefore:
$$C = \max_{p(x)} I(X;Y) = 1 - H_b(\varepsilon) \text{ bits per channel use}$$

```
Capacity
   1 |*
     | *
     |  *
     |   **
 0.5 |     **
     |       ***
     |          ****
   0 +----------------
     0     0.5      1
            ε
```

---

## 4.4 Example: Binary Erasure Channel (BEC)

```
        1-ε
    0 ─────── 0
      \
       ε \
          ╲
           → e (erasure)
          ╱
       ε /
      /
    1 ─────── 1
        1-ε
```

Each bit is either received correctly or erased (marked unknown) with probability ε.

**Capacity:**
$$C = 1 - \varepsilon \text{ bits per channel use}$$

**Derivation:**
- H(Y|X) = H_b(ε) for each input
  
Wait, let me recalculate. Y ∈ {0, 1, e}.

For X = 0: Y = 0 with prob 1-ε, Y = e with prob ε
$$H(Y|X=0) = H_b(\varepsilon)$$

Actually, this is:
$$H(Y|X=0) = -(\varepsilon)\log\varepsilon - (1-\varepsilon)\log(1-\varepsilon) = H_b(\varepsilon)$$

Same for X = 1.

For uniform input: P(Y=0) = (1-ε)/2, P(Y=1) = (1-ε)/2, P(Y=e) = ε

$$H(Y) = -2 \cdot \frac{1-\varepsilon}{2}\log\frac{1-\varepsilon}{2} - \varepsilon\log\varepsilon$$
$$= (1-\varepsilon)(1 + \log\frac{1}{1-\varepsilon}) + \varepsilon\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}$$
$$= (1-\varepsilon) + H_b(\varepsilon)$$

Therefore:
$$I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) = (1-\varepsilon) + H_b(\varepsilon) - H_b(\varepsilon) = 1-\varepsilon$$

**Intuition:** Only fraction (1-ε) of bits get through.

---

## 4.5 Example: Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) Channel

$$Y = X + Z, \quad Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, N)$$

with power constraint $\mathbb{E}[X^2] \leq P$.

**Capacity:**
$$C = \frac{1}{2}\log_2\left(1 + \frac{P}{N}\right) \text{ bits per channel use}$$

**Derivation:**
$$I(X;Y) = h(Y) - h(Y|X) = h(Y) - h(Z)$$

where h(·) denotes differential entropy.

For fixed variance, Gaussian has maximum entropy:
$$h(Z) = \frac{1}{2}\log_2(2\pi e N)$$

The output Y = X + Z has variance at most P + N, so:
$$h(Y) \leq \frac{1}{2}\log_2(2\pi e (P+N))$$

with equality when X is Gaussian(0, P).

Therefore:
$$C = \frac{1}{2}\log_2(2\pi e(P+N)) - \frac{1}{2}\log_2(2\pi e N) = \frac{1}{2}\log_2\left(1 + \frac{P}{N}\right)$$

---

## 4.6 Shannon's Channel Coding Theorem

**Theorem (Noisy Channel Coding Theorem):**

1. **(Achievability):** For any rate R < C, there exist codes with arbitrarily small error probability.

2. **(Converse):** For any rate R > C, the error probability is bounded away from zero.

**Proof Sketch (Achievability via Random Coding):**

1. Generate 2^(nR) random codewords, each i.i.d. from the capacity-achieving distribution.

2. To decode, look for a codeword jointly typical with the received sequence.

3. Error occurs if:
   - The true codeword is not typical with Y: probability → 0 by LLN
   - Another codeword is typical with Y: probability ≈ 2^(-n(I(X;Y) - R))

4. Union bound over 2^(nR) - 1 wrong codewords:
   $$P(\text{wrong codeword typical}) \lesssim 2^{nR} \cdot 2^{-nI(X;Y)} = 2^{-n(I(X;Y)-R)}$$

5. When R < I(X;Y) ≤ C, this → 0 as n → ∞.

# Part 5: Source Coding (Lossless Compression)

## 5.1 The Source Coding Problem

Given a sequence X₁, X₂, ..., Xₙ from a source, encode it into bits such that:
- The original can be perfectly recovered
- The average number of bits is minimized

---

## 5.2 Shannon's Source Coding Theorem

**Theorem:** For an i.i.d. source with entropy H(X):

1. The source can be compressed to H(X) + ε bits per symbol (achievable).
2. Compression below H(X) bits per symbol is impossible (converse).

**Typical Set Definition:**
The typical set A_ε^(n) contains sequences x^n where:
$$2^{-n(H(X)+\varepsilon)} \leq p(x^n) \leq 2^{-n(H(X)-\varepsilon)}$$

**Key Properties:**
- P(X^n ∈ A_ε^(n)) → 1 as n → ∞
- |A_ε^(n)| ≈ 2^(nH(X))

**Proof Idea:**
- Only ≈ 2^(nH(X)) typical sequences have significant probability
- We can index them with nH(X) bits
- Rate = H(X) bits per symbol

---

## 5.3 Prefix-Free Codes and Kraft Inequality

**Definition:** A prefix-free code has no codeword as a prefix of another.

**Kraft Inequality:** A prefix-free code with lengths l₁, l₂, ..., l_m exists iff:
$$\sum_{i=1}^{m} 2^{-l_i} \leq 1$$

**Example:** 
- Code A: {0, 10, 110, 111} — prefix-free ✓
- Code B: {0, 01, 011} — NOT prefix-free (0 is prefix of 01)

---

## 5.4 Optimal Code Lengths

**Theorem:** The expected length L of any prefix-free code satisfies:
$$L = \sum_x p(x) l(x) \geq H(X)$$

with equality achievable when l(x) = log(1/p(x)) (integer lengths: l(x) = ⌈log(1/p(x))⌉).

**Proof of Lower Bound:**

$$L - H(X) = \sum_x p(x)l(x) + \sum_x p(x)\log p(x)$$
$$= \sum_x p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{2^{-l(x)}}$$

Let q(x) = 2^(-l(x)) / Z where Z = Σ 2^(-l(x)) ≤ 1.

$$L - H(X) = \sum_x p(x)\log\frac{p(x)}{q(x)} - \log Z$$
$$= D_{KL}(p \| q) + \log\frac{1}{Z} \geq 0$$

since both terms are non-negative. ∎

---

# Part 6: Rate–Distortion Theory

## 6.1 The Lossy Compression Problem

When exact reconstruction isn't required, how much can we compress?

**Setup:**
- Source: X with distribution p(x)
- Reconstruction alphabet: X̂
- Distortion measure: d(x, x̂) (e.g., squared error)
- Average distortion constraint: E[d(X, X̂)] ≤ D

---

## 6.2 The Rate–Distortion Function

**Definition:**
$$R(D) = \min_{p(\hat{x}|x): \mathbb{E}[d(X,\hat{X})] \leq D} I(X; \hat{X})$$

**Interpretation:** R(D) is the minimum rate (bits per symbol) needed to describe the source with distortion at most D.

---

## 6.3 Rate–Distortion Theorem

**Theorem:** 
- A source with distortion D can be described at rate R(D) + ε (achievable).
- Rate below R(D) cannot achieve distortion D (converse).

---

## 6.4 Example: Binary Source with Hamming Distortion

Source: X ~ Bernoulli(1/2)
Distortion: d(x, x̂) = 1 if x ≠ x̂, else 0 (Hamming distance)

**Derivation:**

We want to find the conditional distribution p(x̂|x) minimizing I(X; X̂) subject to:
$$\mathbb{E}[d(X,\hat{X})] = P(X \neq \hat{X}) \leq D$$

By symmetry, optimal is: Flip X with probability D.
$$p(\hat{x}|x) = \begin{cases} 1-D & \text{if } \hat{x} = x \\ D & \text{if } \hat{x} \neq x \end{cases}$$

This is like passing X through a BSC(D).

Then:
$$I(X;\hat{X}) = H(\hat{X}) - H(\hat{X}|X) = 1 - H_b(D)$$

Therefore:
$$R(D) = \begin{cases} 1 - H_b(D) & 0 \leq D \leq 1/2 \\ 0 & D > 1/2 \end{cases}$$

```
R(D)

    | *
    |  *
    |   *
0.5 |    **
    |      **
    |        ***
  0 +-----------***
    0    0.5     1
           D
```

---

## 6.5 Example: Gaussian Source with Squared-Error Distortion

Source: X ~ N(0, σ²)
Distortion: d(x, x̂) = (x - x̂)²

**Result:**
$$R(D) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}\log_2\frac{\sigma^2}{D} & 0 < D \leq \sigma^2 \\ 0 & D > \sigma^2 \end{cases}$$

**Derivation:**

The optimal test channel is: X̂ = X + Z where Z ~ N(0, D) independent of X.

Actually, let's derive properly. We want X̂ such that E[(X - X̂)²] ≤ D.

The optimal strategy: X̂ = X + N where N is independent noise.

For Gaussian source with "reverse water-filling":
$$R(D) = \frac{1}{2}\log^+\frac{\sigma^2}{D}$$

**Intuition:** 
- D = σ²: Just output 0, achieving distortion σ² with zero bits
- D → 0: Need infinite rate for perfect reconstruction

---

## 6.6 Properties of R(D)

| Property | Statement |
|----------|-----------|
| Monotonicity | R(D) is non-increasing in D |
| Convexity | R(D) is convex in D |
| Boundary | R(0) = H(X) for discrete sources, R(D_max) = 0 |

**Proof of Convexity:**

Given points (D₁, R₁) and (D₂, R₂) achievable, time-sharing achieves:
$$(αD_1 + (1-α)D_2, αR_1 + (1-α)R_2)$$

Since R(D) is the infimum over achievable points, it lies below this line. ∎

## 7.2 Key Formulas Reference

| Quantity | Formula |
|----------|---------|
| Entropy | $H(X) = -\sum_x p(x)\log p(x)$ |
| Conditional Entropy | $H(Y\|X) = -\sum_{x,y} p(x,y)\log p(y\|x)$ |
| Mutual Information | $I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X\|Y) = H(Y) - H(Y\|X)$ |
| Channel Capacity | $C = \max_{p(x)} I(X;Y)$ |
| Rate-Distortion | $R(D) = \min_{p(\hat{x}\|x)} I(X;\hat{X})$ s.t. $E[d] \leq D$ |

## 7.3 Fundamental Limits

| Problem | Limit | Meaning |
|---------|-------|---------|
| Lossless Compression | H(X) | Can't compress below entropy |
| Reliable Communication | C | Can't transmit faster than capacity |
| Lossy Compression | R(D) | Minimum rate for given distortion |

---

## 7.4 The Source-Channel Separation Theorem

**Theorem:** For transmitting a source over a noisy channel:
- Achievable if H(X) ≤ C (or R(D) ≤ C for lossy)
- Optimal to separate source coding and channel coding!

This profound result says we can design compression and error correction independently—a cornerstone of modern communication systems.

---

# Conclusion

Information theory provides:

1. **Entropy** — The fundamental measure of uncertainty
2. **Mutual Information** — How much one variable tells about another
3. **Channel Capacity** — The hard limit on reliable communication
4. **Source Coding** — The hard limit on lossless compression
5. **Rate-Distortion** — The tradeoff between compression and fidelity

These concepts form the mathematical foundation for all of modern communications, compression, and increasingly, machine learning. Shannon's genius was recognizing that probabilistic arguments yield exact limits on what is achievable—not just engineering approximations, but fundamental laws of information.

```python
# Example: Optimal Hedge Ratio Calculation

import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import minimize_scalar

class HedgeRatioOptimizer:
    """
    Calculates optimal hedge ratio using minimum variance approach
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spot_returns, futures_returns):
        self.spot = np.array(spot_returns)
        self.futures = np.array(futures_returns)
    
    def minimum_variance_ratio(self):
        """
        h* = Cov(S,F) / Var(F)
        
        where:
        S = spot price changes
        F = futures price changes
        """
        covariance = np.cov(self.spot, self.futures)[0, 1]
        variance_futures = np.var(self.futures)
        
        return covariance / variance_futures
    
    def hedge_effectiveness(self, hedge_ratio):
        """
        Calculate variance reduction from hedging
        """
        unhedged_variance = np.var(self.spot)
        hedged_portfolio = self.spot - hedge_ratio * self.futures
        hedged_variance = np.var(hedged_portfolio)
        
        effectiveness = 1 - (hedged_variance / unhedged_variance)
        return effectiveness * 100  # As percentage
    
    def calculate_basis_risk(self, hedge_ratio):
        """
        Residual risk after hedging
        """
        hedged_portfolio = self.spot - hedge_ratio * self.futures
        return np.std(hedged_portfolio)

## 3.4 Effectiveness Testing

### Quantitative Methods

```python
# Hedge Effectiveness Testing Methods

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

class HedgeEffectivenessTester:
    """
    Implements multiple hedge effectiveness testing methodologies
    """
    
    def __init__(self, hedge_changes, hedged_item_changes):
        """
        hedge_changes: List of period-over-period changes in hedge FV
        hedged_item_changes: List of period-over-period changes in hedged item
        """
        self.hedge = np.array(hedge_changes)
        self.hedged = np.array(hedged_item_changes)
    
    def dollar_offset_test(self, cumulative=False):
        """
        Dollar Offset Method
        Ratio = Change in Hedge FV / Change in Hedged Item FV
        Must be between 80% and 125% to pass
        """
        if cumulative:
            hedge_change = np.sum(self.hedge)
            hedged_change = np.sum(self.hedged)
        else:
            # Period-by-period
            hedge_change = self.hedge
            hedged_change = self.hedged
        
        # Avoid division by zero
        if np.any(hedged_change == 0):
            return None, "Cannot compute - division by zero"
        
        ratio = abs(hedge_change / hedged_change)
        
        # Check if within 80-125%
        if cumulative:
            passed = 0.80 <= ratio <= 1.25
            return {
                'ratio': ratio,
                'passed': passed,
                'hedge_change': hedge_change,
                'hedged_change': hedged_change
            }
        else:
            results = pd.DataFrame({
                'Period': range(1, len(self.hedge) + 1),
                'Hedge_Change': self.hedge,
                'Hedged_Item_Change': self.hedged,
                'Ratio': ratio,
                'Passed': (ratio >= 0.80) & (ratio <= 1.25)
            })
            return results
    
    def regression_analysis(self):
        """
        Regression Method (Statistical)
        Regress hedge changes on hedged item changes
        Requirements:
        - R² ≥ 0.80
        - Slope between -0.80 and -1.25
        - F-statistic significant at 95% level
        """
        # Flip sign for hedged item (expect negative relationship)
        X = -self.hedged  # Negative because hedge should offset
        Y = self.hedge
        
        # Add constant for intercept
        X_with_const = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(X)), X])
        
        # OLS regression
        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(X, Y)
        r_squared = r_value ** 2
        
        # F-test
        n = len(X)
        f_statistic = (r_squared / 1) / ((1 - r_squared) / (n - 2))
        f_critical = stats.f.ppf(0.95, 1, n - 2)
        
        results = {
            'slope': slope,
            'intercept': intercept,
            'r_squared': r_squared,
            'p_value': p_value,
            'f_statistic': f_statistic,
            'f_critical': f_critical,
            'slope_in_range': 0.80 <= abs(slope) <= 1.25,
            'r_squared_pass': r_squared >= 0.80,
            'f_test_pass': f_statistic > f_critical,
            'overall_pass': (r_squared >= 0.80 and 
                           0.80 <= abs(slope) <= 1.25 and 
                           f_statistic > f_critical)
        }
        
        return results
    
    def hypothetical_derivative_method(self, hypothetical_changes):
        """
        Hypothetical Derivative Method
        Compares actual hedge with 'perfect' hypothetical hedge
        """
        # Calculate ineffectiveness
        ineffectiveness = self.hedge - np.array(hypothetical_changes)
        
        return {
            'actual_hedge_total': np.sum(self.hedge),
            'hypothetical_total': np.sum(hypothetical_changes),
            'ineffectiveness': np.sum(ineffectiveness),
            'period_ineffectiveness': ineffectiveness
        }

## 4.4 Greeks Calculation Implementation

```python
# Greeks Calculator for FX Options

import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import norm

class GarmanKohlhagenGreeks:
    """
    Calculate Greeks for FX options using Garman-Kohlhagen model
    (Black-Scholes adapted for FX)
    """
    
    def __init__(self, S, K, T, r_d, r_f, sigma, option_type='call'):
        """
        S: Spot rate
        K: Strike rate
        T: Time to maturity (years)
        r_d: Domestic risk-free rate
        r_f: Foreign risk-free rate
        sigma: Volatility
        option_type: 'call' or 'put'
        """
        self.S = S
        self.K = K
        self.T = T
        self.r_d = r_d
        self.r_f = r_f
        self.sigma = sigma
        self.option_type = option_type
        
        # Calculate d1 and d2
        self.d1 = (np.log(S/K) + (r_d - r_f + 0.5*sigma**2)*T) / (sigma*np.sqrt(T))
        self.d2 = self.d1 - sigma * np.sqrt(T)
    
    def price(self):
        """Option premium"""
        if self.option_type == 'call':
            price = (self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d1) - 
                    self.K * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d2))
        else:
            price = (self.K * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d2) - 
                    self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d1))
        return price
    
    def delta(self):
        """Delta - sensitivity to spot rate"""
        if self.option_type == 'call':
            return np.exp(-self.r_f * self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d1)
        else:
            return np.exp(-self.r_f * self.T) * (norm.cdf(self.d1) - 1)
    
    def gamma(self):
        """Gamma - sensitivity of delta to spot rate"""
        return (np.exp(-self.r_f * self.T) * norm.pdf(self.d1)) / \
               (self.S * self.sigma * np.sqrt(self.T))
    
    def theta(self, trading_days=252):
        """Theta - time decay (per day)"""
        term1 = -(self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.pdf(self.d1) * 
                  self.sigma) / (2 * np.sqrt(self.T))
        
        if self.option_type == 'call':
            term2 = self.r_f * self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d1)
            term3 = -self.r_d * self.K * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d2)
        else:
            term2 = -self.r_f * self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d1)
            term3 = self.r_d * self.K * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d2)
        
        annual_theta = term1 + term2 + term3
        return annual_theta / trading_days  # Daily theta
    
    def vega(self):
        """Vega - sensitivity to volatility (per 1% vol change)"""
        return self.S * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * \
               norm.pdf(self.d1) * np.sqrt(self.T) / 100
    
    def rho_domestic(self):
        """Rho domestic - sensitivity to domestic interest rate"""
        if self.option_type == 'call':
            return self.K * self.T * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d2) / 100
        else:
            return -self.K * self.T * np.exp(-self.r_d*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d2) / 100
    
    def rho_foreign(self):
        """Rho foreign - sensitivity to foreign interest rate"""
        if self.option_type == 'call':
            return -self.S * self.T * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(self.d1) / 100
        else:
            return self.S * self.T * np.exp(-self.r_f*self.T) * norm.cdf(-self.d1) / 100
    
    def all_greeks(self):
        """Return all Greeks as dictionary"""
        return {
            'price': self.price(),
            'delta': self.delta(),
            'gamma': self.gamma(),
            'theta': self.theta(),
            'vega': self.vega(),
            'rho_domestic': self.rho_domestic(),
            'rho_foreign': self.rho_foreign()
        }


# Example: EUR/USD Call Option Greeks
# ────────────────────────────────────

option = GarmanKohlhagenGreeks(
    S=1.0850,        # Spot EUR/USD
    K=1.1000,        # Strike
    T=0.25,          # 3 months
    r_d=0.050,       # USD rate 5%
    r_f=0.040,       # EUR rate 4%
    sigma=0.08,      # 8% volatility
    option_type='call'
)

greeks = option.all_greeks()

print("EUR/USD Call Option Greeks")
print("=" * 40)
print(f"Spot: {option.S:.4f}")
print(f"Strike: {option.K:.4f}")
print(f"Time to Expiry: {option.T:.2f} years")
print(f"Implied Volatility: {option.sigma*100:.1f}%")
print("-" * 40)
print(f"Premium:       ${greeks['price']*1000000:.2f} per EUR 1M")
print(f"Delta:         {greeks['delta']:.4f}")
print(f"Gamma:         {greeks['gamma']:.4f}")
print(f"Theta (daily): ${greeks['theta']*1000000:.2f}")
print(f"Vega (1% vol): ${greeks['vega']*1000000:.2f}")
print(f"Rho (domestic): ${greeks['rho_domestic']*1000000:.2f}")
print(f"Rho (foreign):  ${greeks['rho_foreign']*1000000:.2f}")

## 5.6 VaR and Expected Shortfall

```python
# Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall Calculation

import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

class RiskMetricsCalculator:
    """
    Calculate VaR and Expected Shortfall for derivatives portfolio
    """
    
    def __init__(self, returns, confidence_level=0.99):
        """
        returns: Historical returns array (negative = loss)
        confidence_level: Confidence level for VaR (e.g., 0.95, 0.99)
        """
        self.returns = np.array(returns)
        self.confidence = confidence_level
        
    def historical_var(self):
        """
        Historical Simulation VaR
        """
        return np.percentile(self.returns, (1 - self.confidence) * 100)
    
    def parametric_var(self):
        """
        Parametric (Normal) VaR
        Assumes returns are normally distributed
        """
        mean = np.mean(self.returns)
        std = np.std(self.returns)
        z_score = stats.norm.ppf(1 - self.confidence)
        return mean + z_score * std
    
    def expected_shortfall(self):
        """
        Expected Shortfall (Conditional VaR)
        Average of returns below VaR threshold
        """
        var = self.historical_var()
        return np.mean(self.returns[self.returns <= var])
    
    def cornish_fisher_var(self):
        """
        Modified VaR using Cornish-Fisher expansion
        Accounts for skewness and kurtosis
        """
        mean = np.mean(self.returns)
        std = np.std(self.returns)
        skew = stats.skew(self.returns)
        kurt = stats.kurtosis(self.returns)  # Excess kurtosis
        
        z = stats.norm.ppf(1 - self.confidence)
        
        # Cornish-Fisher expansion
        z_cf = (z + 
                (z**2 - 1) * skew / 6 + 
                (z**3 - 3*z) * kurt / 24 - 
                (2*z**3 - 5*z) * (skew**2) / 36)
        
        return mean + z_cf * std


# Example: Portfolio VaR Calculation
# ──────────────────────────────────

# Simulated daily P&L data for derivatives portfolio ($ millions)
np.random.seed(42)
daily_pnl = np.random.normal(0, 0.5, 252)  # 1 year of daily returns
daily_pnl = daily_pnl + np.random.standard_t(5, 252) * 0.1  # Add fat tails

# Scale to represent portfolio P&L
portfolio_pnl = daily_pnl * 100000  # Scale to dollars

calc = RiskMetricsCalculator(portfolio_pnl, confidence_level=0.99)

print("RISK METRICS REPORT")
print("=" * 50)
print(f"Observation Period: 252 trading days")
print(f"Confidence Level: 99%")
print("-" * 50)
print(f"Historical VaR (1-day):     ${-calc.historical_var():,.0f}")
print(f"Parametric VaR (1-day):     ${-calc.parametric_var():,.0f}")
print(f"Cornish-Fisher VaR (1-day): ${-calc.cornish_fisher_var():,.0f}")
print(f"Expected Shortfall:         ${-calc.expected_shortfall():,.0f}")
print("-" * 50)

# Scaling to different horizons
var_1d = -calc.historical_var()
var_10d = var_1d * np.sqrt(10)
var_30d = var_1d * np.sqrt(30)

print("VaR BY TIME HORIZON (Historical, 99%)")
print(f"  1-Day VaR:   ${var_1d:,.0f}")
print(f" 10-Day VaR:   ${var_10d:,.0f}")
print(f" 30-Day VaR:   ${var_30d:,.0f}")
